The table shows three values of x and corresponding values of g(x), where \[ g(x) = \frac{f(x)}{x + 2} \]and f is a linear function. What is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of the graph of y = f(x) in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: Rearrange the definition to recover f: multiply both sides by x + 2 to get f(x) = g(x)(x + 2). Now convert each table row: f(-23) = 2(-21) = -42, f(-9) = 0(-7) = 0, f(19) = 4(21) = 84. Those three points are collinear with slope (84 - 0) / (19 - (-9)) = 3, so f(x) = 3(x + 9) = 3x + 27, and the y-intercept value is 27.

questions.stem:
\(-\frac{3}{19}rx + \frac{s}{8} = 10 - \frac{5}{57}x\)

In the given equation, \(r\) and \(s\) are constants and \(s \ne 80\). The equation has no solution. What is the value of \(r\)?
questions.whyCorrect: No solution means the two sides must have the same coefficient of \(x\) but different constants. Match the \(x\) coefficients: \(-\frac{3}{19}r = -\frac{5}{57}\), so \(r = \frac{5}{57} \cdot \frac{19}{3} = \frac{95}{171} = \frac{5}{9}\). The condition \(s \ne 80\) is what guarantees the constants \(\frac{s}{8}\) and 10 differ, so the equation really is unsolvable.

questions.stem: A linear model estimates the population of a city from 1991 to 2015. The model estimates the population was 59 thousand in 1991, 222 thousand in 2011, and x thousand in 2015. To the nearest whole number, what is the value of x?
questions.whyCorrect: A linear model grows by the same amount every year, so find that amount first: the population rose 222 − 59 = 163 thousand over the 20 years from 1991 to 2011, which is \(\frac{163}{20} = 8.15\) thousand per year. From 2011 to 2015 is 4 more years, so add 4(8.15) = 32.6 to 222, giving 254.6 — 255 to the nearest whole number.

questions.stem:
\[ 4x^2+21=48+r \]
In the given equation, \(r\) is a constant. The equation has exactly one real solution. What is the value of \(r\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Isolate the squared term: \(4x^2=27+r\), so \(x^2=\frac{27+r}{4}\). A squared quantity equal to a positive number gives two solutions and equal to a negative number gives none, so exactly one solution requires \(27+r=0\), i.e. \(r=-27\) (and then \(x=0\)).

questions.stem: To cut a lawn, Antwan charges a fee of $10.00 for his equipment and $8.50 per hour spent cutting a lawn. Taylor charges a fee of $7.00 for his equipment and $9.50 per hour spent cutting a lawn. If x represents the number of hours spent cutting a lawn, what are the values of x for which Taylor’s total charge is greater than Antwan’s total charge?
questions.whyCorrect: Write both totals and compare: Taylor charges 7 + 9.50x and Antwan charges 10 + 8.50x. Setting 7 + 9.50x > 10 + 8.50x gives x > 3. Taylor starts $3 cheaper but gains $1 per hour, so he overtakes after 3 hours.

whyWrong.A: At x = 2 Taylor charges $26 and Antwan $27, so Taylor is still cheaper. This range is entirely on the wrong side of the crossover.
whyWrong.B: At x = 3 the two charges are equal ($35.50 each), so the inequality is strict and the interval must be open and unbounded above.
whyWrong.C: Below 2 hours Taylor is cheaper still, since his $3 head start has not been eaten up by the $1-per-hour difference.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = 7.3(0.98)^{x} \] The function shown models the annual soil erosion rate, in tons per acre per year, on US croplands \(x\) years since 1982. According to the model, which is the best interpretation of \(7.3(0.98)^{10}\) in this context?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The number of acres of US cropland in 1982

choices.label: B
choices.content: The number of acres of US cropland in 1992

choices.label: C
choices.content: The annual soil erosion rate, in tons per acre per year, in 1982

choices.label: D
choices.content: The annual soil erosion rate, in tons per acre per year, in 1992

questions.whyCorrect: The expression is \(f(10)\), and \(x\) counts years since 1982, so \(x = 10\) is the year 1992. The output of \(f\) is the erosion rate in tons per acre per year, so this value is the 1992 erosion rate.

whyWrong.A: \(f\) outputs an erosion rate, not an acreage, and 1982 corresponds to \(x = 0\), which would be \(7.3(0.98)^{0} = 7.3\).
whyWrong.B: The units are wrong: the model never counts acres, it gives tons per acre per year.
whyWrong.C: The year is wrong. 1982 is \(x = 0\); the exponent 10 places this ten years later.

questions.stem: Scientists examined water samples from different water springs. For these samples, the partial pressure of carbon dioxide in a closed system (limited carbon dioxide supply) had a minimum of 0.014 atmosphere (atm) and a maximum of 0.180 atm. The partial pressure of carbon dioxide in an open system (unlimited carbon dioxide supply) had a minimum of 0.00049 atm and a maximum of 0.05900 atm. Which statement best compares the range of the partial pressure of carbon dioxide for closed systems and open systems?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The range for closed systems is less than the range for open systems.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The range for closed systems is greater than the range for open systems.

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is not enough information to compare the ranges.

questions.whyCorrect: The range of a data set is maximum minus minimum, and both a maximum and a minimum are given for each system, so you have everything you need. Closed: 0.180 − 0.014 = 0.166 atm. Open: 0.05900 − 0.00049 = 0.05851 atm. 0.166 is bigger than 0.0585, so the closed-system range is greater.

whyWrong.A: This reverses the comparison. The open-system numbers have more decimal places, which makes them look more precise, but 0.05851 is still much smaller than 0.166.
whyWrong.C: The two differences are not equal — 0.166 against 0.05851, almost three times apart.
whyWrong.D: A range needs only the maximum and the minimum, and both are stated for both systems. You never need the individual data values.

questions.stem: \[v = -\frac{w}{161x}\]The given equation relates the distinct positive numbers \(v\), \(w\), and \(x\). Which equation correctly expresses \(w\) in terms of \(v\) and \(x\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Multiply both sides by \(161x\) to clear the denominator: \(161xv = -w\). Then multiply by \(-1\), giving \(w = -161vx\). The \(x\) is in the denominator on the right, so it moves up to the left side as a factor.

whyWrong.B: This leaves \(x\) in the denominator. Since \(x\) divides \(w\) in the original equation, undoing that division multiplies by \(x\).
whyWrong.C: This inverts the whole expression — \(v\) ends up in the denominator, but \(v\) is by itself on the left, so it becomes a factor, not a divisor.
whyWrong.D: The original relationship is a product/quotient, not a sum; you cannot move \(161x\) across the equals sign by adding it.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \[ (x + 8)^2 + 14(x + 8) + 49? \]
questions.whyCorrect: Treat \(x + 8\) as a single quantity. Writing \(u = x + 8\), the expression is \(u^2 + 14u + 49\), which is the perfect square \((u + 7)^2\). Substitute back: \((x + 8 + 7)^2 = (x + 15)^2\).

whyWrong.B: This is \((u + 7)^2\) with the substitution left undone — you have to put \(x + 8\) back in place of \(u\), not \(x\).
whyWrong.C: There is no factor of 8 to pull out; the 8 belongs inside the binomial \(x + 8\), not in front of the square.
whyWrong.D: The 49 is not a factor of the expression, it is the constant term of the perfect square. Expanding \(7(x + 8)^2\) gives a leading coefficient of 7, but the original expands with a leading coefficient of 1.

questions.stem: A sphere has a radius of \(\frac{13}{5}\) feet. What is the volume, in cubic feet, of the sphere?
questions.whyCorrect: Use \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\) and cube the whole fraction, top and bottom: \(\left(\frac{13}{5}\right)^3 = \frac{2197}{125}\). Then \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot \frac{2197}{125} = \frac{8788\pi}{375}\).

whyWrong.B: This does not come from the volume formula; nothing here produces a denominator of 5 once the radius is cubed.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{52\pi}{15}\) is \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r\) — the radius was never cubed.
whyWrong.D: This is the reciprocal of the radius times \(\pi\), with the formula ignored.

questions.stem: The combined original price for a towel and chair is $36. After a 45% discount to the chair and a 25% discount to the towel are applied, the combined sale price for the two items is $25. Which system of equations gives the original price \(t\) in dollars of the towel and \(c\) in dollars of the chair?
questions.whyCorrect: A discount equation has to use the fraction of the price still paid, not the fraction taken off. A 25% discount on the towel leaves \(0.75t\); a 45% discount on the chair leaves \(0.55c\). Those add to the sale price: \(0.75t + 0.55c = 25\). Also check which letter each percent belongs to — the 25% goes with the towel \(t\).

whyWrong.A: These are the amounts discounted, so this equation says the two discounts add to $25, when in fact the discounts total \(36 - 25 = 11\) dollars. The percents are also attached to the wrong items.
whyWrong.B: The paid fractions are right in form but swapped between the items: 0.55 belongs to the chair and 0.75 to the towel.
whyWrong.C: These are the discount fractions, correctly matched to their items but describing money saved rather than money paid.

questions.stem:
3x − 2y = 5
x = 7

What is the solution (x, y) to the given system of equations?
questions.whyCorrect: The second equation gives x = 7 outright, so substitute it into the first: 3(7) − 2y = 5, which is 21 − 2y = 5. Subtract 21 from both sides to get −2y = −16, then divide by −2 to get y = 8. The solution is (7, 8).

whyWrong.B: You reached 2y = 16 and then subtracted the 2 instead of dividing by it. Substituting y = 14 gives 21 − 28 = −7, not 5.
whyWrong.C: This keeps the negative sign from −2y = −16 after dividing, but a negative divided by a negative is positive. Substituting gives 21 + 16 = 37, not 5.
whyWrong.D: This combines both slips: the wrong sign and subtracting 2 instead of dividing by it. Substituting gives 21 + 28 = 49, not 5.

questions.stem: The graph of a polynomial function \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane passes through the point \( (8, 9) \) . What is the value of \( f(8) \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: A point on the graph is written \( (x, f(x)) \) , so \( (8, 9) \) says that the input 8 produces the output 9. That is exactly \( f(8) = 9 \) . No work with the polynomial itself is needed.

whyWrong.A: This is the input, the x-coordinate. \( f(8) \) asks for what comes out when 8 goes in.
whyWrong.C: This adds the two coordinates, which has no meaning for a function value.
whyWrong.D: This multiplies the two coordinates, which also has no meaning here.

questions.stem: In \(\triangle FGH\), the measure of \(\angle F\) and \(\angle G\) are each 39°. What is the measure of \(\angle H\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The two equal angles account for \(39 + 39 = 78\) degrees. The three angles of a triangle total 180°, so \(\angle H = 180 - 78 = 102^\circ\).

whyWrong.A: 78° is the combined measure of \(\angle F\) and \(\angle G\), not what remains for \(\angle H\).
whyWrong.C: 129° is 90 + 39, which would only apply if one of the angles were a right angle.
whyWrong.D: 141° is 180 − 39, subtracting only one of the two 39° angles.

questions.stem: A choir of 48 singers has 12 members who sing bass. If one singer from the choir is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a singer who sings bass?
questions.whyCorrect: Divide the number of bass singers by the total number of singers: 12 out of 48, so \( \frac{12}{48} \). You do not need to reduce it — the choices are all written over 48.

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{1}{48} \) is the probability of picking one specific named singer, not any of the 12 basses.
whyWrong.C: \( \frac{36}{48} \) is the probability of selecting a singer who does not sing bass.
whyWrong.D: \( \frac{48}{48} \) says every singer sings bass, which contradicts the stem.

questions.stem:
w(t) = 3.1t − 1.7

The function w models the weight, in pounds, of a certain pig t months after it was born, where 1 ≤ t ≤ 36. Which statement is the best interpretation of w(7) = 20 in this context?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The pig weighed 20 pounds 7 months after it was born.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The pig weighed 7 pounds 20 months after it was born.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The pig's weight increased by 20 pounds during the 7th month after it was born.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The pig's weight increased by 7 pounds during the 20th month after it was born.

questions.whyCorrect: In w(t), the input t is months after birth and the output is weight in pounds. So in w(7) = 20 the 7 is the time and the 20 is the weight: seven months after birth the pig weighed 20 pounds. Whatever sits inside the parentheses is the input.

whyWrong.B: The two numbers are reversed. The 7 is inside the parentheses, so it is the input (months); the 20 is the output (pounds).
whyWrong.C: An increase over one month would be the slope, 3.1 pounds per month. A single function value gives a weight at one moment, not a change.
whyWrong.D: This reverses the numbers and also reads the value as a change. Neither 7 nor 20 describes growth here; growth is the 3.1.

questions.stem: The predicted number, \(B(t)\), of a certain type of bacterial cell in a growth medium is given by the function \(B(t) = 40(3)^{t}\), where \(t\) is the time, in days, since the number of bacterial cells was first measured. Which of the following is the best interpretation of \(B(5) = 9{,}720\) in this context?

choices.label: A
choices.content: 5 days after the number of bacterial cells was first measured, the predicted number of bacterial cells was 9,720

choices.label: B
choices.content: 243 days after the number of bacterial cells was first measured, the predicted number of bacterial cells was 9,720

choices.label: C
choices.content: 9,720 days after the number of bacterial cells was first measured, the predicted number of bacterial cells was 5

choices.label: D
choices.content: 9,720 days after the number of bacterial cells was first measured, the predicted number of bacterial cells was 243

questions.whyCorrect: In \(B(t)\) the input \(t\) is days and the output is the number of cells, so \(B(5) = 9{,}720\) means that at 5 days the model predicts 9,720 cells. (It checks out: \(40 \cdot 3^{5} = 40 \cdot 243 = 9{,}720\).)

whyWrong.B: 243 is the value of \(3^{5}\), an intermediate step in the arithmetic, not a time.
whyWrong.C: This reverses input and output: 9,720 is the cell count, 5 is the day.
whyWrong.D: Same reversal as C, with the intermediate 243 substituted for the cell count.

questions.stem: Circle \(A\) has equation \[(x-7)^2+(y+3)^2=1.\]In the xy-plane, circle \(B\) is obtained by translating circle \(A\) to the right 4 units. Which equation represents circle \(B\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The center of circle \(A\) is \((7,-3)\). Translating right 4 units changes only the x-coordinate: \(7+4=11\), so the new center is \((11,-3)\). The radius does not change, so the equation is \((x-11)^2+(y+3)^2=1\).

whyWrong.A: This moves the center vertically to \((7,-7)\); a horizontal translation cannot change \(y\).
whyWrong.B: This subtracts 4 from the x-coordinate, giving center \((3,-3)\) — a shift 4 units left.
whyWrong.D: This moves the center up to \((7,1)\), again changing the wrong coordinate.

questions.stem: A triathlon is a multisport race consisting of three different legs. A triathlon participant completed the cycling leg with an average speed of 19.3 miles per hour. What was the average speed, in yards per hour, of the participant during the cycling leg? (1 mile = 1760 yards)
questions.whyCorrect: Only the distance unit changes, so the hours are untouched. A yard is much smaller than a mile, so multiply: 19.3 x 1,760 = 33,968 yards per hour.

whyWrong.B: 91.2 is roughly 19.3 divided by a fifth of the conversion factor. Dividing is the wrong direction — changing to a smaller unit makes the number bigger.
whyWrong.C: 57.9 is 19.3 x 3, the number of feet per yard used backwards. The conversion given is 1,760 yards per mile.
whyWrong.D: 5,280 is the number of feet in a mile, a fact not used here, and it ignores the 19.3 entirely.

questions.stem: A newspaper stand sells magazines for $5 each and newspapers for $2 each. The stand needs to sell m magazines and n newspapers for a combined total value of at least $150 each day to cover operation costs. Which inequality represents this situation?
questions.whyCorrect: Each item type contributes price times quantity, so the revenue is 5m + 2n. "At least $150" is a lower bound, so the revenue must be greater than or equal to 150.

whyWrong.A: This caps the revenue at 150, the opposite of what is needed. The stand must reach 150, not stay below it.
whyWrong.C: Adding the two prices to get 7 and multiplying by mn is not how revenue works — the two products are added, not the prices.
whyWrong.D: The inequality direction is right, but 7mn is not the revenue. Selling 10 magazines and 0 newspapers would give 0 here instead of $50.

questions.stem: \[ 3x^{2} - 4x + 7 = 0 \] How many distinct real solutions does the given equation have?
questions.whyCorrect: The count comes from the discriminant \( b^{2} - 4ac = (-4)^{2} - 4(3)(7) = 16 - 84 = -68 \) . A negative discriminant means the square root in the quadratic formula is not real, so there are no real solutions. The parabola sits entirely above the x-axis.

whyWrong.B: Exactly one requires the discriminant to be 0, which happens only when \( b^{2} = 4ac \) . Here 16 is far short of 84.
whyWrong.C: Exactly two requires a positive discriminant. The sign is negative because \( 4ac \) is larger than \( b^{2} \) .
whyWrong.D: A quadratic equation can never have infinitely many solutions; that only happens when both sides are identical for all x.

questions.stem: Which of the following could be the equation of the graph shown?
questions.whyCorrect: Two features decide it. The curve touches the x-axis without crossing at x = −2 and x = 3, so the factors are \( (x + 2)^{2} \) and \( (x - 3)^{2} \) — note the sign flip, a zero at −2 comes from \( (x + 2) \) . That leaves A and C, separated by their height: at x = 0, A gives \( 4 \cdot 9 = 36 \) but the graph is up near 70, and C gives \( 2 \cdot 4 \cdot 9 = 72 \) . C also matches the local maximum of about 78.

whyWrong.A: The zeros are right, but every value is half what the graph shows: it would peak near 39, not near 78.
whyWrong.B: Its zeros are at 2 and −3, the mirror image of the graph's.
whyWrong.D: Same wrong zeros as B, with the correct vertical stretch applied to the wrong shape.

questions.imageAlt: Coordinate grid in the xy-plane, x-axis marked from −4 to 4 and y-axis marked in twenties up to 100, showing a single W-shaped quartic curve.

questions.stem:
In the given system of equations, p is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of p?

\[ \frac{3}{2}y - \frac{1}{4}x = \frac{2}{3} - \frac{3}{2}y \]
\[ \frac{1}{6}x + \frac{3}{6} = py + \frac{9}{5} \]
questions.whyCorrect: No solution means the two lines are parallel: the x and y coefficients are in the same ratio while the constants are not. Put both equations in the form \( ax + by = c \) first. The first becomes \( -\frac{1}{4}x + 3y = \frac{2}{3} \) once the \( \frac{3}{2}y \) is brought across; the second becomes \( \frac{1}{6}x - py = \frac{13}{10} \) . Matching x-coefficients, \( \frac{1}{6} \div \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = -\frac{2}{3} \) , so the y-coefficients must satisfy \( -p = 3\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = -2 \) , giving p = 2. The constants do not follow the same ratio, so the lines really are parallel and not identical.

questions.stem:
An equation for the graph shown is

\[ y = a(x + 3)(x + b) \]

where a and b are constants. What is the value of ab?
questions.whyCorrect: The graph crosses the x-axis at −3 and 4. The factor \( (x + 3) \) already accounts for the zero at −3, so \( (x + b) \) must vanish at x = 4, which means b = −4 — the sign flips. For a, use the y-intercept: the curve passes through (0, −4), and \( a(3)(-4) = -12a = -4 \) gives \( a = \frac{1}{3} \) . So \( ab = \frac{1}{3}(-4) = -\frac{4}{3} \) .

whyWrong.A: −2 comes from misreading the y-intercept as −6, which would make \( a = \frac{1}{2} \) .
whyWrong.C: \( \frac{1}{2} \) is a value of a from that same misreading, not the product ab.
whyWrong.D: 8 keeps b = 4 instead of −4 (forgetting that a zero at 4 needs the factor x − 4) and pairs it with a = 2.

questions.stem:
\[ \frac{x}{7} + \frac{y}{5} = \frac{41}{35} \]

An engineer connects resistors in series, where the resistors in the series have a total resistance of \( \frac{41}{35} \) ohms. In this series, there are x resistors of type A, which each have a resistance of a ohms, and y resistors of type B, which each have a resistance of b ohms. The given equation represents this situation. According to this equation, what is the positive difference between the value of a and the value of b?
questions.whyCorrect: In series the resistances add, so the total is \( ax + by \) . Matching that against \( \frac{x}{7} + \frac{y}{5} \) term by term, the coefficient of x is \( a = \frac{1}{7} \) and the coefficient of y is \( b = \frac{1}{5} \) . The difference is \( \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{7} = \frac{7 - 5}{35} = \frac{2}{35} \) . The 7 and 5 are denominators, so a and b are their reciprocals, not the numbers themselves.

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{1}{35} \) is \( \frac{1}{7} \times \frac{1}{5} \) , the product of the two resistances rather than their difference.
whyWrong.C: \( \frac{3}{35} \) does not come from these values; check the subtraction, \( \frac{7 - 5}{35} \) .
whyWrong.D: \( \frac{12}{35} \) is \( \frac{1}{7} + \frac{1}{5} \) , the sum instead of the difference.

questions.note: The slice records this as free response; the book prints four choices.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by \( f(x) = -a^{x} + b \) , where a and b are constants. In the xy-plane, the graph of y = f(x) - 12 has a y-intercept at \( \left(0, -\frac{75}{7}\right) \) . The product of a and b is 320. What is the value of a?
questions.whyCorrect: A y-intercept is the value at x = 0, so f(0) - 12 = \( -\frac{75}{7} \) . The key step is \( a^{0} = 1 \) for any base, so f(0) = -1 + b and the equation becomes \( b - 13 = -\frac{75}{7} \) , giving \( b = \frac{16}{7} \) . Then ab = 320 gives \( a = 320 \div \frac{16}{7} = 140 \) .
questions.note: The exponent is on a: the printed function is -a^x + b, not -ax + b. Text extraction drops the superscript.

questions.stem:
\[ j(x - k) = \frac{3}{4}x + 15 \]

In the equation above, j and k are constants. If the equation has infinitely many solutions for x, what is the value of k?
questions.whyCorrect: Infinitely many solutions means the two sides are the same expression, so expand and match coefficients. The left becomes \( jx - jk \) . Matching the x-terms gives \( j = \frac{3}{4} \) ; matching the constants gives \( -jk = 15 \) . Substituting, \( -\frac{3}{4}k = 15 \) , so \( k = -20 \) . Watch the minus sign that comes out of the parentheses — dropping it gives +20.

questions.stem:
The graph of \( f(x) \) is the result of shifting the graph of \( g(x) \) 3 units to the right and 3 units up. If the equation of \( f(x) \) is

\[ f(x) = x^{2} + 4x \]

what is the equation of \( g(x) \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: f is the shifted one, so to recover g you undo the shift: move 3 left and 3 down, that is \( g(x) = f(x + 3) - 3 \) . Put f in vertex form first: \( f(x) = (x + 2)^{2} - 4 \) , with vertex (−2, −4). Undoing the shift moves the vertex to (−5, −7), so \( g(x) = (x + 5)^{2} - 7 \) .

whyWrong.A: This shifts f the same way again instead of undoing it, and it adds 3 rather than subtracting.
whyWrong.B: The vertical part is right, but the horizontal shift went the wrong way, to +5 instead of −5.
whyWrong.D: The horizontal shift is right but the vertical one was never applied: −4 is f's vertex height, not g's.

questions.stem: Harold is writing a book. To finish by his deadline, he needs to write an average of 3,000 words per week for 4 weeks. He wrote 4,500 words in the first week, 2,800 words in the second week, and 2,400 words in the third week. Which inequality represents the number of words, x, Harold needs to write in the 4th week to meet or exceed his goal?
questions.whyCorrect: An average of 3,000 words over 4 weeks means a total of \(4 \times 3{,}000 = 12{,}000\) words. Add the four weekly totals on the left and require that sum to be at least 12,000; that is exactly choice A. Clearing the fraction from \(\frac{4{,}500+2{,}800+2{,}400+x}{4} \ge 3{,}000\) gives the same inequality.

whyWrong.B: This averages only the first three weeks and then adds the whole fourth week to that average, mixing a per-week figure with a weekly total.
whyWrong.C: Here x multiplies 3,000 rather than counting words, and the inequality points the wrong way — it says the words already written are at least some multiple of 3,000.
whyWrong.D: Only the three known weeks are divided by 4; x is not. Every term has to be inside the average, or none of them.

questions.stem: Line segment GH and point R are shown in the xy-plane. If line \( \ell \) (not shown) contains point R and is perpendicular to line segment GH, which of the following is an equation of line \( \ell \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Read the two endpoints off the grid: G is at (0, 3) and H at (4, 0), so segment GH has slope \( \frac{0 - 3}{4 - 0} = -\frac{3}{4} \) and the perpendicular slope is \( \frac{4}{3} \) . Line \( \ell \) passes through R at (0, 2), so \( y = \frac{4}{3}x + 2 \) . Clearing the fraction gives \( 3y = 4x + 6 \) , that is \( -4x + 3y = 6 \) . Checking a choice quickly: put x = 0 and see whether y = 2.

whyWrong.B: Its slope is \( \frac{3}{4} \) , the negative of GH's slope rather than the negative reciprocal, and at x = 0 it gives y = 2 by coincidence.
whyWrong.C: Its slope is \( -\frac{3}{4} \) , which is parallel to GH, not perpendicular.
whyWrong.D: Its slope is \( -\frac{4}{3} \) : the fraction is flipped but the sign is wrong, so it is perpendicular to the wrong line.

questions.imageAlt: Coordinate grid in the xy-plane with x- and y-axes labelled 1 through 6, showing a line segment labelled G to H and a separate marked point R.

questions.stem: The xy-plane above shows two points of intersection of the graphs of a linear function and a quadratic function. The vertex of the graph of the quadratic function is at (3, −4) and (r, s) is one of the points of intersection of the graphs. What is the value of r?
questions.whyCorrect: Build both functions from the figure. The line passes through (0, −6) and the vertex (3, −4), so its slope is \( \frac{2}{3} \) and \( y = \frac{2}{3}x - 6 \) . The parabola has vertex (3, −4) and x-intercepts at 0 and 6, so \( y = A(x - 3)^{2} - 4 \) with \( 9A = 4 \) , that is \( A = \frac{4}{9} \) . Setting them equal, \( \frac{4}{9}(x - 3)^{2} = \frac{2}{3}(x - 3) \) , and factoring out \( (x - 3) \) leaves \( \frac{4}{9}(x - 3) = \frac{2}{3} \) , so \( x - 3 = \frac{3}{2} \) and r = 4.5. Factoring rather than expanding keeps the known root x = 3 out of the way.
questions.note: The stem alone does not fix the parabola's leading coefficient; it has to be read off the figure, where the curve meets the x-axis at 0 and 6, giving A = 4/9.
questions.imageAlt: The xy-plane showing an upward-opening parabola and a straight line that cross each other; two intersection points and the line's y-intercept are marked with dots.

questions.stem: The three points shown define a circle. The circumference of this circle is \(k\pi\), where k is a constant. What is the value of k?
questions.whyCorrect: Two of the points share the x-coordinate 12, so the chord joining them is vertical and the center lies on its perpendicular bisector, the horizontal line y = 7. Write the center as (h, 7) and set the distances to two of the points equal: \((h-12)^{2}+3^{2}=(h-9)^{2}\). Expanding gives \(-24h+153=-18h+81\), so h = 12 and the center is (12, 7) with radius 3. The circumference is \(2\pi(3)=6\pi\), so k = 6.

whyWrong.A: 3 is the radius. Circumference is \(2\pi r\), so the coefficient of \(\pi\) is 6.
whyWrong.C: 9 is \(r^{2}\), the coefficient of \(\pi\) in the area, not the circumference.
whyWrong.D: This uses the diameter 6 in place of the radius in \(2\pi r\), doubling the circumference.

questions.note: Figure needed: an xy-grid with both axes running from 0 to about 15, with three plotted points at (12, 10), (9, 7) and (12, 4). The coordinates appear only in the figure.
questions.imageAlt: Three plotted points on a square grid in the xy-plane, with both axes running from 0 to 15.

questions.stem: The mass of object A is 450% of the mass of object B, and the mass of object A is 0.090% of the mass of object C. If the mass of object C is p% of the mass of object B, what is the value of \(\frac{p}{1{,}000}\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Turn each percent into a decimal multiplier before doing anything else. \(A=4.5B\) and \(A=0.0009C\), so \(0.0009C=4.5B\) and \(C=\frac{4.5}{0.0009}B=5{,}000B\). Writing that as a percent, C is 500,000% of B, so p = 500,000 and \(\frac{p}{1{,}000}=500\). The two places the arithmetic goes wrong are reading 0.090% as 0.09 instead of 0.0009, and forgetting the final division by 1,000 that the question actually asks for.

questions.stem: The graph shows the total amount of rainfall y, in centimeters, from the start of a 10-hour period, where x is the number of hours after the start of the period. Which of the following statements about the rainfall during this time period is true?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The rate of rainfall was 2 centimeters per hour between x = 2 and x = 4.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The rate of rainfall was the greatest between x = 4 and x = 10.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The rate of rainfall increased between x = 0 and x = 2.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The rate of rainfall was 0 centimeters per hour between x = 2 and x = 4.

questions.whyCorrect: The graph plots the total rainfall so far, so the rate of rainfall is the graph's steepness, not its height. Between x = 2 and x = 4 the graph is flat at 2 centimeters: the total is not growing, so no rain fell and the rate was 0 centimeters per hour.

whyWrong.A: 2 is the height of the graph over that stretch, the total accumulated, not the slope. The slope there is zero.
whyWrong.B: From x = 4 to x = 10 the graph rises only about 0.6 centimeters in 6 hours, a rate of about 0.1. The steepest stretch is the first two hours, at about 1 centimeter per hour.
whyWrong.C: From x = 0 to x = 2 the graph is a straight line, so the rate is constant. The total rises, but a constant slope means an unchanging rate.

questions.stem: The graph of \( y = f(x) - k \) is shown in the xy-plane. If \(k\), \(a\), and \(b\) are positive constants, which equation could define \(f\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Start from the end behaviour. The curve rises on the left and on the right, so the degree is even — that alone kills both cubic choices. Then use the two minimum points: they sit at the same height, and \( y = f(x)-k \) is just \(f\) pushed down \(k\) units, so \(f\) itself has two equal minimum values, each equal to 0. A quartic whose two minima are both 0 is a perfect square with two double roots, one at a negative \(x\) (about \(-1.5\)) and one at a positive \(x\) (about 5), which is what \( f(x)=(x+a)^2(x-b)^2 \) gives with \(a\) and \(b\) positive.

whyWrong.A: This is a cubic with a positive leading coefficient, so it falls without bound on the left; the graph shown rises on the left. A cubic also has only one local minimum, not two.
whyWrong.B: Same problem as A — degree 3, so the left end goes down instead of up, and there is only one local minimum.
whyWrong.C: This has the same shape as the correct choice (a double root at a positive \(x\) and a double root at a negative \(x\)), so it is not distinguishable from D; see the note.

questions.note: DEFECT: choices C and D are equivalent. With a and b any positive constants, (x-a)^2(x+b)^2 and (x+a)^2(x-b)^2 both describe a quartic with one positive and one negative double root, so both fit the graph. The item has two correct answers.
questions.imageAlt: Coordinate grid in the xy-plane with the x-axis marked at −10, −5, 5 and 10 and the y-axis marked at −10 and 10, showing a single W-shaped quartic curve.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = 9x - 7 \]Function f is defined by the given equation. The function g is defined by \[ g(x) = f(x) - (7x - 2). \]What is the x-coordinate of the x-intercept of the graph of y = g(x) in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: Substitute the formula for f and distribute the subtraction across both terms in the bracket: g(x) = (9x - 7) - 7x + 2 = 2x - 5. An x-intercept has y = 0, so set 2x - 5 = 0, giving \( x = \frac{5}{2} \) .

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{9}{16} \) comes from adding the two expressions instead of subtracting: 9x - 7 + 7x - 2 = 16x - 9.
whyWrong.B: \( \frac{7}{9} \) is the x-intercept of f itself, from 9x - 7 = 0. The question asks about g, not f.
whyWrong.D: \( \frac{9}{2} \) comes from dropping the minus sign on the 2, giving 2x - 9 instead of 2x - 5. Subtracting -2 adds 2.

questions.note: The book prints "Whats is" and "ing the xy-plane"; corrected here.

questions.stem: Alex engages in up to 3 types of exercise each week for a total of 9 hours while training for a triathlon. Alex swims for the same number of minutes each week. The equation y = 540 − x − 200 represents the situation, where Alex bikes for x minutes during a week and runs for any remaining training time, y, in minutes. If this equation is graphed in the xy-plane, which statement is the best interpretation of the x-intercept of the graph?

choices.label: A
choices.content: During a week when Alex swims for 340 minutes, he bikes for 200 minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Each week, Alex bikes and runs for a total of 340 minutes.

choices.label: C
choices.content: During a week when Alex doesn't bike, he runs for 340 minutes.

choices.label: D
choices.content: During a week when Alex doesn't run, he bikes for 340 minutes.

questions.whyCorrect: At an x-intercept, y = 0. Here y is running minutes, so y = 0 means Alex does no running that week. Setting 0 = 540 − x − 200 gives x = 340, and x is biking minutes. So the x-intercept says: in a week with no running, Alex bikes 340 minutes.

whyWrong.A: Swimming is the fixed 200 minutes subtracted in the equation, not a variable. Neither coordinate of the x-intercept refers to swim time.
whyWrong.B: 340 is the value of x alone at that one point, not a weekly total of two activities. Bike plus run is 340 only when running happens to be zero.
whyWrong.C: This swaps the roles of the variables. Zero biking is the y-intercept (x = 0), which gives y = 340 minutes of running — a different point on the graph.

questions.stem: The difference between the measure of angle A and the measure of angle B is \( -\frac{5}{12}\pi \) radians. Which expression shows the difference between the measure of angle A and the measure of angle B, in degrees?
questions.whyCorrect: Radians become degrees when you multiply by \( \frac{180^{\circ}}{\pi} \), since π radians is 180°. Apply it to the whole radian measure: \( -\frac{5}{12}\pi \cdot \frac{180^{\circ}}{\pi} \), which simplifies to -75°.

whyWrong.B: \( \frac{\pi}{180^{\circ}} \) is the factor that converts degrees into radians, so this runs the conversion backwards.
whyWrong.C: This has both errors at once: the reciprocal factor and 360 in place of 180.
whyWrong.D: 360° corresponds to 2π radians, not π, so this factor is twice too large and gives -150°.

questions.note: Same template as Lines&Angles question 17 in this book, with -5/12 pi in place of -3/4 pi.

questions.stem:
ValuesData set A frequencyData set B frequencyData set C frequencyData set D frequency
400088
432334
464332
498800
The table shows the frequencies of the data values for four data sets. Which data set has the greatest mean?
questions.whyCorrect: Every column totals 14 values, so the one with the greatest mean is the one whose weight sits highest up the value list. Sets C and D are built out of 40s and 43s and can be eliminated at a glance. Between A and B, both put 8 values at 49, but A has 4 values at 46 and only 2 at 43, while B has 3 and 3 — swapping a 43 for a 46 raises the total, so A wins. The sums are 662 for A against 659 for B, giving means of about 47.3 and 47.1.

whyWrong.B: B has the same eight 49s as A but trades one 46 for a 43, which lowers its total by 3 and so lowers its mean.
whyWrong.C: C puts 8 of its 14 values at 40, the smallest value, and none at 49; its mean is about 41.9.
whyWrong.D: D is the lowest of all, with 8 values at 40 and only 2 at 46; its mean is about 41.7.

questions.stem: An employee earns $30 per hour for the first 40 hours worked in a week. For each hour worked over 40 hours, the employee earns $45 per hour. What is the least number of whole hours that the employee must work in a week to earn at least $1,610?
questions.whyCorrect: The first 40 hours bring in 40 × 30 = $1,200, leaving 1,610 − 1,200 = $410 to earn at the overtime rate. Since \( \frac{410}{45} = 9.1\overline{1} \) , nine overtime hours give only $1,605, so a tenth is needed. The question asks for total hours, so the answer is 40 + 10 = 50.

whyWrong.B: This is 40 + 9, rounding the 9.1 overtime hours down. At 49 hours the pay is $1,605, which falls short of $1,610.
whyWrong.C: This is the number of overtime hours alone. The question asks for the total hours worked in the week.
whyWrong.D: This is the overtime figure rounded down and not added to the first 40 hours — two errors at once.

questions.stem: The function \(f(x)=\frac{1}{9}(x-6)^2+3\) gives a toy car’s height above the ground \(f(x)\), in inches, \(x\) seconds after it started moving on an elevated track, where \(0\le x\le 10\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of the vertex of the graph of \(y=f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The toy car’s minimum height was 3 inches above the ground.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The toy car’s minimum height was 6 inches above the ground.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The toy car’s height was 3 inches above the ground when it started moving.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The toy car’s height was 6 inches above the ground when it started moving.

questions.whyCorrect: In vertex form \(a(x-h)^2+k\) the vertex is \((6,3)\), so 6 is a time and 3 is a height. The coefficient \(\frac{1}{9}\) is positive, so the parabola opens upward and the vertex is the lowest point: the minimum height is 3 inches, reached 6 seconds in.

whyWrong.B: 6 is the time in seconds at which the minimum occurs, not the height.
whyWrong.C: “When it started moving” is \(x=0\), and \(f(0)=\frac{36}{9}+3=7\) inches, not 3.
whyWrong.D: Both numbers are misread: 6 is a time, and the starting height is 7 inches.

questions.stem:
For two acute angles, angle Q and angle R,
\[\cos(Q) = \sin(R).\]The measures, in degrees, of angle Q and angle R are x + 61 and 4x + 4, respectively. What is the value of x?
questions.whyCorrect: For acute angles, \(\cos(Q) = \sin(R)\) exactly when Q and R are complementary, so their measures add to 90. That gives (x + 61) + (4x + 4) = 90, so 5x + 65 = 90 and x = 5. Checking: Q = 66° and R = 24°, which do add to 90 and are both acute.

whyWrong.B: This comes from setting the two expressions equal to each other, x + 61 = 4x + 4. Equal sine and cosine values mean the angles are complementary, not equal.
whyWrong.C: This uses 180 instead of 90: 5x + 65 = 180. The angles here are complementary, not supplementary — 180 belongs to angles in a triangle.
whyWrong.D: This sets x + 61 = 90, treating angle Q alone as a right angle. Both angles are stated to be acute, and it is their sum that is 90.

questions.stem: A sleep study consisted of 59 participants, of which 53 participants each had an average of more than 120 minutes of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep per night. If a participant from this study is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a participant that had an average of more than 120 minutes of REM sleep per night?
questions.whyCorrect: The denominator of a probability is the size of the group you are choosing from, which here is the 59 participants in the study — not 100. The numerator is the 53 who met the REM condition, so the probability is \( \frac{53}{59} \).

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{53}{100} \) treats the study as if it had 100 participants; nothing in the stem is out of 100.
whyWrong.B: \( \frac{59}{100} \) uses the total group size as the numerator and an invented denominator of 100.
whyWrong.D: \( \frac{59}{53} \) inverts the fraction. A probability can never exceed 1, so this is impossible on sight.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = m\sqrt{-x-n} \]where \(m\) and \(n\) are constants. If \( f(8)=0 \) and \( f(4) < -16 \), which of the following must be true?
questions.whyCorrect: Pin down \(n\) first. \( f(8) = m\sqrt{-8-n} = 0 \) forces either \(m=0\) or the radical to be 0, and \(m=0\) would make \(f(4)=0\), which contradicts \( f(4) < -16 \). So \( -8-n = 0 \), giving \( n = -8 \) and \( f(x) = m\sqrt{8-x} \). Then \( f(4) = m\sqrt{4} = 2m < -16 \), so \( m < -8 \). With \(n=-8\), \( n-m = -8-m \), and \( m < -8 \) makes \( -8-m > 0 \).

whyWrong.A: This reverses the inequality. Dividing \( 2m < -16 \) by 2 gives \( m < -8 \), not \( m > -8 \).
whyWrong.B: \( n+m=0 \) with \(n=-8\) would mean \(m=8\), a positive \(m\); then \(f(4)=16\), not less than \(-16\).
whyWrong.C: \( n+m > 0 \) means \( m > 8 \), the opposite sign for \(m\). It comes from treating \(m\) as positive after dropping the minus sign in \( f(4) < -16 \).

questions.stem: During the first 5.00 seconds after a car started moving, its speed increased to 12.0 meters per second. From 5.00 seconds to 13.0 seconds after the car started moving, its speed increased from 12.0 meters per second to 25.0 meters per second. To the nearest hundredth, what is the positive difference between the average rate of change of the speed of the car, in meters per second per second, during the first 5.00 seconds after the car started moving and the average rate of change of the speed of the car, in meters per second per second, from 5.00 seconds to 13.0 seconds after the car started moving?
questions.whyCorrect: Average rate of change is change in speed divided by the time it took. The car starts from rest, so the first interval is (12.0 - 0) ÷ 5.00 = 2.40. The second interval runs from 5.00 to 13.0 seconds, a span of 8.00 seconds, so it is (25.0 - 12.0) ÷ 8.00 = 1.625. The positive difference is 2.40 - 1.625 = 0.775, which rounds to 0.78. The trap is dividing the second change by 13.0 instead of by the 8.00-second length of that interval.

questions.stem: The solutions to \( x^{2} + 12x + 35 = 0 \) are r and s, where \( r < s \) . The solutions to \( x^{2} + 12x + 27 = 0 \) are t and u, where \( t < u \) . The solutions to \( x^{2} + 24x + c = 0 \) , where c is a constant, are \( r + u \) and \( s + t \) . What is the value of c?
questions.whyCorrect: Factor both quadratics. \( x^{2} + 12x + 35 = (x + 7)(x + 5) \) gives r = −7 and s = −5, and \( x^{2} + 12x + 27 = (x + 9)(x + 3) \) gives t = −9 and u = −3 — keeping the ordering \( r < s \) and \( t < u \) straight is what makes the rest work. The new roots are \( r + u = -10 \) and \( s + t = -14 \) . For a monic quadratic the constant term is the product of the roots, so \( c = (-10)(-14) = 140 \) . (Their sum, −24, matches the given 24x, a useful check.)

questions.stem:
7kx + 13my = 20.5
6kx + 5my = -48

In the given system of equations, k and m are constants. The system has a solution of (2, y). What is the value of k?
questions.whyCorrect: The solution has x = 2, so substitute it and treat the whole product my as a single unknown: 14k + 13(my) = 20.5 and 12k + 5(my) = -48. Eliminate my by multiplying the first by 5 and the second by 13: 70k + 65(my) = 102.5 and 156k + 65(my) = -624. Subtracting gives 86k = -726.5, so \( k = -\frac{1453}{172} \) , about -8.4477.
questions.note: The exact value is -1453/172 = -8.44767..., which does not fit a grid-in field and is not an SAT-shaped answer. The arithmetic was checked with sympy against the printed coefficients (7, 13, 20.5; 6, 5, -48) and x = 2. A constant in the printed system is probably mistyped. Flag for human review before shipping.

questions.stem: For the function f, for every increase of \( \frac{1}{2} \) in the value of x, the value of f(x) increases by a factor of c, where c is a constant. Which of the following equivalent forms of the function f displays the value of c as the base?
questions.whyCorrect: All four are the same function, \( f(x) = 38(64)^{x} \) , so simplifying gets you nowhere — you have to match the exponent to the step size. Raising x by \( \frac{1}{2} \) multiplies f by \( 64^{\frac{1}{2}} = 8 \) , so c = 8. A base shows the factor for one unit of whatever sits in the exponent, and only choice B has exponent 2x, which counts half-units of x, so its base 8 is c.

whyWrong.A: The exponent 6x counts sixths of a unit of x, so base 2 is the factor for an increase of \( \frac{1}{6} \) , not \( \frac{1}{2} \) .
whyWrong.C: Exponent x means base 64 is the factor for a full unit increase. Halving the step takes the square root, 8.
whyWrong.D: Exponent \( \frac{x}{2} \) counts steps of 2, so 4,096 is the factor for an increase of 2 in x.

questions.note: The book writes "as the base or the coefficient"; only the base is at issue in the four printed forms.

questions.stem:
In the given system of equations, t is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of t?

\[ 4x - 6y = 10y + 2 \]
\[ ty = \frac{1}{2} + 2x \]
questions.whyCorrect: Collect the variables on one side of each equation before comparing anything. The first becomes \( 4x - 16y = 2 \) , the second \( -2x + ty = \frac{1}{2} \) . For no solution the coefficient pairs must be proportional: the x-coefficients scale by \( \frac{-2}{4} = -\frac{1}{2} \) , so \( t = -16 \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = 8 \) . Check the constants: \( 2 \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = -1 \) , which is not \( \frac{1}{2} \) , so the lines are parallel rather than the same line.

questions.stem: \[ 8rx^2 - 80sx + 8r = 0 \]For the given equation, \(r\) and \(s\) are constants such that \( r > 0 \), \( s < 0 \) and \( \frac{r}{s} > k \). What is the least value of \(k\) that ensures that the equation has two distinct real solutions?
questions.whyCorrect: Two distinct real solutions means the discriminant is positive: \( (-80s)^2 - 4(8r)(8r) > 0 \), i.e. \( 6400s^2 - 256r^2 > 0 \), so \( r^2 < 25s^2 \). Divide by \( s^2 \) to get \( \left(\frac{r}{s}\right)^2 < 25 \), so \( -5 < \frac{r}{s} < 5 \). Because \( r > 0 \) and \( s < 0 \), the ratio \( \frac{r}{s} \) is already negative, so the only part of that range that can bind is \( \frac{r}{s} > -5 \). The smallest \(k\) for which \( \frac{r}{s} > k \) still guarantees a positive discriminant is therefore \( k = -5 \).

questions.whyCorrect: Standard deviation asks how far values sit from the mean, so the winner is the table that concentrates its counts on one value. A puts 40 of its 60 values at 6 and the other 20 just one unit away, giving about 0.58 — no other table comes close.

whyWrong.B: A mound shape, but a broad one: 16 of its 60 values are two units from the center, giving about 1.24.
whyWrong.C: A flat distribution — 4 and 8 occur exactly as often as 6 — which is wide, about 1.41.

questions.stem:
\[ \frac{20}{p} = \frac{20}{q} - \frac{20}{r} - \frac{20}{s} \]

The given equation relates the positive variables p, q, r, and s. Which of the following is equivalent to q?
questions.whyCorrect: Every term carries a 20, so divide it out at once: \( \frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{q} - \frac{1}{r} - \frac{1}{s} \) . Isolate the reciprocal of q rather than q itself: \( \frac{1}{q} = \frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{r} + \frac{1}{s} = \frac{rs + ps + pr}{prs} \) . Only now take reciprocals of both sides, giving \( q = \frac{prs}{pr + rs + ps} \) .

whyWrong.A: This is what you get by reading \( \frac{1}{q} = \frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{r} + \frac{1}{s} \) as q = p + r + s. Reciprocals do not distribute over addition.
whyWrong.B: Same error, with the 20 kept even though it cancels from every term.
whyWrong.D: The 20s cancel completely, so leaving three of them in the denominator makes this 20 times too small.

questions.note: The slice records this as free response; the book prints four choices.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \( \sqrt[12]{x^{5}y^{5}} \) , where x and y are positive?
questions.whyCorrect: Since x and y carry the same exponent, \( x^{5}y^{5} = (xy)^{5} \) . A twelfth root is the power \( \frac{1}{12} \) , so the expression is \( (xy)^{\frac{5}{12}} \) — the root index goes in the denominator.

whyWrong.A: The fraction is upside down. The index of the root is the denominator, not the numerator.
whyWrong.C: This adds 5 and 12. Roots and powers combine by multiplying exponents, never by adding them.
whyWrong.D: This multiplies 5 by 12. Taking a root makes the exponent smaller, so the answer must be less than 5, not far greater.

questions.stem: Rectangles \(ABCD\) and \(EFGH\) are similar. The length of each side of \(EFGH\) is 6 times the length of the corresponding side of \(ABCD\). The area of \(ABCD\) is 96 square units. What is the area, in square units, of \(EFGH\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Both dimensions are 6 times longer, so the area grows by \(6^2 = 36\), not by 6. That gives 96 × 36 = 3,456 square units.

whyWrong.A: 16 is 96 ÷ 6 — shrinking instead of enlarging, and by the length factor rather than its square.
whyWrong.B: 36 is the area factor itself, not the new area. It still has to multiply 96.
whyWrong.C: 576 is 96 × 6, scaling by the length factor once. A second dimension also grew by 6.

questions.stem: The cost to rent a bus from Company X is $750 for the first 2 hours and an additional $50 per hour for each hour after the first 2 hours. If the total cost to rent the bus from Company X for t hours, where t > 2, is $1,050, which equation represents this situation?
questions.whyCorrect: The $750 is a flat charge covering the first 2 hours, so it is not multiplied by anything. The hours that get billed at $50 are the ones beyond the first two, and there are t − 2 of them. Adding the two parts gives 750 + 50(t − 2) = 1,050.

whyWrong.A: This multiplies the flat $750 by the number of extra hours and then charges $50 for every hour including the first two. Both parts are backwards.
whyWrong.B: 750(2t) charges the flat fee twice for each hour. The $750 is paid once, no matter how long the rental runs.
whyWrong.D: 50(2t) bills 2t hours at $50, which double-counts the whole rental instead of counting only the hours past the second.

questions.stem:
Data set \(A\) and data set \(B\) each consist of 26 values. The table shows the frequencies of the values for each data set.
ValueData set \(A\) frequencyData set \(B\) frequency
4028
4347
4655
4974
5282
Which of the following statements best compares the means of the two data sets?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The mean of data set \(A\) is greater than the mean of data set \(B\).

choices.label: B
choices.content: The mean of data set \(A\) is less than the mean of data set \(B\).

choices.label: C
choices.content: The mean of data set \(A\) is equal to the mean of data set \(B\).

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is not enough information to compare the means of the data sets.

questions.whyCorrect: The two data sets use the same five values and the same total count, 26, so only the weighting differs. Data set \(A\) puts its biggest frequencies on the largest values (7 at 49 and 8 at 52) while data set \(B\) puts them on the smallest (8 at 40 and 7 at 43) — the frequency columns are mirror images. So \(A\) must have the larger mean. If you compute: \(A\) totals 1,241 and \(B\) totals 1,151, giving means of about 47.7 and 44.3.

whyWrong.B: This reads the columns the wrong way round. Data set \(B\)'s weight sits on 40 and 43, the small end.
whyWrong.C: Equal means would need the frequency columns to balance around the same centre; here they lean in opposite directions.
whyWrong.D: Every value and every frequency is given, so both means can be computed exactly.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((x^2+11)^2+(x-8)(x+8)\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Expand each piece separately. \((x^2+11)^2=x^4+22x^2+121\) — the middle term is \(2\cdot 11\cdot x^2\), not zero. \((x-8)(x+8)=x^2-64\). Adding: \(x^4+(22+1)x^2+(121-64)=x^4+23x^2+57\).

whyWrong.A: This drops the \(22x^2\) middle term and adds 64 instead of subtracting it (\(121+64=185\)).
whyWrong.B: The middle term is wrong and the second product has been ignored entirely; 121 alone is the constant from the first square.
whyWrong.C: The \(x^2\) term is right, but the constant subtracts 64 from 11 rather than from 121.

questions.whyCorrect: Compute 5x - 6 at each x and require y to be strictly above it: at x = 3 it is 9, at x = 5 it is 19, at x = 8 it is 34. The values 11, 21 and 39 all exceed those, so every row works.

whyWrong.A: At x = 3 the boundary is 9 and y is 3, which is below it, so the very first row already fails.
whyWrong.B: These y-values sit exactly on the line 5x - 6. The inequality is strict, so equality is not a solution.
whyWrong.D: All three y-values are negative and far below the boundary; at x = 3 the boundary is 9 and y is -9.

questions.stem: In triangle DEF, the measure of ∠D is 114°. Which of the following could be the measure, in degrees, of ∠E?
questions.whyCorrect: The three angles total 180°, so once D takes 114°, angles E and F must share the remaining 66°. Angle F has to be greater than 0, so E must be less than 66. Of the choices only 65 is under 66.

whyWrong.A: 115 alone would already push the total past 180 when added to 114.
whyWrong.C: 67 is the trap: 114 + 67 = 181, just one degree too much, leaving no room for angle F. Check the sum rather than eyeballing which values look small enough.

questions.stem: After 20% of the original number of objects in a group were removed from the group, 180 objects remained in the group. How many objects were removed from the group?
questions.whyCorrect: The 180 that remain are the other 80%, not the whole group. So \(0.80x=180\) gives an original \(x=225\), and the number removed is \(225-180=45\) (or 20% of 225).

whyWrong.A: 36 is 20% of 180. That treats 180 as the original group, but 180 is what was left after the removal.
whyWrong.C: 225 is the original number of objects, not the number removed. The question asks how many were taken out.
whyWrong.D: 900 comes from dividing 180 by 0.20 instead of by 0.80 — that is the size of a group whose 20% is 180.

questions.stem: Which expression is a factor of \( 49p^{19} - 121p^{17} \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Take out the largest common power of p first: \( 49p^{19} - 121p^{17} = p^{17}(49p^{2} - 121) \) . What is left is a difference of squares, \( (7p)^{2} - (11)^{2} \) , which factors as \( (7p-11)(7p+11) \) . So \( 7p + 11 \) is a factor.

whyWrong.B: This is a sum of squares, and the bracket after factoring is a difference. A sum of squares does not factor over the real numbers anyway.
whyWrong.C: The 7 and 11 have been swapped. The coefficient 7 belongs with p, since \( 49p^{2} = (7p)^{2} \) .
whyWrong.D: Nothing in the factoring produces a degree of 40 — the original expression is only degree 19.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, angle B is a right angle and the length of \(\overline{BC}\) is 204 millimeters. If \(\cos A = \frac{3}{5}\), what is the length, in millimeters, of \(\overline{AB}\)?
questions.whyCorrect: With the right angle at B, AC is the hypotenuse, AB is the leg adjacent to angle A and BC is the leg opposite it. So \(\cos A = \frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{3}{5}\), which makes this a 3-4-5 triangle with AB : BC : AC = 3 : 4 : 5. The given side BC = 204 matches the 4, so the scale factor is 204 ÷ 4 = 51, and AB = 3(51) = 153.

whyWrong.A: This is AC, the hypotenuse: 5(51) = 255. The question asks for the leg AB.
whyWrong.B: This just repeats the given length BC. BC is opposite angle A, not adjacent to it, so it is not the side the cosine's numerator refers to.
whyWrong.D: This is the scale factor 51 itself, from 204 ÷ 4. You still have to multiply it by the 3 in the ratio.

questions.stem: A survey was conducted in Madison to estimate the percent of adult residents who support the addition of streetlights at every corner in their town. Based on the survey, it is estimated that 40% of all adult residents of Madison support the addition of streetlights at every corner in their town, with an associated margin of error of 6%. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion about all adult residents of Madison?

choices.label: A
choices.content: Plausible values for the percent of all adult residents of Madison who support the addition of streetlights at every corner in their town are between 34% and 46%.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The addition of streetlights at every corner in the town is supported by exactly 34% of all adult residents of Madison.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Plausible values for the percent of all adult residents of Madison who support the addition of streetlights at every corner in their town are either less than 34% or more than 46%.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The addition of streetlights at every corner in the town is supported by more than 46% of all adult residents of Madison.

questions.whyCorrect: Step the margin of error off either side of the estimate: 40 − 6 = 34 and 40 + 6 = 46. Those two percentages bound the plausible values for the true level of support.

whyWrong.B: 34% is simply the lower endpoint. An interval estimate never asserts an exact population value.
whyWrong.C: These are the values outside the interval, which the survey makes less plausible, not more.
whyWrong.D: 46% is the upper endpoint, so figures above it lie outside what the survey supports.

questions.note: Same template as ma2 Research organizing #10 (Franklin, 77% ± 5%); do not place both in one test.

questions.stem: The total amount of food y in pounds that a zookeeper feeds a giraffe over x days is represented by the equation y = 30x. What is the total amount of food, in pounds, that the zookeeper feeds the giraffe over 3 days?
questions.whyCorrect: x counts days, so substitute x = 3 into the equation you were given: y = 30(3) = 90 pounds. Nothing else in the equation changes — there is no fixed starting amount to add.

whyWrong.A: 30 is the amount for a single day, x = 1. You have to multiply by the 3 days.
whyWrong.B: This adds 3 to 30. The 30 multiplies the number of days, it is not a starting total that days get added to.
whyWrong.D: This multiplies correctly and then adds an extra 3 that the equation does not contain.

questions.stem:
y = 0
\(y=8(x^2-36)\)

Which ordered pair \((x,y)\) is a solution to the given system of equations?
questions.whyCorrect: Substituting \(y=0\) gives \(8(x^2-36)=0\), so \(x^2=36\) and \(x=\pm 6\). The solution points are \((6,0)\) and \((-6,0)\); the \(y\)-coordinate must be 0 because the first equation says so.

whyWrong.A: The coordinates are reversed. \(y\) is forced to 0 by the first equation, so 6 belongs in the \(x\) slot.
whyWrong.B: 36 is \(x^2\), not \(x\), and it is in the \(y\) position as well.
whyWrong.D: 36 is \(x^2\); you still have to take the square root to get \(x=6\).

questions.stem: \[ \sqrt[5]{119n}\left(\sqrt[6]{119n}\right)^{2} \]For what value of x is the given expression equivalent to \( (119n)^{30x} \) , where \( n > 1 \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Treat \( 119n \) as a single base. The first factor is \( (119n)^{\frac{1}{5}} \) and the second is \( \left((119n)^{\frac{1}{6}}\right)^{2} = (119n)^{\frac{1}{3}} \) . Multiplying adds the exponents: \( \frac{1}{5} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{8}{15} \) . Setting \( 30x = \frac{8}{15} \) gives \( x = \frac{8}{450} = \frac{4}{225} \) .

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = |71 - 2x| \]The function f is defined by the given equation. For which of the following values of k does \( f(k) = 3k \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: An absolute value equation splits into two cases. Taking \( 71 - 2k = 3k \) gives \( 5k = 71 \) , so \( k = \frac{71}{5} \) . The other case, \( 2k - 71 = 3k \) , gives k = −71, which has to be thrown out: an absolute value is never negative, so \( 3k \) cannot be negative either. Checking the survivor: \( |71 - 28.4| = 42.6 = 3(14.2) \) .

whyWrong.B: This is the value that makes \( 71 - 2k \) equal to zero, so \( f(k) = 0 \) rather than \( 3k \) .
whyWrong.C: This is \( 3 \times \frac{71}{5} \) , which is the function's value at the correct k, not k itself.
whyWrong.D: This treats the equation as \( 71 - k = 0 \) , ignoring the coefficient 2 inside the absolute value.

questions.stem:
x(r - 7) + 3 = 19x + 25

In the given equation, \(r\) is a positive integer. If the given equation has exactly one solution, what CANNOT be the value of \(r\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Collect the \(x\) terms on one side: \((r - 7)x - 19x = 22\), so \((r - 26)x = 22\). A linear equation of this shape has exactly one solution as long as the coefficient is not zero, so the one value that breaks it is \(r = 26\), which would give \(0 = 22\).

whyWrong.A: \(r = 3\) gives \(-23x = 22\), a perfectly good single solution.
whyWrong.B: 7 makes the parenthesis \(r - 7\) equal 0, but the equation is then \(-19x = 22\), which still has one solution. It is the combined coefficient that matters, not the one in parentheses.
whyWrong.C: \(r = 22\) gives \(-4x = 22\), again one solution.

questions.stem:
xy
−11−25

The table shows two values of x and their corresponding values of y. The graph of the linear equation representing this relationship passes through the point \((\frac{1}{3}, a)\). What is the value of a?
questions.whyCorrect: Build the equation from the two table rows, then evaluate it at \(x = \frac{1}{3}\). The slope is \(\frac{55 - (-25)}{9 - (-11)} = \frac{80}{20} = 4\); watch both double negatives. Using (9, 55): \(55 = 4(9) + b\), so b = 19 and y = 4x + 19. Then \(a = 4 \cdot \frac{1}{3} + 19 = \frac{4}{3} + 19 = \frac{61}{3}\), about 20.33.

questions.stem:
\[ f(x) = (2x - 20)(2x + 8) \]

What is the minimum value of the given function?
questions.whyCorrect: The factored form hands you the zeros: \(2x - 20 = 0\) at \(x = 10\) and \(2x + 8 = 0\) at \(x = -4\). The parabola opens upward, so its minimum sits at the midpoint of the zeros, \(x = \frac{10 + (-4)}{2} = 3\). Then \(f(3) = (6 - 20)(6 + 8) = (-14)(14) = -196\). Note the question wants the minimum value of the function, not the \(x\) where it occurs.

questions.stem:
\[ y > 17 \]
\[ 4x + y < 21 \]The point \( (x, 54) \) is a solution to the given system of inequalities in the xy-plane. Which of the following could be the value of x ?
questions.whyCorrect: The first inequality is already satisfied, since 54 > 17, so it tells you nothing about x. Substitute y = 54 into the second: \( 4x + 54 < 21 \) , so \( 4x < -33 \) and \( x < -8.25 \) . Of the four choices only −9 is less than −8.25.

whyWrong.A: Substituting gives 36 + 54 = 90, nowhere near less than 21. Any positive x makes the left side larger still.
whyWrong.B: This gives 20 + 54 = 74, which is far above 21.
whyWrong.C: This is the trap: negative, but not negative enough. It gives −20 + 54 = 34, still greater than 21. You need \( x < -8.25 \) , not merely x < 0.

questions.stem: A model estimates that the initial number of photons in a beam is 800 when the beam reaches the surface of a certain material. The model also estimates that when the beam passes through this material the number of photons in the beam decreases by 50% for each 13 millimeters of the material the beam passes through. Which equation represents this model, where \(I\) is the estimated number of photons in the beam when the beam reaches a point \(x\) millimeters from the surface?
questions.whyCorrect: Losing 50% leaves a factor of 0.5, and that factor applies once per 13 millimeters, so the exponent must count 13-millimeter intervals: \(\frac{x}{13}\). Hence \(I = 800(0.5)^{\frac{x}{13}}\). Check \(x = 13\): \(I = 400\), half of 800.

whyWrong.B: This halves the beam every single millimeter; at \(x = 13\) it leaves \(800(0.5)^{13} \approx 0.098\) photons.
whyWrong.C: A base of 2 doubles the count, but the beam is being absorbed, so the number must fall.
whyWrong.D: The 13 and the 2 have been swapped into the wrong roles: 13 is the distance per halving, not a growth factor, and 2 is not the interval.

questions.note: Book prints "photos" throughout; transcribed as "photons", which is what the physics and the original question intend.

questions.stem: An environmental scientist is investigating the volatility of 175 organic compounds by finding the boiling point of each compound. The mean boiling point of all 175 compounds is 167 degrees Celsius. The scientist classifies each of these compounds as either semivolatile or volatile. Of the 175 compounds, 50 compounds were classified as semivolatile, and these 50 compounds have a mean boiling point of 327 degrees Celsius. The remaining 125 compounds were classified as volatile. What is the mean boiling point, in degrees Celsius, of the 125 compounds classified as volatile compounds?
questions.whyCorrect: Means do not combine by averaging — work with totals. The 175 compounds have a combined boiling point total of 175 × 167 = 29,225. The 50 semivolatile ones account for 50 × 327 = 16,350. So the 125 volatile compounds total 29,225 − 16,350 = 12,875, and their mean is 12,875 ÷ 125 = 103 degrees Celsius.

questions.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\left(\frac{a}{4} + \frac{b}{3}\right)^{2}\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Use \((m+n)^{2} = m^{2} + 2mn + n^{2}\) with \(m = \frac{a}{4}\) and \(n = \frac{b}{3}\). The squares are \(\frac{a^{2}}{16}\) and \(\frac{b^{2}}{9}\), and the middle term is \(2 \cdot \frac{a}{4} \cdot \frac{b}{3} = \frac{2ab}{12} = \frac{ab}{6}\). Squaring the denominators and remembering the factor of 2 are the two steps that get dropped.

whyWrong.A: This squares the numerators but leaves the denominators alone and drops the middle term entirely.
whyWrong.B: The squares are right, but a binomial squared always has a cross term \(2mn\); it is missing here.
whyWrong.C: The cross term \(\frac{ab}{12}\) omits the factor of 2, and the denominators 4 and 3 were not squared.

questions.stem: \[ x^{2} - 4x - 1 = 0 \] A solution to the given equation is \( x = \sqrt{k} + 2 \) . What is the value of k?
questions.whyCorrect: Solve the equation and match the form. Completing the square gives \( (x - 2)^{2} = 5 \) , so \( x = 2 \pm \sqrt{5} \) . The positive root is \( \sqrt{5} + 2 \) , so \( \sqrt{k} = \sqrt{5} \) and k = 5. Note k is what sits under the radical, not the whole solution.

questions.stem: A circle is inscribed in a square such that the circumference of the circle touches the midpoint of each side of the square. The length of the diagonal of the square is 176 units. What is the area, in square units, of the circle?
questions.whyCorrect: An inscribed circle touching each side's midpoint has diameter equal to the square's side, so its radius is half the side. For a square, diagonal \(d = s\sqrt{2}\), so \(s^{2} = \frac{d^{2}}{2} = \frac{176^{2}}{2} = 15{,}488\). The circle's area is \(\pi r^{2} = \pi\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{\pi s^{2}}{4} = \frac{15{,}488\pi}{4} = 3{,}872\pi\). You never need the side length itself, only its square.

whyWrong.B: \(7{,}744 = 88^{2}\), so this uses half the diagonal as the radius. Half the diagonal reaches a corner of the square, not the midpoint of a side, so it is too long.
whyWrong.C: \(15{,}488 = s^{2}\), so this uses the full side length as the radius instead of as the diameter — the area comes out four times too big.
whyWrong.D: \(30{,}976 = 176^{2}\), so this uses the whole diagonal as the radius.

questions.stem: For each of two rectangles, the ratio of the rectangle's length to its width is 10 to 5. The width of rectangle \(X\) is 16.5 times the width of rectangle \(Y\). How does the length of rectangle \(X\) compare to the length of rectangle \(Y\)?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The length of rectangle \(X\) is 0.5 times the length of rectangle \(Y\).

choices.label: B
choices.content: The length of rectangle \(X\) is 2 times the length of rectangle \(Y\).

choices.label: C
choices.content: The length of rectangle \(X\) is 16.5 times the length of rectangle \(Y\).

choices.label: D
choices.content: The length of rectangle \(X\) is 33 times the length of rectangle \(Y\).

questions.whyCorrect: Both rectangles obey length \(= 2 \times\) width, since \(\frac{10}{5} = 2\). So \(L_X = 2W_X = 2(16.5\,W_Y) = 16.5(2W_Y) = 16.5\,L_Y\). The shape factor of 2 applies to both rectangles and cancels out; only the scale factor 16.5 survives.

whyWrong.A: 0.5 is \(\frac{5}{10}\), the width-to-length ratio inside one rectangle. It says nothing about comparing the two rectangles.
whyWrong.B: 2 is the length-to-width ratio within a single rectangle, not the factor relating rectangle \(X\) to rectangle \(Y\).
whyWrong.D: This multiplies 16.5 by the shape factor 2. That factor applies to \(Y\) as well, so it cancels rather than doubling the comparison.

questions.stem:
y = 18x + 25
y = -14x - 7

What is the solution \((x, y)\) to the given system of equations?
questions.whyCorrect: Both equations already give \(y\), so set them equal: \(18x + 25 = -14x - 7\). That gives \(32x = -32\), so \(x = -1\), and substituting back, \(y = 18(-1) + 25 = 7\).

whyWrong.A: This just reuses the numbers \(-7\) and 25 from the equations; substituting gives \(y = -101\), not 25.
whyWrong.C: This is the correct pair with the coordinates swapped. The first number is \(x\).
whyWrong.D: Again a pair lifted from the constants; \(x = 25\) gives \(y = 475\) in the first equation.

questions.note: The book misprints the fourth choice label as "E)" instead of "D)"; relabeled D here.

questions.stem: The graph of the polynomial function f in the xy-plane, where y = f(x), has x-intercepts of (-5, 0) and (6, 0). Which of the following must be true?
questions.whyCorrect: An x-intercept is a point where the graph crosses the x-axis, so its y-coordinate is 0. The point (-5, 0) on the graph of y = f(x) means the input -5 produces the output 0, which is exactly f(-5) = 0.

whyWrong.A: This reads the -5 as an output at input 0. Nothing in the question says the graph passes through (0, -5); the y-intercept is not given.
whyWrong.B: This pairs the input from one intercept with the number from the other. The point (6, 0) gives f(6) = 0, not -5.
whyWrong.D: This treats the two intercepts as a single input-output pair. They are two separate points, each with output 0.

questions.stem: The triangle shown has one side with a length of x inches and two sides each with a length of y inches. The perimeter of the triangle is 47 inches. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.whyCorrect: Perimeter is the sum of all three side lengths, so add each side once: one side of length x plus two sides of length y each gives x + y + y = x + 2y. Setting that equal to the given perimeter gives x + 2y = 47.

whyWrong.A: This adds only two of the three sides — it counts the side of length y once instead of twice.
whyWrong.C: This doubles the wrong side. There is one side of length x and two of length y, not the other way around.
whyWrong.D: This counts four sides in total. A triangle has three.

questions.stem: A district board in a certain state is proposing a change to the time school starts to all high schools in the district. A sample of 353 high school students were selected from all high school students in the district. The selected students were asked if they approved of the proposed change, and 300 students responded that they did not approve. Which of the following is the largest population that the results of the survey can be generalized?

choices.label: A
choices.content: All high school students in the district

choices.label: C
choices.content: The 300 students that responded that they did not approve of the proposed change

choices.label: D
choices.content: All high school students in the state

questions.whyCorrect: The results generalize to the group the sample was drawn from, and no further. The 353 students were selected from all high school students in the district, so that district-wide group is the largest population the survey speaks for.

whyWrong.B: The whole point of sampling is to say something about a group larger than the sample itself, so this is not the largest population.
whyWrong.C: This is a subset of the sample, smaller still, and it is defined by the answer given — not a population you would generalize to at all.
whyWrong.D: Students in other districts had no chance of being selected, so the survey says nothing about the state as a whole.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by the equation f(x) = 100x + 2. What is the value of f(x) when x = 8?
questions.whyCorrect: Substitute 8 wherever x appears: f(8) = 100(8) + 2. Multiply before adding, so this is 800 + 2 = 802.

whyWrong.A: This adds 100 and 8 and then adds 2. The 100 multiplies x, it is not added to it.
whyWrong.B: This is 100 + 8 + 8, or some other combination by addition. The expression 100x means 100 times x.
whyWrong.C: This is 100(8) with the +2 forgotten. The constant term still has to be added.

questions.stem: A certain neighborhood had a population of 1,130 in 2006. Each year for the next 5 years the population of the neighborhood increased by approximately 4% of the population of the previous year. Which of the following equations represents the population, \(N\), of the neighborhood \(t\) years after 2006, where \(t \le 5\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Increasing by 4% each year multiplies the population by 1.04 annually, so the growth factor 1.04 is the base and the 2006 population 1,130 is the coefficient: \(N = 1{,}130(1.04)^{t}\). Substituting \(t = 0\) returns 1,130, which is the check to run on every one of these.

whyWrong.A: The roles are swapped — the population is raised to the power \(t\) and the rate multiplies it, so \(t=0\) gives a population of 0.04.
whyWrong.B: Base 0.04 means each year the population becomes 4% of the previous year, a 96% collapse.
whyWrong.D: Again the starting population sits in the base, so \(t=0\) gives 1.04 people instead of 1,130.

questions.note: Same template as satmath-ma2-exponential-functions-6 (1,340 at 3%) - do not place both in one test.

questions.stem: A circle in the xy-plane has its center at \((16, 17)\) and has a radius of 7k. Which equation represents this circle?
questions.whyCorrect: Standard form is \((x-h)^{2}+(y-k)^{2} = r^{2}\), and the right side is the radius squared. Squaring 7k means squaring both factors: \((7k)^{2} = 7^{2}k^{2} = 49k^{2}\). All four choices have the same left side, so the whole question is whether you squared the radius correctly.

whyWrong.A: This squares only the 7 and leaves k to the first power. \((7k)^{2}\) squares the entire product.
whyWrong.C: This puts the radius itself on the right instead of its square.
whyWrong.D: This squares only the k and leaves the 7 alone.

questions.stem: The water depth in a certain river is 78.7 feet (ft). During a 30-day period, the water depth in this river is predicted to increase by a minimum of 1 ft and a maximum of 3 ft. What is the predicted maximum water depth, in feet, during this time?
questions.whyCorrect: The maximum final depth comes from the maximum increase, so add the larger of the two increases: 78.7 + 3 = 81.7 feet.

whyWrong.A: 75.7 subtracts 3. The depth is predicted to increase, not fall.
whyWrong.B: 77.7 subtracts 1, again moving in the wrong direction.
whyWrong.C: 79.7 uses the minimum increase of 1 foot, which gives the minimum depth, not the maximum.

questions.stem: A company studied a random sample of 20 lawns in a small town. The company found that 4 of these lawns contain fertilizer. If there are 260 lawns in the town, which of the following is the best estimate of the number of lawns that contain fertilizer?
questions.whyCorrect: The sample rate is \(\frac{4}{20}=0.2\), so apply that rate to the whole town: 0.2 × 260 = 52 lawns. Set it up as the proportion \(\frac{4}{20}=\frac{n}{260}\) if you prefer.

whyWrong.A: 3 is close to \(\frac{260}{...}\) nothing meaningful; it is far too small — a fifth of 260 cannot be a single-digit number.
whyWrong.B: 5 is \(\frac{20}{4}\), the reciprocal of the rate rather than the rate applied to 260.
whyWrong.C: 13 is \(\frac{260}{20}\) — the number of sample-sized groups in the town, not the number of fertilized lawns. You still have to multiply that by 4.

questions.stem:
\[ x^2-28x=0 \]
Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Factor out the common \(x\): \(x(x-28)=0\), so \(x=0\) or \(x=28\). Do not divide both sides by \(x\) — that would lose the \(x=0\) solution, though here 28 is the one offered.

whyWrong.A: 56 doubles 28; substituting gives \(3136-1568=1568\), not 0.
whyWrong.C: 14 halves 28, which would be right for the vertex, not for a root.
whyWrong.D: \(\sqrt{28}\) comes from treating the equation as \(x^2=28\), but the second term is \(28x\), not 28.

questions.stem: For the function f, for each increase in the value of x by c, where c is a positive constant, the value of f(x) increases by a factor of 16. Which of the following forms of the function f displays \( \frac{1}{c} \) as a coefficient of x?
questions.whyCorrect: You want the form written as \( 139(16)^{\frac{1}{c}x} \) : with base 16, the function multiplies by 16 exactly when the exponent rises by 1, which happens when x rises by c. Simplify each base and check. \( 64^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left(4^{3}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}} \) — more simply, \( 64^{\frac{1}{3}} = 4 \) and \( 4^{2} = 16 \) — so choice D is \( 139(16)^{\frac{1}{8}x} \) . Its base is 16 and its coefficient of x is \( \frac{1}{8} \) , so c = 8 and \( \frac{1}{c} = \frac{1}{8} \) is displayed.

whyWrong.A: The base simplifies to \( 16^{\frac{1}{3}} \) , not 16, so f multiplies by 16 only when x rises by 6. The displayed coefficient \( \frac{1}{2} \) is not \( \frac{1}{6} \) .
whyWrong.B: Base 8 with exponent 2x reaches a factor of 16 when x rises by \( \frac{2}{3} \) , so \( \frac{1}{c} = \frac{3}{2} \) , while the displayed coefficient is 2.
whyWrong.C: \( 8^{2} = 64 \) , so this is \( 139(64)^{\frac{1}{2}x} \) , which reaches a factor of 16 when x rises by \( \frac{4}{3} \) . The displayed coefficient \( \frac{1}{2} \) is not \( \frac{3}{4} \) .

questions.note: The book calls these "equivalent forms", but the four printed expressions are not equal to one another (they reduce to 139*2^(2x/3), 139*2^(6x), 139*2^(3x) and 139*2^(x/2)). Exactly one choice, D, satisfies the property the question asks about, so the item is still answerable; the word "equivalent" should be dropped.

questions.stem:
Energy per Gram of Typical Macronutrients
MacronutrientFood caloriesKilojoules
Protein4.016.7
Fat9.037.7
Carbohydrate4.016.7
The table above gives the typical amounts of energy per gram, expressed in both food calories and kilojoules, of the three macronutrients in food. If the 180 food calories in a granola bar come entirely from p grams of protein, f grams of fat, and c grams of carbohydrate, which of the following expresses f in terms of p and c?
