questions.whyCorrect: Use only the food-calorie column; the kilojoule column is there to be ignored. Total calories: 4p + 9f + 4c = 180. Isolate f: 9f = 180 - 4p - 4c, so \( f = 20 - \frac{4}{9}(p + c) \) . The minus sign is the point — more protein or carbohydrate leaves fewer calories for fat.

whyWrong.A: The sign is wrong. Moving 4p + 4c across the equals sign makes them negative, and physically more of the other two nutrients must mean less fat, not more.
whyWrong.C: The two subtracted terms are 4p and 4c, so factoring gives p + c. Writing p - c would mean carbohydrate adds to the fat, which the calorie equation does not say.
whyWrong.D: Both the sign and the fraction are wrong: dividing 4p + 4c by 9 gives \( \frac{4}{9} \) , not \( \frac{9}{4} \) .

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = 250(5)^{x} \]The function f is defined by the given equation. If g(x) = f(x - 2), which of the following equations defines the function g?
questions.whyCorrect: Substitute x - 2 into the formula: \( g(x) = 250(5)^{x-2} \) . Split the exponent using \( 5^{x-2} = \frac{5^{x}}{5^{2}} \) , so \( g(x) = \frac{250}{25}(5)^{x} = 10(5)^{x} \) . Shifting the input changes the coefficient, never the base.

whyWrong.B: 125 is 250 divided by 2, not by \( 5^{2} = 25 \) . Subtracting 2 from the exponent divides by the base twice.
whyWrong.C: Squaring the base is what \( f(2x) \) would do. Replacing x by x - 2 leaves the base alone.
whyWrong.D: Doubling the base is not an exponent rule at all, and the coefficient must change, not stay at 250.

questions.stem:
\[ f(x) = 3 + \left| -2x - x^{2} \right| \]
\[ g(w) = \left| -\frac{w}{w - 1} \right| - w + 5 \]

The functions f and g are defined by the given equations. If \( f(-4) = c \) , where c is a constant, what is the value of \( g(c) \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Work strictly inside out, and keep the absolute value bars until the very last moment. \( f(-4) = 3 + \left| -2(-4) - (-4)^{2} \right| = 3 + |8 - 16| = 3 + 8 = 11 \) — note \( (-4)^{2} \) is +16, so the inside is −8 and the bars make it 8. So c = 11. Then \( g(11) = \left| -\frac{11}{10} \right| - 11 + 5 = 1.1 - 6 = -4.9 \) . Only the fraction sits inside the bars; the −w + 5 is outside and stays negative.

questions.stem:
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by the given equations, where \( x \ge 0 \). Which of the following equations displays, as a constant or coefficient, the maximum value of the function it defines, where \( x \ge 0 \)?
I. \( f(x) = 16(1.24)^x + 43 \)
II. \( g(x) = 8(0.72)^x \)
questions.whyCorrect: Check whether each function even has a maximum on \( x \ge 0 \). In I the base is 1.24, greater than 1, so \(f\) grows without bound as \(x\) increases — there is no maximum value at all, so no number in the equation can display one. In II the base is 0.72, less than 1, so \(g\) decreases; its largest value on \( x \ge 0 \) is at \( x=0 \), where \( g(0) = 8(0.72)^0 = 8 \). That 8 is the coefficient sitting in the equation, so only II displays its maximum.

whyWrong.A: For I, the 43 is the minimum the graph approaches from above as \(x\) decreases, and on \( x \ge 0 \) the smallest value is \( 16+43 = 59 \). Either way it is a floor, not a maximum — an increasing exponential has no maximum.
whyWrong.C: This requires I to have a maximum, which it does not; a base greater than 1 makes the function unbounded above.
whyWrong.D: This misses that a decaying exponential does have a maximum on \( x \ge 0 \), reached at \( x = 0 \), and that its value there is exactly the coefficient 8.

questions.stem:
The equation \( 9x + 5 = a(x + b) \) , where a and b are constants, has no solutions. Which of the following must be true?

I. a = 9
II. b = 5
III. \( b \ne \frac{5}{9} \)
questions.whyCorrect:
Expand the right side to \( ax + ab \) . A linear equation has no solution only when the x-terms match but the constants do not, so you need a = 9 and \( ab 
e 5 \) . With a = 9 the second condition becomes \( 9b 
e 5 \) , that is \( b 
e  rac{5}{9} \) . So statements I and III must hold. Statement II is one allowed value of b among infinitely many, not a requirement.

whyWrong.A: a = 9 alone is not enough: if a = 9 and \( b = \frac{5}{9} \) the two sides are identical and every x is a solution, which is not "no solutions".
whyWrong.B: Without a = 9 the x-coefficients differ, and then the equation has exactly one solution rather than none.
whyWrong.D: Both I and III are forced, so "none of the above" cannot be right.

questions.note: The slice records this as free response; the book prints four choices.

questions.stem: The expression \( 6x^4 + 17x^2 + 7 \) can be rewritten as \( (3x^2+a)(2x^2+b) \), where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive integers, or as \( (3x^2+c)(2x^2+d) \), where \(c\) and \(d\) are positive nonintegers. What is the value of \( a+c \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Expanding \( (3x^2+a)(2x^2+b) \) gives \( 6x^4 + (3b+2a)x^2 + ab \), so you need \( ab = 7 \) and \( 3b+2a = 17 \). The integer pair is \( a=7 \), \( b=1 \) (the other order gives 23, not 17). The same two conditions with nonintegers: substitute \( d = \frac{7}{c} \) into \( 3d+2c = 17 \) to get \( 2c^2 - 17c + 21 = 0 \), whose roots are \( c = 7 \) and \( c = 1.5 \); the noninteger one is \( c = 1.5 \) (with \( d = \frac{14}{3} \)). So \( a + c = 7 + 1.5 = 8.5 \).

questions.stem: Data set A contains 23 positive integers and has mean score of 83. The highest and two lowest values in data set A are removed to create data set B. The average of data set B is 87. What is the greatest possible range of the 3 values that were removed to create data set B?
questions.whyCorrect: Totals do the work: data set A sums to \(23 \times 83 = 1{,}909\) and data set B sums to \(20 \times 87 = 1{,}740\), so the three removed values add to 169. To stretch their range, make the two low ones as small as possible: they are positive integers, so both can be 1, leaving the highest at \(169 - 1 - 1 = 167\). The range is \(167 - 1 = 166\), and it is achievable (the remaining 20 values can all be 87, which lies between 1 and 167).

questions.stem:
In the given pair of equations, a and b are constants. The graph of this pair of equations in the xy-plane is a pair of perpendicular lines.

\[ 5x + 7y = 1 \]
\[ ax + by = 1 \]

Which of the following pairs of equations also represents a pair of perpendicular lines?
questions.whyCorrect: From the original pair, \( 5x + 7y = 1 \) has slope \( -\frac{5}{7} \) , so the other line's slope must be \( \frac{7}{5} \) : \( -\frac{a}{b} = \frac{7}{5} \) , which fixes \( \frac{a}{b} = -\frac{7}{5} \) . Now test each pair with that ratio. In choice B the slopes are \( -\frac{10}{7} \) and \( -\frac{a}{2b} = \frac{7}{10} \) , and their product is −1.

whyWrong.A: The slopes come out as \( -\frac{10}{7} \) and \( -\frac{7}{10} \) . Their product is +1, so the lines are reflections of each other, not perpendicular.
whyWrong.C: Doubling a instead of b gives slopes \( -\frac{10}{7} \) and \( \frac{14}{5} \) , whose product is −4.
whyWrong.D: Flipping the sign on 7y changes the first slope to \( \frac{5}{7} \) while the second line is untouched at \( \frac{7}{5} \) ; the product is +1.

questions.note: The slice records this as free response; the book prints four choices.

questions.stem: The function \(h\) is defined by \[ h(x) = -\sqrt{x^2+bx+c} \]The graph of \( y = h(x) \) passes through \( (2,0) \) and \( \left(0, -\sqrt{358}\right) \). If \( h(m) = 0 \), what is the greatest possible value of \(m\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Use the second point first, because \( x = 0 \) kills two terms: \( h(0) = -\sqrt{c} = -\sqrt{358} \), so \( c = 358 \). The point \( (2,0) \) gives \( -\sqrt{4+2b+358} = 0 \), so \( 2b + 362 = 0 \) and \( b = -181 \). Now \( h(m)=0 \) means \( m^2 - 181m + 358 = 0 \); the discriminant is \( 32761 - 1432 = 31329 = 177^2 \), so \( m = \frac{181 \pm 177}{2} \), i.e. \( m = 2 \) or \( m = 179 \). The greatest is 179.

questions.stem: A circle has center A, and points B and C lie on the circle. Line segments BD and CD are tangent to the circle at points B and C, respectively. The measure of angle BDC is 120°. The length of line segment CD is 12 inches. What is the area of the region that is both inside quadrilateral ABDC and outside the circle, in square inches? (Round your answer to the nearest hundredth of a square inch)
questions.whyCorrect: A radius meets a tangent at a right angle, so angles ABD and ACD are both 90°. The four angles of quadrilateral ABDC sum to 360, so angle BAC = 360 − 90 − 90 − 120 = 60°. Segment AD splits the figure into two congruent right triangles, each with a 30° angle at A, so \(\tan 30^{\circ}=\frac{12}{r}\) and \(r=12\sqrt{3}\). The quadrilateral's area is \(2\cdot\frac{1}{2}(r)(12)=12r=144\sqrt{3}\). The part of the circle inside it is the sector with central angle 60°: \(\frac{60}{360}\pi(12\sqrt{3})^{2}=72\pi\). Subtracting, \(144\sqrt{3}-72\pi\approx 249.415-226.195=23.22\) square inches.

questions.stem: For a poll, an organizer randomly selected 21 professors from a certain liberal arts program at a university. These professors were asked whether they were interested in using a new textbook for their classes, and 14 of them responded "Yes." What is the largest group to which the results of the poll can be generalized?

choices.label: B
choices.content: All liberal arts professors at the university

questions.whyCorrect: Results generalize to exactly the population the sample was drawn from at random. The 21 professors were selected randomly from one liberal arts program, so the poll speaks for the professors in that program and no wider group.

whyWrong.A: The 14 who said yes are a result of the poll, not a population it describes; a poll is never generalized to only the people who gave one particular answer.
whyWrong.B: Other liberal arts programs at the university had no chance of being selected, so nothing here represents them.
whyWrong.D: This is wider still. Professors outside the program, in liberal arts or any other field, were never in the sampling pool.

questions.stem: In the xy-plane, a parabola has vertex \( (9,-14) \) and intersects the x-axis at two points. If the equation of the parabola is written in the form \( y = ax^2+bx+c \) where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants, which of the following could be the value of \( a+b+c \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Notice that \( a+b+c \) is just \( y \) when \( x = 1 \). Write the parabola in vertex form, \( y = a(x-9)^2 - 14 \); since the vertex is below the x-axis and the curve still crosses it twice, the parabola opens upward, so \( a > 0 \). At \( x = 1 \), \( y = 64a - 14 \), and with \( a > 0 \) that is strictly greater than \(-14\). Only \(-12\) clears that bound (it needs \( a = \frac{1}{32} \)).

whyWrong.A: \(-23\) is below \(-14\), which would require \( 64a-14 = -23 \), i.e. a negative \(a\) — then the parabola opens downward from a vertex already below the x-axis and never crosses it.
whyWrong.B: Same problem: \(-19 < -14\) forces \( a < 0 \), contradicting a parabola with two x-intercepts and vertex \( (9,-14) \).
whyWrong.C: \(-14\) is the vertex's y-value, reached only at \( x=9 \); getting it at \( x=1 \) needs \( a=0 \), which is not a parabola at all.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{y + 2}{x - 9} + \frac{y(x - 9)}{x^{2}y - 9xy}\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Factor the second denominator first: \(x^{2}y - 9xy = xy(x-9)\), so the second fraction is \(\frac{y(x-9)}{xy(x-9)} = \frac{1}{x}\). Now add over the common denominator \(x(x-9)\): \(\frac{x(y+2) + (x-9)}{x(x-9)} = \frac{xy + 3x - 9}{x^{2} - 9x}\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(y\) puts it in the printed form \(\frac{xy^{2} + 3xy - 9y}{x^{2}y - 9xy}\).

whyWrong.A: The numerator is wrong and the denominator is \(xy(x-9)^{2}\) — the result of multiplying the two denominators without noticing they share the factor \((x-9)\).
whyWrong.B: This adds the numerators and adds the denominators. Fractions are never added that way.
whyWrong.D: The numerator is right but the denominator was not reduced: \(x^{3}y - 18x^{2}y + 81xy = xy(x-9)^{2}\) carries one extra factor of \((x-9)\), which cancels.

questions.stem:
f(x) = 5x − 9

Function f is defined by the given equation. The function g is defined by g(x) = f(x)(3x − 2). What is the x-coordinate of the x-intercept of the graph of y = g(x) in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: Do not multiply the brackets out. g(x) = (5x − 9)(3x − 2) is a product, and a product is zero exactly when one factor is zero. That gives 5x − 9 = 0, so \(x = \frac{9}{5}\), or 3x − 2 = 0, so \(x = \frac{2}{3}\). Only \(\frac{9}{5}\) appears among the choices.

whyWrong.A: This comes from adding the two expressions instead of using them as separate factors: solving 8x − 11 = 0 gives \(\frac{11}{8}\). The functions are multiplied, not added.
whyWrong.C: There is no step in the problem that produces \(\frac{7}{2}\); it mixes the constants 9 and 2 with the coefficients. Substituting it gives g(x) = 8.5 × 8.5, not 0.
whyWrong.D: This looks like 9 + 2 over 2. Substituting \(x = \frac{11}{2}\) gives (27.5 − 9)(16.5 − 2), which is far from 0.

questions.stem: For two acute angles, ∠A and ∠B, \( \cos A = \sin B \). The measures, in degrees, of ∠A and ∠B are x + 8 and 4x + 2, respectively. What is the value of x?
questions.whyCorrect: For acute angles, the cosine of one equals the sine of another exactly when the two angles are complementary — that is the meaning of "co-sine". So set the measures to add to 90: (x + 8) + (4x + 2) = 90, giving 5x + 10 = 90 and x = 16. Check: the angles are 24° and 66°, which add to 90°.

whyWrong.A: 37 makes the angles 45° and 150°. Those sum to 195°, and 150° is not acute, so both stated conditions fail.
whyWrong.B: 34 makes the angles 42° and 138°, which sum to 180°, not 90°. Supplementary is the wrong relationship — that is what equal sines would give.
whyWrong.D: 2 makes the angles 10° and 10°. Equal angles would mean sin A = sin B, not cos A = sin B.

questions.stem:
The values in data sets \(X\) and \(Y\) are shown in the table.
Data set \(X\)131314141516161717
Data set \(Y\)223345566
The standard deviation of data set \(X\) is \(q\), and the standard deviation of data set \(Y\) is \(s\). Which of the following statements about the standard deviation of the data sets is true?

choices.label: D
choices.content: The relationship between \(q\) and \(s\) cannot be determined.

questions.whyCorrect: Line the two rows up: 13 and 2, 14 and 3, 15 and 4, 16 and 5, 17 and 6. Every value of \(Y\) is exactly 11 less than the matching value of \(X\), so \(Y\) is \(X\) shifted down by a constant. Subtracting the same amount from every value slides the whole distribution without changing how far the values sit from each other, so the standard deviations are identical.

whyWrong.A: \(Y\)'s numbers are smaller, but standard deviation measures spread, not size. Both sets spread the same distance around their own means.
whyWrong.B: Same mistake in reverse — \(X\)'s larger numbers do not make it more spread out.
whyWrong.D: Both data sets are listed in full, so both standard deviations are fully determined.

questions.note: The book prints this as a two-row table with data set X on the first row and data set Y on the second; rendered here with the X row as the header row.

questions.stem:
\[ x^2+2x=72 \]
What is one of the solutions to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Complete the square: \(x^2+2x+1=72+1\), so \((x+1)^2=73\) and \(x=-1\pm\sqrt{73}\). The 1 you add to complete the square also goes onto the right side, which is why the radicand is 73 and not 71.

whyWrong.A: The radicand is right but the sign is not: \((x+1)^2\) gives \(x=-1\pm\sqrt{73}\), not \(+1\).
whyWrong.B: Both parts are wrong — the sign, and a radicand of 71 from subtracting 1 from 72 instead of adding.
whyWrong.D: Correct sign, but 71 comes from subtracting the completing-the-square constant instead of adding it.

questions.stem: When several resistors are connected in series in a circuit, the total resistance of the circuit is the sum of the resistances of these resistors. A certain circuit consists of 8 resistors connected in series, where the resistance of each resistor is positive. This circuit has a total resistance of 130 ohms. The total resistance of 3 resistors in this circuit is 90 ohms. Which inequality best represents all possible values of the resistance x, in ohms, of one of the other 5 resistors in this circuit?
questions.whyCorrect: The other 5 resistors must account for 130 - 90 = 40 ohms between them. Every resistance is positive, so one of the five is more than 0, and since the other four also take a positive share, no single one can reach the full 40. That gives 0 < x < 40.

whyWrong.A: 8 is the number of resistors, not an amount of resistance. Nothing caps a single resistor at 8 ohms.
whyWrong.C: 40 is the total for all five, so it is an upper bound, not a lower one. A single resistor cannot exceed the group total.
whyWrong.D: 130 is the resistance of the whole circuit, including the three resistors already accounted for by the 90 ohms.

questions.stem: In right triangle RST, the sum of the measures of angle R and angle S is 90 degrees. The value of \(\sin(R)\) is \(\frac{3\sqrt{17}}{13}\). What is the value of \(\cos(S)\)?
questions.whyCorrect: R and S add to 90 degrees, so they are complementary, and for complementary angles the sine of one equals the cosine of the other: \(\cos(S) = \cos(90^{\circ} - R) = \sin(R)\). The value carries straight over as \(\frac{3\sqrt{17}}{13}\). There is nothing to simplify or rationalize — the awkward-looking radical is a decoy.

whyWrong.A: This is \(\frac{1}{\tan R}\). It comes from finding the third side (\(\cos R = \frac{4}{13}\)) and then building a ratio of the two legs instead of using the complementary relationship.
whyWrong.C: This is \(\frac{1}{\sin R}\), the reciprocal. Taking a reciprocal converts sine to cosecant, not to cosine.
whyWrong.D: This is \(\tan R\), from dividing \(\sin R\) by \(\cos R = \frac{4}{13}\). The question asks for a cosine, not a tangent.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by \[ f(x) = (x-5)(x-8)(x+k), \] where k is a constant. In the xy-plane, the graph of \( y = f(x) \) passes through the point \( (-2, 0) \) . What is the value of \( f(0) \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Passing through \( (-2, 0) \) means \( f(-2) = 0 \) . The first two factors give \( (-7)(-10) = 70 \) , which is not zero, so the third factor must vanish: \( -2 + k = 0 \) , so k = 2. Now evaluate at x = 0: \( (-5)(-8)(2) = 80 \) .

whyWrong.A: This evaluates the function at x = −2 rather than x = 0, and with the wrong value of k. The point \( (-2,0) \) is what determines k; it is not where the question asks you to evaluate.
whyWrong.B: This is the x-coordinate of the given point, not a function value.
whyWrong.C: This is 5 + 8 − 2, combining the numbers in the factors instead of multiplying \( f(0) \) out.

questions.stem: A machine fills bags with approximately 29 ounces of walnuts. To test the accuracy of the filling process, 169 bags of walnuts were selected at random and weighed. Based on the sample, it is estimated that the average weight of all bags of walnuts filled by the machine in an 8-hour period is 28.88 ounces, with an associated margin of error of 0.13 ounce. Which of the following is the best interpretation of this estimate?

choices.label: A
choices.content: Plausible values for the average weight of all bags of walnuts filled by the machine are between 28.75 ounces and 29.01 ounces.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Plausible values for the average weight of all bags of walnuts filled by the machine are less than 28.75 ounces or greater than 29.01 ounces.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The average weight of all bags of walnuts filled by the machine is less than 28.99 ounces.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The average weight of all bags of walnuts filled by the machine is greater than 28.99 ounces.

questions.whyCorrect: Take the estimate and step the margin of error off in both directions: 28.88 − 0.13 = 28.75 and 28.88 + 0.13 = 29.01. Those two numbers bracket the plausible values for the true average.

whyWrong.B: This names the values outside the interval, which are the ones the estimate argues against.
whyWrong.C: 28.99 is not an endpoint of anything here, and a margin of error supports a two-sided interval rather than a one-sided claim.
whyWrong.D: Same problem in the other direction, and 28.99 does not come from 28.88 and 0.13 at all.

questions.note: Same template as ma2 Research organizing #2 (cranberries, 9.89 ± 0.14); do not place both in one test.

questions.stem: If \( x = \sqrt[2n]{2x^{n} + 35} \) , where n is a positive integer constant, what is the value of \( x^{n} \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Raise both sides to the power 2n to clear the radical: \( x^{2n} = 2x^{n} + 35 \) . Now notice that \( x^{2n} = (x^{n})^{2} \) , so with \( u = x^{n} \) this is \( u^{2} - 2u - 35 = 0 \) , which factors as (u - 7)(u + 5) = 0. An even root is never negative, so x and therefore \( x^{n} \) cannot be -5; the value is 7.
questions.note: This question is printed twice on the same page of the book, as Advanced Math #3 and #6, word for word. Do not place both in one test.

questions.stem: \[ \sqrt[7]{p^4} = t^{\frac{5}{7}} \]In the given equation, \( p > 1 \) and \( t > 1 \). If \( t = p^{2n-1} \), where \(n\) is a constant, what is the value of \(n\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Rewrite the radical as a power: \( \sqrt[7]{p^4} = p^{\frac{4}{7}} \), so \( p^{\frac{4}{7}} = t^{\frac{5}{7}} \). Raise both sides to the 7th power to clear the sevenths: \( p^4 = t^5 \), so \( t = p^{\frac{4}{5}} \). Since \( p > 1 \), the base is not 0, 1 or \(-1\), so equal powers of \(p\) force equal exponents: \( 2n-1 = \frac{4}{5} \). That gives \( 2n = \frac{9}{5} \) and \( n = \frac{9}{10} = 0.9 \).
questions.note: Book prints the last sentence as two fragments ("If t = p^{2n-1}, where n is a constant. What is the value of n?"); joined into one sentence.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{y + 4}{x - 7} + \frac{y(x - 7)}{x^{2}y - 7xy}\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Factor the second denominator: \(x^{2}y - 7xy = xy(x-7)\), so the second fraction reduces to \(\frac{y(x-7)}{xy(x-7)} = \frac{1}{x}\). Adding over the common denominator \(x(x-7)\) gives \(\frac{x(y+4) + (x-7)}{x(x-7)} = \frac{xy + 5x - 7}{x^{2}-7x}\), which is the printed choice once numerator and denominator are multiplied by \(y\).

whyWrong.A: The numerator is wrong and the denominator \(xy(x-7)^{2}\) comes from multiplying the denominators together without cancelling the shared \((x-7)\).
whyWrong.B: Numerators and denominators were added separately, which is not how fractions add.
whyWrong.D: The numerator is correct but the denominator keeps an extra factor of \((x-7)\) that cancels.

questions.stem: \[ y = ax^2+bx+c \]The function \(f\) is defined above, where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane passes through the points \( (-16,0) \) and \( (9,0) \). If \(a\) is an integer greater than 3, what is the smallest possible value of \( 3b-2a \)?
questions.whyCorrect: The two given points are the x-intercepts, so factored form gives \( y = a(x+16)(x-9) = a(x^2+7x-144) \). Matching coefficients, \( b = 7a \), so \( 3b-2a = 21a-2a = 19a \) — it depends only on \(a\). Since \(a\) is an integer greater than 3, the smallest allowed value is \( a = 4 \), and \( 19(4) = 76 \).
questions.note: Book labels the displayed equation with y but calls the function f in the prose; transcribed as printed.

questions.stem:
xg(x)
−254
−90
156
The table shows three values of x and their corresponding values of g(x), where \(g(x) = \frac{f(x)}{x + 5}\) and f is a linear function. What is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of the graph of y = f(x) in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: Rearrange the definition to f(x) = g(x)(x + 5), which turns each table row into a point on f. At x = −25: f = 4(−20) = −80. At x = −9: f = 0(−4) = 0. At x = 15: f = 6(20) = 120. Those three points are collinear with slope 5 (check: \(\frac{0 - (-80)}{-9 - (-25)} = 5\) and \(\frac{120 - 0}{15 - (-9)} = 5\)), so f(x) = 5(x + 9) = 5x + 45, and the y-intercept is 45.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = ax^2+bx+c \]The function \(f\) is defined above, where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants and \( 4 < b < 7 \). The graph of \( y = f(x) \) is such that \( f(1) = f(5) \). If \(b\) is an integer, what could be the value of \( ab \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Equal outputs at \( x=1 \) and \( x=5 \) put the axis of symmetry halfway between them, at \( x = 3 \). So \( -\frac{b}{2a} = 3 \), which rearranges to \( b = -6a \), i.e. \( a = -\frac{b}{6} \). The integers strictly between 4 and 7 are 5 and 6, and \( ab = -\frac{b^2}{6} \); taking \( b = 6 \) gives \( a = -1 \) and \( ab = -6 \).
questions.note: Nothing in the stem forces a to be an integer, so b = 5 (a = -5/6, ab = -25/6) also satisfies every stated condition. -6 is the intended value; a grader should accept -25/6 as well.

questions.stem: In a set of four consecutive odd integers, where the integers are ordered from least to greatest, the first integer is represented by x. The product of 18 and the fourth odd integer is at most 22 less than the sum of the first and third odd integers. Which inequality represents this situation?
questions.whyCorrect: Consecutive odd integers step by 2, not 1, so the four are x, x + 2, x + 4 and x + 6. The fourth is x + 6 and the first and third are x and x + 4. "At most 22 less than" the sum means the product is no larger than (that sum) - 22, so \( 18(x+6) \le x + (x+4) - 22 \).

whyWrong.B: The expressions are right but the comparison is inverted and the subtraction is reversed: "22 less than S" is S - 22, not 22 - S.
whyWrong.C: This uses x + 4 as the fourth integer and x + 3 as the third, which is the spacing for consecutive integers. Odd integers are 2 apart.
whyWrong.D: Wrong on both counts — the spacing is 1 instead of 2, and the subtraction and inequality direction are both reversed.

questions.stem: The result of increasing a positive quantity by 11% is x. Which expression represents the original quantity in terms of x?
questions.whyCorrect: Call the original quantity q. Increasing it by 11% multiplies it by 1.11, so \(1.11q = x\). Solving for the original quantity means undoing that multiplication: \(q = \frac{x}{1.11}\). Reversing a percent increase is division, not another multiplication.

whyWrong.A: This applies the increase a second time. \(1.11x\) is 11% more than x, but x is already the increased amount.
whyWrong.C: The 100s here treat x as a percentage rather than a quantity, and it multiplies by 1.11 instead of dividing.
whyWrong.D: Same misuse of x as a percent, and the expression shrinks as x grows, which is backwards: a larger result must come from a larger original.

questions.stem: \[ y = ax^2+bx+c \]The equation of a parabola is given, where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. In the xy-plane, the parabola has vertex \( (3,11) \) and \( c < 0 \). Which of the following could be the value of \(b\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The vertex's x-coordinate gives \( -\frac{b}{2a} = 3 \), so \( b = -6a \). The constant \(c\) is the y-intercept, and from vertex form \( y = a(x-3)^2+11 \) that is \( c = 9a+11 \). Requiring \( c < 0 \) gives \( a < -\frac{11}{9} \), and multiplying by \(-6\) flips the inequality: \( b = -6a > \frac{66}{9} = 7\frac{1}{3} \). Only 8 exceeds that.

whyWrong.A: \( b=5 \) gives \( a = -\frac{5}{6} \) and \( c = 9\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right)+11 = 3.5 \), which is positive, so \( c < 0 \) fails.
whyWrong.B: \( b=6 \) gives \( a = -1 \) and \( c = 2 \) — still positive.
whyWrong.C: \( b=7 \) gives \( a = -\frac{7}{6} \) and \( c = 11 - 10.5 = 0.5 \), positive by a hair. This is the trap: \(b\) must exceed \( \frac{22}{3} \approx 7.33 \), not just 7.

questions.stem: If 5(x + 4) = 4(x + 4) + 39, what is the value of x + 4?
questions.whyCorrect: Treat \(x + 4\) as one unknown \(u\): \(5u = 4u + 39\), so \(u = 39\). There is no need to expand or to find \(x\).

whyWrong.A: \(-4\) makes \(x + 4\) zero, which turns the equation into \(0 = 39\).
whyWrong.B: This is \(39 - 4\), the value of \(x\), not of \(x + 4\).
whyWrong.D: This is \(39 + 4\); you added the 4 a second time after already treating \(x+4\) as the unknown.

questions.stem: Rectangle \(ABCD\) is similar to rectangle \(EFGH\). The area of rectangle \(ABCD\) is 648 square inches, and the area of rectangle \(EFGH\) is 72 square inches. The length of the longest side of rectangle \(ABCD\) is 36 inches. What is the length, in inches, of the longest side of rectangle \(EFGH\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The areas are in the ratio \(\frac{648}{72} = 9\), and for similar figures the area ratio is the square of the length ratio. So lengths are in the ratio \(\sqrt{9} = 3\), and the longest side of EFGH is 36 ÷ 3 = 12 inches.

whyWrong.A: 4 is 36 ÷ 9, dividing by the area ratio instead of its square root.
whyWrong.B: 9 is the ratio of the areas, not a length.
whyWrong.D: 36 is ABCD's side. EFGH is the smaller rectangle, so its longest side must be shorter.

questions.stem:
The table shows the yearly snowfall in centimeters (cm) in Toronto for 9 years.
YearSnowfall (cm)
2002114.9
2003129.6
2004134.9
2005162.6
200632.4
2007114.1
2008216.5
200989.0
201045.6
What was the median snowfall, in cm, in Toronto for these years?
questions.whyCorrect: The median is the middle value once the data are put in order, and the table is ordered by year, not by size — that is the step most students skip. Sorted, the snowfalls are 32.4, 45.6, 89.0, 114.1, 114.9, 129.6, 134.9, 162.6, 216.5. With 9 values the middle one is the 5th, which is 114.9.

whyWrong.A: 32.4 is the smallest value, not the middle one.
whyWrong.C: 115.5 is the mean (1,039.6 ÷ 9 = 115.51), not the median. The two are close here, which is exactly why the mean is offered.
whyWrong.D: 184.1 is the range, 216.5 − 32.4.

questions.stem: Which of the following expressions has a factor of \(x+2b\), where \(b\) is a positive integer constant?
questions.whyCorrect: If \(x+2b\) is a factor, the other factor must be \(3x+c\) so the leading term is \(3x^2\). Expanding, \((x+2b)(3x+c)=3x^2+(c+6b)x+2bc\). Matching the constant \(2bc=14b\) forces \(c=7\), so the middle coefficient must be \(7+6b\). Only 25 fits a positive integer: \(b=3\), and \((x+6)(3x+7)=3x^2+25x+42\).

whyWrong.A: \(7+6b=7\) needs \(b=0\), and the stem says \(b\) is positive.
whyWrong.B: \(7+6b=16\) gives \(b=1.5\), not an integer.
whyWrong.C: \(7+6b=18\) gives \(b=\frac{11}{6}\), not an integer.

questions.stem:
4x − 16y = 8

One of the two equations in a system of linear equations is given. The system has no solution. Which equation could be the second equation in this system?
questions.whyCorrect: No solution means parallel but distinct lines: the same left side up to a scale factor, but a constant that does not scale the same way. Divide the given equation by 4 to get x − 4y = 2. Choice C doubles to x − 4y = 0 — identical left side, different constant — so the lines are parallel and never meet.

whyWrong.A: Doubling nothing helps here: x − 8y = 0 has slope \(\frac{1}{8}\) while the given line has slope \(\frac{1}{4}\). Different slopes means the lines cross, so the system has exactly one solution.
whyWrong.B: This is the trap. Doubling it gives x − 4y = 2, which is the given equation itself — the same line, so infinitely many solutions, not none.
whyWrong.D: This is the given equation divided by 4, so again it is the same line and the system has infinitely many solutions.

questions.stem: Quadrilaterals \(PQRS\) and \(WXYZ\) are similar, where \(P\), \(Q\), and \(R\) correspond to \(W\), \(X\), and \(Y\), respectively. The measure of \(\angle S\) is 105°, \(PS = 25\), and \(WZ = 5\). What is the measure of \(\angle Z\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Similar figures have equal corresponding angles; only the side lengths scale. Three correspondences are given, so the fourth vertices must match too: \(S\) corresponds to \(Z\). Therefore \(\angle Z = \angle S = 105^\circ\). The lengths 25 and 5 are there to tempt you into scaling the angle, which similarity never does.

whyWrong.A: 5 is the length \(WZ\), not an angle measure.
whyWrong.B: 21° is 105 ÷ 5, applying the side ratio to the angle. Angles are unchanged by a dilation, so they are never divided by the scale factor.
whyWrong.C: 75° is the supplement of 105°. Corresponding angles in similar figures are equal, not supplementary.

questions.stem: There is a proportional relationship between \(p\) and \(t\). If \(p = 2{,}340\) when \(t = 3{,}120\), then what is the value of \(p\) when \(t = 2{,}496\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Proportional means \(p = kt\) for one fixed constant \(k\). Find it from the given pair: \(k = \frac{2340}{3120} = 0.75\). Then \(p = 0.75(2{,}496) = 1{,}872\).

whyWrong.A: This is \(\frac{2340}{3120}\) applied in the wrong direction or with a mis-multiplication; 1,716 corresponds to \(k = 0.6875\), not the given ratio.
whyWrong.C: This scales upward, \(2{,}496 \times \frac{3120}{2340}\). Since \(t\) went down from 3,120 to 2,496, \(p\) must go down from 2,340 too.
whyWrong.D: This is \(2{,}496 \times \frac{4}{3}\), again using the reciprocal constant. Check the direction: a smaller \(t\) gives a smaller \(p\).

questions.stem:
\[ \sqrt{x^{2}} = 24 - 5x \]

Which value of x is a solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: For positive x, \( \sqrt{x^{2}} = x \) , so the equation becomes x = 24 − 5x, giving 6x = 24 and x = 4. Check it in the original: \( \sqrt{16} = 4 \) and 24 − 5(4) = 4.

whyWrong.A: At x = 2 the left side is 2 but the right side is 24 − 10 = 14.
whyWrong.C: At x = 19 the right side is 24 − 95 = −71, which a square root can never equal.
whyWrong.D: At x = 30 the right side is 24 − 150 = −126, again negative.

questions.stem: A linear function f gives a company's profit, in dollars, for selling x items. The company's profit is $320 when it sells 6 items, and its profit is $640 when it sells 10 items. Which equation defines f?
questions.whyCorrect: You are given two points, (6, 320) and (10, 640). The slope is \(\frac{640 - 320}{10 - 6} = \frac{320}{4} = 80\). Then use one point in f(x) = 80x + b: 320 = 80(6) + b = 480 + b, so b = −160. That gives f(x) = 80x − 160, and checking the other point, 80(10) − 160 = 640.

whyWrong.A: Neither number here comes from the slope calculation; 180 is roughly 320 divided by something and 640 is copied from the data. Testing x = 6 gives 1,080 − 640 = 440, not 320.
whyWrong.B: This is 640 ÷ 10, assuming the profit is directly proportional to items sold. But 320 ÷ 6 is not 64, so the relationship does not pass through the origin.
whyWrong.C: The slope is right but the constant is wrong. Testing x = 6 gives 480 − 10 = 470, not 320; you need to subtract 160.

questions.stem: The measure of angle C is \(\frac{5\pi}{4}\) radians. What is the value of \(\cos C\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Split the angle: \(\frac{5\pi}{4} = \pi + \frac{\pi}{4}\), so the terminal ray is a quarter-turn past the negative x-axis, in the third quadrant. The reference angle is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\), whose cosine is \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), and cosine is negative in the third quadrant because x-coordinates there are negative. So \(\cos\frac{5\pi}{4} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\).

whyWrong.B: This is the cosine of a third-quadrant angle with reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) (that is, \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\)). The sign is right but the reference angle is wrong.
whyWrong.C: This has the correct reference angle but the wrong sign — it is \(\cos\frac{\pi}{4}\), the first-quadrant value. Landing in the third quadrant makes cosine negative.
whyWrong.D: This is \(\cos\frac{\pi}{6}\): both the reference angle and the sign are wrong.

questions.stem:
Each of 185 animals can be classified as one of three species, as shown in the frequency table.
ClassificationFrequency
species X112
species Y3
species Z70
If one of the animals is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting an animal of species Y?
questions.whyCorrect: Probability is the count you want over the total count. Species Y has 3 animals and the total is 185, so the probability is \( \frac{3}{185} \).

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{70}{185} \) is the probability of species Z.
whyWrong.C: \( \frac{182}{185} \) is the probability of NOT selecting species Y, since 185 - 3 = 182.
whyWrong.D: \( \frac{112}{185} \) is the probability of species X.

questions.stem: A model estimates that a gray whale travels 72 to 77 miles each day during its migration. Based on this model, which inequality represents the estimated total number of miles, x, a gray whale could travel in 14 days of its migration?
questions.whyCorrect: Total distance is the daily rate times the number of days. The slowest total is 72 x 14 and the fastest is 77 x 14, so x lies between those two products.

whyWrong.B: Adding days to miles per day is not a valid operation and produces a total of about 86 to 91 miles for two weeks of travel.
whyWrong.C: This makes x the daily rate and constrains 14 days of travel to 72-77 miles in total.
whyWrong.D: Adding 14 to x bounds x between 58 and 63, which is less than one day of travel.

questions.note: Near-identical template to satmath-ma2-linear-inequalities-4 (73-78 miles, 31 days); do not place both in one test.

questions.stem:
\[ x^2-15x+12=0 \]
What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: For \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) the sum of the solutions is \(-\frac{b}{a}\). Here that is \(-\frac{-15}{1}=15\). You do not need the roots themselves, which are irrational.

whyWrong.B: 12 is \(\frac{c}{a}\), the product of the solutions, not their sum.
whyWrong.C: 3 is \(15-12\), combining the two constants for no reason.
whyWrong.D: 0 would be the sum only if the \(x\) term were missing, as in \(x^2+12=0\).

questions.stem: The function f is defined by \[ f(x) = a\sqrt{b - x}, \]where a and b are constants. In the xy-plane, the graph of y = f(x) passes through the point (22, 0), and \( f(-22) < 0 \) . Which of the following must be true?
questions.whyCorrect: Use the two facts in order. f(22) = 0 means \( a\sqrt{b - 22} = 0 \) ; a cannot be 0, because then f would be 0 everywhere and could not be negative at -22, so the radical must vanish and b = 22. Now \( f(-22) = a\sqrt{44} \) , and \( \sqrt{44} \) is positive, so for the product to be negative a must be negative.

whyWrong.B: b = 22 exactly, from the zero at x = 22. It is positive.
whyWrong.C: \( f(0) = a\sqrt{22} \) . Nothing pins down the size of a — only its sign — so this value is not determined. It also confuses the input -22 with an output.
whyWrong.D: f(0) is negative, since a is negative and the radical is positive, so it cannot be 22.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{20\pi^{2}}{\pi^{2} - x^{2}} - \frac{20\pi}{x + \pi}\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Factor the first denominator as a difference of squares: \(\pi^{2} - x^{2} = (\pi - x)(\pi + x)\). The second fraction already has \((x+\pi)\), so multiply it by \(\frac{\pi - x}{\pi - x}\): \(\frac{20\pi(\pi - x)}{\pi^{2}-x^{2}} = \frac{20\pi^{2} - 20\pi x}{\pi^{2}-x^{2}}\). Subtracting, the \(20\pi^{2}\) terms cancel and \(\frac{20\pi x}{\pi^{2}-x^{2}}\) is left.

whyWrong.A: This cancels \(\pi\) from numerator and denominator of the first fraction before the subtraction; you cannot cancel across a sum.
whyWrong.C: This subtracts the numerators without first giving the second fraction the missing factor \((\pi - x)\).
whyWrong.D: The denominator here is not a correct factorisation of anything in the problem — \(\pi^{2}-x^{2}\) factors into \((\pi-x)(\pi+x)\).

questions.stem:
\[ 2x^2-12x-13=0 \]
One solution to the given equation can be written as \(h-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{k}\), where \(h\) and \(k\) are integer constants. What is the value of \(h+k\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: By the quadratic formula, \(x=\frac{12\pm\sqrt{144+104}}{4}=\frac{12\pm\sqrt{248}}{4}\). Simplify the radical before matching the form: \(\sqrt{248}=2\sqrt{62}\), so \(x=3\pm\frac{\sqrt{62}}{2}=3\pm\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{62}\). That gives \(h=3\), \(k=62\), and \(h+k=65\).

whyWrong.A: 13 is the constant term of the equation; \(k\) is the simplified radicand, not \(c\).
whyWrong.B: With \(h=3\) this needs \(k=11\), and \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{11}\approx 1.66\), while the actual offset from 3 is \(\approx 3.94\).
whyWrong.C: 31 is \(\frac{248}{8}\) — the radicand halved once too often. Pulling \(\sqrt{4}\) out of \(\sqrt{248}\) divides the radicand by 4, giving 62.

questions.stem: \[ 6(x - 9) = 11(x - 9) \]What value of \( x \) is the solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Both sides are a multiple of the same quantity \( x - 9 \). Subtracting gives \( 5(x - 9) = 0 \), and since 5 is not zero, \( x - 9 = 0 \), so x = 9. Expanding works too but takes longer: 6x − 54 = 11x − 99 gives 45 = 5x.

questions.stem: \[ f(t) = 7{,}000(0.67)^{t} \] The given function \(f\) models the number of catalogs a company sent to their customers at the end of each year, where \(t\) represents the number of years since the end of 1995, and \(0 \le t \le 5\). If \(y = f(t)\) is graphed in the ty-plane, which of the following is the best interpretation of the y-intercept of the graph in this context?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The minimum estimated number of catalogs the company sent to their customers during the 5 years is 1,411

choices.label: B
choices.content: The minimum estimated number of catalogs the company sent to their customers during the 5 years was 7,000

choices.label: C
choices.content: The estimated number of catalogs the company sent to their customers at the end of 1995 was 1,411

choices.label: D
choices.content: The estimated number of catalogs the company sent to their customers at the end of 1995 was 7,000

questions.whyCorrect: The y-intercept is the value at \(t = 0\), and \(t\) counts years since the end of 1995, so it describes the end of 1995 itself. \(f(0) = 7{,}000(0.67)^{0} = 7{,}000\) catalogs.

whyWrong.A: Wrong on both counts: the intercept is a starting value, and since the base 0.67 is less than 1 the function is decreasing, so the starting value is the maximum over the interval, not the minimum.
whyWrong.B: 7,000 is the right number but it is where the model starts and is the largest value in the interval; the minimum is at \(t = 5\).
whyWrong.C: 1,411 is roughly \(f(4)\), not the intercept. At \(t = 0\) the power equals 1 and the value is 7,000.

questions.stem: During hibernation, American black bears do not eat or replenish calories. A certain black bear weighed 389 pounds when entering hibernation and lost weight at a rate of 0.9 pound per day. At this rate, how many days after entering hibernation did the black bear weigh 380 pounds?
questions.whyCorrect: Work with the weight lost rather than the weights themselves. The bear needs to drop 389 − 380 = 9 pounds, and it loses 0.9 pound each day, so the number of days is \(\frac{9}{0.9} = 10\). (As an equation: 389 − 0.9d = 380.)

questions.stem: \[ (x + 16)(-x + 12)(x + 7)(x + 13) = 0 \]What is the positive solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Set each factor to zero. Three of them start with +x and give the negatives -16, -7 and -13. The second factor is -x + 12, and -x + 12 = 0 gives x = 12 — the leading minus sign means this root is positive, not -12. So the only positive solution is 12.

questions.stem:
\[ y < 42 - 7x \]
\[ \frac{y}{7} > 10 \]Which inequality represents the x values for all solutions \( (x, y) \) that satisfy the given system of inequalities in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: Clear the fraction in the second inequality first: \( \frac{y}{7} > 10 \) means y > 70. Chaining that with the first gives \( 70 < y < 42 - 7x \) , so \( 70 < 42 - 7x \) . Subtract 42 to get \( 28 < -7x \) , then divide by −7 and flip the sign: \( x < -4 \) .

whyWrong.A: This has the sign backwards and uses the wrong bound. Dividing by the negative −7 flips the inequality, which is the step this question is built around.
whyWrong.B: This is what you get from \( 42 - 7x > 0 \) , using 0 as the lower bound on y instead of 70.
whyWrong.C: Right boundary value, wrong direction — the sign flip on dividing by −7 was missed.

questions.stem:
The frequency table summarizes the mass, in grams, of 35 objects.
Mass (grams)Frequency
1012
206
308
409
What is the mean mass, in grams, of these objects?
questions.whyCorrect: Each row stands for several objects, so weight each mass by its frequency instead of averaging the four masses. The total mass is 10(12) + 20(6) + 30(8) + 40(9) = 120 + 120 + 240 + 360 = 840 grams, spread over 12 + 6 + 8 + 9 = 35 objects. That gives 840 ÷ 35 = 24 grams. Averaging 10, 20, 30, 40 instead would give 25, which ignores that the 10-gram objects are the most numerous.

questions.stem:
y = 4x + 12
\(y=(x+2)^2\)

A solution to the given system of equations is \((x,y)\). What is the value of \(x^2\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Set the two expressions for \(y\) equal: \((x+2)^2=4x+12\). Expanding gives \(x^2+4x+4=4x+12\); the \(4x\) terms cancel, leaving \(x^2=8\). The question asks for \(x^2\), so you can stop there rather than taking a square root.

questions.stem: A rectangular banner has an area of 2,500 square inches. A copy of the banner is made in which the length and width of the original banner are each increased by 40%. What is the area of the copy, in square inches?
questions.whyCorrect: Each dimension is multiplied by 1.40, and area is length times width, so the area is multiplied by \(1.40 \times 1.40 = 1.96\). That gives 2,500 × 1.96 = 4,900 square inches. The key point is that a percent increase applied to both dimensions scales the area by the square of the factor, not by the factor itself.

whyWrong.A: This adds 40 to the area once instead of scaling both dimensions by 40%.
whyWrong.B: This adds 40 twice (once per dimension). Percent increases multiply; they are not amounts you add to the area.
whyWrong.C: This is 2,500 × 1.40, which increases the area by 40% — but it is the length and the width that each grow by 40%, so the factor is applied twice.

questions.stem: The ratio 5 to \(x\) is equivalent to the ratio \(y\) to 8. Which equation represents \(x\) in terms of \(y\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Write the ratios as fractions in the order given: \(\frac{5}{x} = \frac{y}{8}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(xy = 40\), so \(x = \frac{40}{y}\). Because \(x\) and \(y\) sit on opposite sides of their fractions, they vary inversely — a bigger \(y\) forces a smaller \(x\).

whyWrong.A: This treats \(x\) and \(y\) as directly proportional, which would follow from \(\frac{5}{x} = \frac{8}{y}\) — the wrong pairing.
whyWrong.B: Also a direct relationship, with the 5 and 8 swapped as well.
whyWrong.C: This has the product 40 in the wrong place; it gives \(xy\) growing with \(y^2\) instead of staying at 40. Test \(y = 5\): the ratio \(5 : x\) must equal \(5 : 8\), so \(x = 8\), which only choice D produces.

questions.stem:
3x + 5y = 21
y = 3

What is the solution (x, y) to the given system of equations?
questions.whyCorrect: The second equation fixes y = 3, so the solution must have 3 as its second coordinate — that alone rules out two choices. Substitute: 3x + 5(3) = 21, so 3x + 15 = 21, 3x = 6 and x = 2. The solution is (2, 3).

whyWrong.A: Here 3 is in the x slot, but the given equation says y = 3, not x = 3. This also comes from dividing 21 by 3 and calling the result y.
whyWrong.B: Same misplacement of the 3, with y found by substituting x = 3 into 3x + 5y = 21. The system tells you y directly; you never need to solve for it.
whyWrong.C: The y-coordinate is right but x is wrong: this treats the equation as 5x + 3y = 21 or divides 8 by 5 somewhere. Substituting x = \(\frac{8}{5}\) gives \(\frac{24}{5} + 15\), not 21.

questions.stem: \[ \sqrt{a^{2}b^{6}} \]If a and b are positive numbers, which of the following is equivalent to the expression above?
questions.whyCorrect: A square root halves each exponent: \( \sqrt{a^{2}} = a \) and \( \sqrt{b^{6}} = b^{3} \) . Since both letters stand for positive numbers there are no absolute-value complications, so the answer is \( ab^{3} \) .

whyWrong.A: The exponent on b should be halved (6 to 3), not reduced by 2.
whyWrong.C: Something has been left under the radical that did not need to be — both exponents are even, so the root comes out completely.
whyWrong.D: Same problem: \( b^{6} \) is a perfect square, so no \( b \) stays inside the radical.

questions.stem: The perimeter of an obtuse triangle is 27 meters. The lengths of two sides of this triangle are 5 meters and 9 meters. What is the length, in meters, of the third side of this triangle?
questions.whyCorrect: The perimeter is the sum of all three sides, so the third side is 27 - 5 - 9 = 13. The word 'obtuse' is a consistency check rather than an extra condition: 5 + 9 = 14 > 13, so a triangle exists, and \(13^{2} = 169\) is larger than \(5^{2}+9^{2} = 106\), so the angle across from the 13 is indeed obtuse.

whyWrong.B: This is 5 + 9, the sum of the two given sides. That value would make the three sides 5, 9 and 14, which lie flat in a line rather than forming a triangle.
whyWrong.C: This subtracts only the 9 from the perimeter and forgets the side of length 5.
whyWrong.D: This subtracts only the 5 from the perimeter and forgets the side of length 9.

questions.stem: For a survey, a sample of 996 people was selected at random from all registered voters in a county. Based on the survey, it is estimated that 42% of all registered voters in the county are in favor of a new law, with an associated margin of error of 3.07%. Which of the following best describes the plausible values for the percent of all registered voters in the county who are in favor of the new law?

choices.label: A
choices.content: Any value greater than 38.93% and less than 45.07%

choices.label: C
choices.content: Any value less than 38.92% or greater than 45.07%

questions.whyCorrect: A margin of error defines an interval on both sides of the estimate: \(42\% \pm 3.07\%\). Subtracting gives 38.93% and adding gives 45.07%, so the plausible values run from 38.93% to 45.07%. The estimate has to be bounded above and below.

whyWrong.B: This drops the upper bound, so it would call 90% plausible.
whyWrong.C: This is the region outside the interval — exactly the values the margin of error rules out.
whyWrong.D: This drops the lower bound, so it would call 2% plausible.

questions.stem: What is the slope of the graph of \[ 8x - 4y = -12 \]in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: Solve for y so the slope is the coefficient of x: \(-4y = -8x - 12\), then divide every term by -4 to get y = 2x + 3. Both signs flip when you divide by a negative, which is exactly the step that produces the wrong sign if you rush it.

whyWrong.A: You divided by -4 on the left but not the right, or dropped one of the two sign changes. The negatives cancel here.
whyWrong.B: This mixes up the coefficients, dividing 8 by -12 rather than solving for y.
whyWrong.C: Same coefficient mix-up, with the sign corrected. The slope comes from y = mx + b, not from a ratio of the two constants.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = 6{,}000(0.70)^{x} \] A conservation scientist implemented a program to reduce a certain invasive insect population in an area. The given function estimates this insect species' population \(x\) years after 2008, where \(x \le 8\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of 6,000 in this context?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The estimated percent decrease in the insect population for this species and area every 8 years after 2008

choices.label: B
choices.content: The estimated percent decrease in the insect population for this species and area each year after 2008

choices.label: C
choices.content: The estimated insect population for this species and area 8 years after 2008

choices.label: D
choices.content: The estimated initial insect population for this species and area in 2008

questions.whyCorrect: In \(f(x) = a\cdot b^{x}\) the coefficient \(a\) is the value at \(x = 0\), because \(b^{0} = 1\). Here \(x\) counts years after 2008, so \(f(0) = 6{,}000\) is the population in 2008 itself.

whyWrong.A: The percent change is carried by the base 0.70, not by the coefficient; and 6,000 is a count of insects, not a percent.
whyWrong.B: Same confusion: the annual change is the 30% drop implied by the base 0.70.
whyWrong.C: The population 8 years later is \(f(8) = 6{,}000(0.70)^{8} \approx 346\), far below 6,000.

questions.stem: The circle K has a radius of 2 millimeters (mm). Circle L has an area of \(144\pi\) mm<sup>2</sup>. What is the total area, in mm<sup>2</sup>, of circle K and L?
questions.whyCorrect: Circle K's area is \(\pi r^{2} = \pi(2)^{2} = 4\pi\). Circle L's area is already given as \(144\pi\), so you never need its radius. Adding the two areas gives \(4\pi + 144\pi = 148\pi\).

whyWrong.A: This adds the radii: circle L has radius 12, and 12 + 2 = 14. Radii do not add to give an area.
whyWrong.B: This adds the two circumferences, \(4\pi + 24\pi\), instead of the areas.
whyWrong.C: This is twice that circumference sum. Neither quantity is an area.

questions.stem: A plant nursery classifies a perennial species as tall if its typical height when fully grown is more than 100 centimeters. Each of the following inequalities represents the possible heights h, in centimeters, for a specific perennial species when fully grown. Which inequality represents the possible heights h, in centimeters, of a tall perennial flower species?
questions.whyCorrect: For the species to count as tall, every height the inequality allows must exceed 100 cm. That means the lower bound itself has to be at least 100. Only the range starting at 107 clears it.

whyWrong.B: The upper bound is 100, so no height in this range is more than 100.
whyWrong.C: Every value here is below 95, well short of the 100 cm threshold.
whyWrong.D: Every value here is below 91, so this species is never tall.

questions.stem: Each side of square \(A\) has a length of 24 inches. Each side of square \(A\) is multiplied by a scale factor of 2 to create square \(B\). What is the length, in inches, of each side of square \(B\)?
questions.whyCorrect: A scale factor multiplies the side length: 24 × 2 = 48 inches. A scale factor is never added or subtracted.

whyWrong.A: 22 is \(24-2\); you subtracted the scale factor instead of multiplying by it.
whyWrong.B: 24 is the original side length, unchanged. The square was scaled, so it cannot stay the same.
whyWrong.C: 26 is \(24+2\); you added the scale factor instead of multiplying by it.

questions.stem:
\[ x^2-2=23 \]
Which value is a solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Add 2 to both sides: \(x^2=25\), so \(x=\pm 5\). Only 5 is listed.

whyWrong.A: \(-23\) is the right side with a sign flipped; the square root of 25 is still needed.
whyWrong.B: \(-21\) is \(2-23\), subtracting in the wrong direction and skipping the square root.
whyWrong.C: \(-2\) is a constant lifted from the equation, not a solution: \((-2)^2-2=2\), not 23.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = \sqrt[3]{x^3+ax^2+bx+c} \]The function \(f\) is defined by the given equation, where \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) are integers. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) passes through the point \( (9,0) \), and \( f(0) = 27 \). What is the value of \( 9a+b \)?
questions.whyCorrect: A cube root is 0 only when its radicand is 0, so \( f(9)=0 \) gives \( 729 + 81a + 9b + c = 0 \). The other condition is easier: \( f(0) = \sqrt[3]{c} = 27 \), so \( c = 27^3 = 19{,}683 \). Substituting, \( 81a + 9b = -729 - 19{,}683 = -20{,}412 \). The question asks for \( 9a+b \), which is that expression divided by 9: \( -20{,}412 \div 9 = -2{,}268 \).

questions.stem: A quadratic function models the height, in feet, of an object above the ground in terms of the time, in seconds, after the object was launched. According to the model, the object was launched from a height of 0 feet and reached its maximum height of 1,600 feet 10 seconds after it was launched. Based on the model, what was the height, in feet, of the object 7 seconds after it was launched?
questions.whyCorrect: The maximum tells you the vertex, so write the model in vertex form: \( h(t) = a(t - 10)^{2} + 1600 \) . Launch height gives h(0) = 0, so \( 100a + 1600 = 0 \) and a = -16. Then \( h(7) = -16(7 - 10)^{2} + 1600 = -16(9) + 1600 = 1456 \) . A shortcut: 7 seconds is 3 before the peak, and by symmetry it has the same height as t = 13.

questions.stem: \[\frac{49}{p} = \frac{49}{q} - \frac{49}{r} - \frac{49}{s}\]The given equation relates the positive variables \(p\), \(q\), \(r\), and \(s\). Which of the following is equivalent to \(q\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Divide the whole equation by 49: \(\frac{1}{p} = \frac{1}{q} - \frac{1}{r} - \frac{1}{s}\), so \(\frac{1}{q} = \frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{r} + \frac{1}{s} = \frac{rs + ps + pr}{prs}\). Inverting both sides gives \(q = \frac{prs}{pr + ps + rs}\). Reciprocals cannot be added term by term, which is what makes this more than one step.

whyWrong.A: This inverts a sum of reciprocals term by term, which is not valid: \(\frac{1}{q}=\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{r}+\frac{1}{s}\) does not give \(q=p+r+s\).
whyWrong.B: The same invalid inversion, with a stray 49 that actually cancels out of every term.
whyWrong.D: The 49 divides out of the whole equation, so it cannot remain in the denominator of the answer.

questions.stem: A chemical reaction in a closed container produces a gas, and the volume V of gas produced over time t (in minutes) can be modeled by a quadratic function. At t = 5.0 minutes, the volume of gas produced is 40.0 liters, and at t = 15.0 minutes, the volume of gas produced is 160.0 liters. If the reaction starts at t = 0 without gas produced, what will be the volume of gas produced at t = 25.0 minutes?
questions.whyCorrect: "Starts at t = 0 without gas" makes the constant term 0, so \( V(t) = at^{2} + bt \) with only two unknowns. The two data points give 25a + 5b = 40 and 225a + 15b = 160, which solve to \( a = \frac{4}{15} \) and \( b = \frac{20}{3} \) . Then \( V(25) = \frac{4}{15}(625) + \frac{20}{3}(25) = \frac{1000}{3} \approx 333.3 \) liters, which matches choice D.

whyWrong.A: 375 is roughly what you get by fitting a straight line through (5, 40) and scaling, ignoring that the growth is quadratic.
whyWrong.B: 483.6 comes from assuming the volume keeps the 40-liters-per-5-minutes rate seen early on, which underestimates a and overshoots here.
whyWrong.C: 423.3 comes from dropping the linear term and fitting \( V = at^{2} \) through one of the points instead of solving both equations together.

questions.note: The exact value is 1000/3 = 333.33 liters; the printed choice reads 333.5, off by about 0.17. Every other choice is more than 40 liters away, so the intended answer is unambiguous, but the choice value is slightly wrong.

questions.stem: Lines \(h\) and \(k\) are graphed in the xy-plane. The graph of line \(h\) has a slope of \(\frac{5}{3}\) and an x-intercept at (17, 0). Line \(k\) is the result of translating the graph of line \(h\) down 4 units. What is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of the graph of line \(k\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Build h from the point and slope: \(y = \frac{5}{3}(x - 17)\), so at x = 0 its y-intercept is \(-\frac{85}{3}\). Translating down 4 units subtracts 4 from every y-value and leaves the slope alone, so k's intercept is \(-\frac{85}{3} - 4 = -\frac{85}{3} - \frac{12}{3} = -\frac{97}{3}\), about -32.33. A common slip is shifting the x-intercept by 4 instead of the y-values.

questions.stem: The graph of y = f(x) is shown in the xy-plane. If a, b, and c are positive constants, which of the following equations could define the function f?
questions.whyCorrect: Read two features off the graph and match them to the algebra. The parabola opens upward, so the leading coefficient is positive, which rules out the two choices beginning with -a. It crosses the x-axis twice and both crossings are to the left of the origin, so both zeros are negative. In factored form the zeros are the values that make a factor vanish, and (x + b)(x + c) has zeros at -b and -c, negative because b and c are positive.

whyWrong.A: The -a makes the parabola open downward; the graph opens upward.
whyWrong.B: Opens downward, and its zeros b and c would be positive.
whyWrong.D: The upward direction is right, but the zeros b and c are positive, putting both crossings to the right of the origin. The graph has them both on the left.

questions.note: Measured reading of the figure: an upward-opening parabola whose vertex lies below the x-axis and whose two x-intercepts are both to the left of the y-axis; the y-axis is drawn near the right edge with the origin labelled O.
questions.imageAlt: An xy-plane with the origin labelled O and no tick marks, showing an upward-opening parabola.

questions.stem: The shaded region shown represents the solutions to \( rx + ty \ge -77 \) , where r and t are constants. What is the value of \( r + t \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Use the two marked points on the boundary, \( (-7, -10) \) and \( (0, -11) \) . The slope is \( \frac{-11-(-10)}{0-(-7)} = -\frac{1}{7} \) , so the line is \( y = -\frac{1}{7}x - 11 \) . Clear the fraction and put it in the form of the given inequality: multiply by 7 to get \( 7y = -x - 77 \) , then \( x + 7y = -77 \) . So r = 1 and t = 7, and r + t = 8. (The shading above the line confirms the direction is \( \ge \) once t is positive.)

whyWrong.B: This is 7 − 1. Once you have r = 1 and t = 7 the question asks for their sum, and both are positive.
whyWrong.C: This is 1 − 7, which also comes from mixing up which coefficient is which and then subtracting.
whyWrong.D: This is the x-coordinate of the marked point, read straight off the graph. It is a coordinate, not a coefficient.

questions.note: Needs the graph rebuilt: an xy-plane with x from about −11 to 1 and y from about −15 to 1, the solid boundary line through the marked points \( (-7,-10) \) and \( (0,-11) \) (that is, \( y = -\frac{1}{7}x - 11 \) ), both points shown as filled dots, and the region above the line shaded.
questions.imageAlt: An xy-plane with a square unit grid and numbered axes; a solid slanted line is drawn through two marked points and the half-plane on one side of it is shaded.

questions.stem:
A science class studied the feeding behavior of the birds that visited a bird feeder each school day for a period of time. The table summarizes the number of birds the class observed visiting the bird feeder each school day during this period of time.
Number of birdsNumber of days
143
153
164
171
183
199
What is the median number of birds the class observed visiting the bird feeder each school day during this period of time?
questions.whyCorrect: The second column counts days, so there are \(3+3+4+1+3+9 = 23\) days and the median is the 12th value in order. Running totals: 3 days at 14, 6 through 15, 10 through 16, 11 through 17, 14 through 18. The 12th day falls in the 18-bird group, so the median is 18. Taking the middle row of the table (16 or 17) is the trap — the rows are not equally weighted.

questions.stem: If \( p(x) = x^2+kx+4 \) has no real zeros, what is the range of possible values for \(k\)?

choices.label: D
choices.content: No range, \(k\) can be any real number.

questions.whyCorrect: No real zeros means the discriminant is negative: \( k^2 - 4(1)(4) < 0 \), so \( k^2 < 16 \). Taking the square root of both sides of \( k^2 < 16 \) gives \( |k| < 4 \), which is the two-sided range \( -4 < k < 4 \), not a one-sided one. Large \(|k|\) in either direction is what forces the parabola to cross the x-axis.

whyWrong.A: This keeps only the negative half and, worse, has the inequality backwards — \( k < -4 \) makes \( k^2 > 16 \), so there are two real zeros.
whyWrong.C: Same error on the positive side: \( k > 4 \) gives \( k^2 > 16 \), a positive discriminant and two real zeros.
whyWrong.D: The discriminant does depend on \(k\); at \( k = 5 \), for instance, \( p(x) = x^2+5x+4 = (x+1)(x+4) \) has real zeros, so not every \(k\) works.

questions.stem:
\(y = 6x^{2} - 36x + 56\)
y + 3 = 0

How many solutions are there to the given system of equations?
questions.whyCorrect: The second equation is the horizontal line \(y = -3\). Substituting gives \(6x^{2} - 36x + 56 = -3\), so \(6x^{2} - 36x + 59 = 0\). Its discriminant is \(36^{2} - 4(6)(59) = 1296 - 1416 = -120\), which is negative, so there are no real intersections. (The parabola's minimum is \(y = 2\), above the line.)

whyWrong.A: One solution would mean the line is tangent to the parabola — that needs a discriminant of exactly 0, and here it is negative.
whyWrong.B: Two is what you get if you assume a horizontal line always cuts a parabola twice. This line sits below the parabola's minimum value of 2.
whyWrong.C: A parabola and a line can meet at most twice, so three is impossible for any values.

questions.stem: Point Q is the center of the circle. Point A, point B, and point C all lie on the circle. Point D lies on segment AC as shown. Segment BD is perpendicular to segment AC. In the figure shown, AB = 58 and AD = 40. If a point within the figure is selected at random, what is the probability that the point is within the shaded region? (Express your answer as a decimal or fraction, not as a percent.) Round your answer to the nearest thousandth.
questions.whyCorrect: AC passes through the center, so it is a diameter and angle ABC is a right angle. In right triangle ABD, \(BD = \sqrt{58^2 - 40^2} = 42\), and the geometric-mean relation \(AB^2 = AD \cdot AC\) gives \(AC = \frac{3364}{40} = 84.1\), so the radius is 42.05. The circle's area is \(\pi(42.05)^2 \approx 5554.97\) and the triangle's is \(\frac{1}{2}(84.1)(42) = 1766.1\); the shaded part is everything outside the triangle, so the probability is \(\frac{5554.97 - 1766.1}{5554.97} \approx 0.682\).
questions.note: Figure: circle with centre Q; horizontal diameter AC with A at the left and C at the right, B on the upper arc, D on AC with BD perpendicular to AC. Everything inside the circle except triangle ABC is shaded.
questions.imageAlt: Line drawing of a circle with centre Q and a horizontal diameter from A to C; B lies on the upper arc and is joined to A and C, and a segment from B meets the diameter at D. The part of the circle outside triangle A B C is shaded.

questions.stem: While the mass of an object is the same everywhere, the weight of an object is not the same on different planets. An object has a weight of 170.00 pounds on Earth and a weight of 186.32 pounds on Neptune. The object's weight on Jupiter is 252.8% of its weight on Earth. If the object's weight on Neptune is x% of its weight on Jupiter, which of the following is closest to the value of x?
questions.whyCorrect: First turn the percentage into a weight: Jupiter \(= 2.528 \times 170.00 = 429.76\) pounds. Then compare Neptune with Jupiter: \(\frac{186.32}{429.76} \approx 0.4335\), so \(x \approx 43.35\). Because Neptune’s 186.32 pounds is well under Jupiter’s 429.76, the answer has to be below 100 — that alone rules out two choices.

whyWrong.B: This is not \(\frac{186.32}{429.76}\). It comes from comparing Neptune with the number 252.8 as though the percentage were itself a weight in pounds, skipping the conversion to 429.76.
whyWrong.C: Over 100%, which would mean the object weighs more on Neptune than on Jupiter. The given weights say the opposite.
whyWrong.D: 429.76 is Jupiter’s weight in pounds, not a percentage. It is the intermediate value, not the answer.

questions.stem:
\[ f(x) = -3x^2+bx+c \]In the given quadratic function \(b\) and \(c\) are constants. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane is a parabola that has a vertex at the point \( (h,k) \), where \(h\) and \(k\) are constants. If \( f(-4) = f(8) \), and the quadratic function has x-intercepts at \( (r,0) \) and \( (s,0) \), which of the following must be true?
I. \( r+s = 4 \)
II. \( b < 0 \)
III. \( c < k \)
questions.whyCorrect: Equal outputs at \( x=-4 \) and \( x=8 \) put the axis of symmetry at their midpoint, \( h = 2 \). The x-intercepts are symmetric about that axis, so \( \frac{r+s}{2} = 2 \) and \( r+s = 4 \) — statement I holds. From \( -\frac{b}{2(-3)} = 2 \) you get \( b = 12 \), which is positive, so II fails. For III, \( k = f(2) = -12 + 24 + c = c + 12 \), so \( c \) is always 12 less than \(k\) and \( c < k \) always holds.

whyWrong.A: II is false: solving \( -\frac{b}{-6} = 2 \) gives \( b = 12 \). The sign trap is forgetting that the leading coefficient is \(-3\), which flips the sign of \(b\) you need for a positive axis of symmetry.
whyWrong.B: II is false for the reason above, and this choice also drops the true statement I.
whyWrong.D: Everything except II is right; a parabola opening downward does not force \( b < 0 \) — the sign of \(b\) follows from where the vertex sits, and here the vertex is at \( x = 2 > 0 \).

questions.stem: \[\frac{x}{5} + \frac{y}{9} = \frac{47}{45}\]An engineer connects resistors in series, where the resistors in the series have a total resistance of \(\frac{47}{45}\) ohms. In this series, there are x resistors of type A, which each have a resistance of a ohms, and y resistors of type B, which each have a resistance of b ohms. The given equation represents this situation. According to this equation, what is the positive difference between the value of a and the value of b?
questions.whyCorrect: Resistors in series add, so the total is \(xa + yb\). Matching that to the given equation, \(\frac{x}{5}\) is \(x \cdot \frac{1}{5}\) and \(\frac{y}{9}\) is \(y \cdot \frac{1}{9}\), so \(a = \frac{1}{5}\) and \(b = \frac{1}{9}\). Their positive difference is \(\frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{9} = \frac{9-5}{45} = \frac{4}{45}\). The step people miss is that the 5 and 9 are denominators, so a and b are their reciprocals, not the numbers themselves.

whyWrong.A: This is the numerator of the total resistance, which is not a difference of anything.
whyWrong.B: This is only the numerator of the correct difference. \(\frac{1}{5}\) and \(\frac{1}{9}\) are both less than 1, so their difference cannot be 4.
whyWrong.C: This is the total resistance of the whole series, not the gap between the two resistor types.

questions.stem: For two acute angles ∠Q and ∠R, \( \cos Q = \sin R \). The measures, in degrees, of ∠Q and ∠R are x + 21 and 4x + 9, respectively. What is the value of x?
questions.whyCorrect: For acute angles, cosine and sine are equal exactly when the angles are complementary, so the two measures must add to 90. Solve (x + 21) + (4x + 9) = 90: that is 5x + 30 = 90, so x = 12. The angles are then 33° and 57°, which add to 90°.

whyWrong.A: 4 makes the angles 25° and 25°. Equal angles would give sin Q = sin R, not cos Q = sin R.
whyWrong.C: 30 makes the angles 51° and 129°, a sum of 180°. Supplementary is the wrong relationship, and 129° is not acute.
whyWrong.D: 69 makes the angles 90° and 285°, neither of which is acute, so it cannot satisfy the setup at all.
