The data value 13 is removed from data set \(A\) to create data set \(B\), which consists of the remaining 10 data values. Which statement best compares the median of data set \(A\) and the median of data set \(B\)?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The median of data set B is less than the median of data set A.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The median of data set B is greater than the median of data set A.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The median of data set B is equal to the median of data set A.

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is not enough information to compare the medians of the two data sets.

questions.whyCorrect: Written out, data set A is 0, 0, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 13 — eleven values, so the median is the 6th, which is 4. Data set B drops the 13, leaving ten values whose median is the average of the 5th and 6th: \(\frac{4+4}{2} = 4\). Because the two middle values are both 4, removing the top value leaves the median unchanged.

whyWrong.A: Removing the largest value shifts the middle positions left by half a step, but positions 5 and 6 are both 4, so nothing changes.
whyWrong.B: Deleting the maximum can never increase the median.
whyWrong.D: The frequency table lists every value and how often it occurs, so both medians can be computed exactly.

questions.stem: The graph of the polynomial function f in the xy-plane, where \( y = f(x) \), has x-intercepts of (-7, 0) and (9, 0). Which of the following must be true?
questions.whyCorrect: An x-intercept is a point where the output is 0. The point (-7, 0) says the input -7 produces the output 0, which is written \( f(-7) = 0 \). Read the pair as (input, output) and the answer falls out.

whyWrong.A: f(0) is the y-intercept, and nothing in the problem tells you what it is.
whyWrong.B: f(9) is 0, because (9, 0) is an x-intercept, not -7.
whyWrong.D: This mixes the two intercepts, feeding one x-value in and reading the other x-value out.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = 15(b)^{x} \]In the given function, b is a positive constant. For every increase in the value of x by 1, the value of f(x) increases by c%, where 0 < c < 100. Which expression gives the value of c in terms of b?
questions.whyCorrect: Raising x by 1 multiplies f by b, so b is the growth factor. An increase of c% means the new value is the old value times \( 1 + \frac{c}{100} \) . Setting the two equal gives \( b = 1 + \frac{c}{100} \) , so \( c = 100(b - 1) \) . The subtraction is the point: only the part of b above 1 is the increase.

whyWrong.A: This is the growth factor written from c, not c itself, and it also has b and c swapped in that role.
whyWrong.B: Adding 100 to a growth factor near 1 gives about 101, which is not a percentage increase between 0 and 100.
whyWrong.C: This adds 1 instead of subtracting it, so a factor of b = 1 (no change at all) would report a 200% increase.

questions.stem:
\[ g(x) = 12(x-a)(x-b)(x-c) \]where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are distinct constants. When \( a < x < b \), \( g(x) \) will be positive. If \( (p,q) \) is on the graph of \( g(x) \), where \(p\) and \(q\) are constants, and \( q = 45 \), which of the following could be true?
I. \( p < a \)
II. \( b < p < c \)
III. \( p > c \)
questions.whyCorrect: The leading coefficient 12 is positive, so the cubic is negative to the left of its smallest zero and then alternates sign at each zero. The only way \(g\) is positive across all of \( (a,b) \) is for that to be the first gap between zeros, so \( a < b < c \), and \(g\) is positive exactly on \( (a,b) \) and on \( x > c \). Since \( q = 45 \) is positive, \(p\) must lie in one of those regions, and of the three statements only \( p > c \) does.

whyWrong.A: Below the smallest zero a positive-leading cubic is negative, so \( p < a \) cannot produce \( q = 45 \).
whyWrong.C: III works, I does not.
whyWrong.D: Between the second and third zeros the cubic is negative, so II is impossible.

questions.note: Nearly identical to question 65 in the same chapter (same setup, coefficient 6 vs 12 and s = 9 vs q = 45) — a template repeat inside the book.

questions.stem:
\(\frac{x}{7} + 5(y - 14) = 29\)
\(\frac{x}{3} - 5(y - 14) = 41\)

The solution to the given system of equations is \((x, y)\). What is the value of 10x?
questions.whyCorrect: The \(5(y - 14)\) terms are exact opposites, so adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) in one step: \(\frac{x}{7} + \frac{x}{3} = 70\). Combining over 21 gives \(\frac{10x}{21} = 70\), so \(10x = 1470\) — the question asks for \(10x\), so you are done without dividing.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by \[ f(x) = ab^{x} \]where a and b are constants and b is an integer. If f(4) = 5 and f(7) = 135, what is the value of f(9)?
questions.whyCorrect: Divide the two given values instead of solving for a and b separately: \( \frac{f(7)}{f(4)} = b^{3} = \frac{135}{5} = 27 \) , so b = 3. Now you only need to step forward: f(9) is two steps past f(7), so \( f(9) = f(7) \cdot b^{2} = 135 \cdot 9 = 1215 \) . (If you want a, it is \( \frac{5}{81} \) , but you never need it.)
questions.note: The book writes "where a, b, and n are constants, and b and n are integers", but no n appears in the printed function. Trimmed here.

questions.stem:
13(x − n) = 13y + 13n

One of the equations in a system of two linear equations is given, where n is a positive constant. The system has no solution. Which equation could be the second equation in this system?
questions.whyCorrect: Divide both sides by 13 first: x − n = y + n, so x − y = 2n. The choices all carry a factor of 2, so scale it to 2x − 2y = 4n. No solution means matching the left side but not the constant, and because n is positive, 2n and 4n are genuinely different numbers. Choice D is 2x − 2y = 2n, which is the parallel distinct line.

whyWrong.A: This is precisely the given equation rewritten, so the two equations describe one line and the system has infinitely many solutions.
whyWrong.B: The y-term is +2y rather than −2y, which changes the slope from 1 to −1. Lines with different slopes intersect at exactly one point.
whyWrong.C: Again the sign on y is wrong, so the slopes differ and the lines cross. Matching the constant 4n does nothing on its own — parallel lines are created by matching coefficients, not constants.

questions.note: Same item as question 24 in this section with 13 in place of 31 and 2 in place of 3; only one of the two should appear in any test.

questions.stem: \[ r(t) = 55t-2t^2 \]The function \(r\) is defined by the given equation. The function \(s\) is defined by \( s(t) = r(t)+1 \). Which expression represents the maximum value of \( s(t) \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Adding 1 shifts the graph up, so the maximum of \(s\) is 1 more than the maximum of \(r\). The parabola \( r(t) = -2t^2+55t \) opens downward with vertex at \( t = -\frac{55}{2(-2)} = \frac{55}{4} \), and \( r\!\left(\frac{55}{4}\right) = 55\!\left(\frac{55}{4}\right) - 2\!\left(\frac{55}{4}\right)^2 = 2\!\left(\frac{55}{4}\right)^2 \), since \( 55 = 4 \cdot \frac{55}{4} \) makes the first term twice the second. So the maximum of \(s\) is \( 1+2\left(\frac{55}{4}\right)^2 \).

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{55}{2} \) is where \(r\) returns to zero, not the vertex; the vertex is at \( \frac{55}{4} \), half of that.
whyWrong.C: The subtraction has the parabola opening upward with a minimum. Here the leading coefficient is \(-2\), so the vertex value is a maximum and is positive.
whyWrong.D: Both errors at once: the wrong \(t\)-value and a sign that would make the maximum negative.

questions.stem:
\(y = 5(x - 2)^{2}\)
y = 10(x - 2)

A solution to the given system of equations is \((x, y)\). What is the one possible value of \(x + y\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Set \(u = x - 2\), so the system is \(y = 5u^{2}\) and \(y = 10u\). Then \(5u^{2} = 10u\) gives \(u = 0\) or \(u = 2\). The first gives \((2, 0)\), so \(x + y = 2\); the second gives \(x = 4\) and \(y = 20\), so \(x + y = 24\). Only 24 is among the choices.

whyWrong.A: Nothing here is negative: both solutions have \(u \ge 0\), so \(y \ge 0\).
whyWrong.B: 4 is the value of \(x\) at that solution; you still have to add \(y = 20\).
whyWrong.C: 20 is the value of \(y\) alone.

questions.stem: To determine if eating chocolate has an effect on men's standardized test scores, researchers surveyed a random population of 8,000 men. Study participants were identified as regular chocolate eaters or non-chocolate eaters and were given a standardized test. They found that the regular chocolate eaters had higher scores than the non-chocolate eaters. What is the most appropriate conclusion for this study?

choices.label: A
choices.content: Eating chocolate regularly causes higher standardized test scores for men and women.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Eating chocolate regularly causes higher standardized test scores for men but not necessarily for women.

choices.label: C
choices.content: There is an association between eating chocolate and higher standardized test scores for men and women, but it is not necessarily a cause-and-effect relationship.

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is an association between eating chocolate and higher standardized test score for men, but it is not necessarily a cause-and-effect relationship and it does not necessarily exist for women.

questions.whyCorrect: Two limits apply at once. Participants were not randomly assigned to eat chocolate — they were only identified as eaters or non-eaters — so the study shows association, not cause. And the sample was 8,000 men, so it says nothing about women. D is the only choice that respects both.

whyWrong.A: Claims cause and extends it to women; the study supports neither.
whyWrong.B: Still claims cause. Without random assignment, some other difference between chocolate eaters and non-eaters could explain the score gap.
whyWrong.C: Correct on cause but wrong on scope: no women were surveyed, so the association cannot be asserted for them.

questions.stem:
The graph of \( y = g(x) \) is shown, where the function g is defined by

\[ g(x) = f(x + a) + b \]

and a and b are constants. If the function f is defined by \( f(x) = x^{3} \) , what is the value of \( a + b \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: With \( f(x) = x^{3} \) , \( g(x) = (x + a)^{3} + b \) . The graph of \( y = x^{3} \) has its flat centre at the origin, so on the shifted graph that centre sits at \( (-a, b) \) . The picture shows the flattening at (4, −1), so \( -a = 4 \) and \( b = -1 \) , giving a = −4 and \( a + b = -5 \) . The sign flip on a is the whole question: \( x + a \) inside the function moves the graph in the opposite direction.

whyWrong.B: −1 is b by itself, with the horizontal shift left out.
whyWrong.C: 1 comes from reading the shift as (4, −1) but then taking a = −4 with b = +... check the vertical shift: the centre is below the x-axis, so b is negative.
whyWrong.D: 5 reads the centre as (−4, 1), reversing both shifts; \( (x + a)^{3} \) with positive a moves the graph left, not right.

questions.note: The slice records this as free response; the book prints four choices.
questions.imageAlt: Coordinate grid in the xy-plane, x-axis marked from −1 to 5 and y-axis from −5 to 5, showing a single S-shaped cubic curve.

questions.stem: \[(5x^{3} - 2) - (-6x^{3} + 3)\]The given expression is equivalent to \(bx^{3} - 5\), where \(b\) is a constant. What is the value of \(b\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Distribute the minus sign over both terms of the second bracket: \(5x^{3} - 2 + 6x^{3} - 3 = 11x^{3} - 5\). Subtracting \(-6x^{3}\) adds it, which is why the coefficient is 11 and not \(-1\). Matching to \(bx^{3} - 5\) gives \(b = 11\).

questions.stem: A right rectangular prism has a length of 26 centimeters (cm), a width of 16 cm, and a height of 14 cm. What is the surface area, in \(\text{cm}^2\), of the right rectangular prism?
questions.whyCorrect: A box has three distinct face shapes, each appearing twice, so the surface area is 2(lw + lh + wh). Here that is 2(26·16 + 26·14 + 16·14) = 2(416 + 364 + 224) = 2(1,004) = 2,008 square centimeters. Forgetting the factor of 2 gives 1,004; multiplying all three dimensions gives the volume instead.

questions.stem: A business consultant charges $408 for the first hour and $204 for each additional hour of work. Which of the following functions gives the charge C(h), in dollars, for h hours of work, where h is a positive integer?
questions.whyCorrect: Only the first hour costs $408; every hour after that costs $204, so the rate that multiplies h is 204, not 408. Write the total as 408 + 204(h − 1), which expands to 204h + 204. Check it at h = 1: 204(1) + 204 = 408, the correct one-hour charge.

whyWrong.B: This charges $204 for the first hour as well and then adds the full $408 on top. At h = 1 it gives $612 instead of $408.
whyWrong.C: This bills every hour at the first-hour rate of $408. At h = 2 it gives 816 + 204 = $1,020, but the true cost is 408 + 204 = $612.
whyWrong.D: Both numbers are too large: the per-hour rate should be 204 and the constant should be 204. At h = 1 this gives $1,020.

questions.stem:
The table summarizes the distribution of age and assigned group for participants in a study.
0-9 years10-19 years20+ yearsTotal
Group A14192760
Group B2772660
Group C1934760
Total606060180
One of these participants will be selected at random. What is the probability of selecting a participant from group A, given that the participant is at least 10 years of age? (Express your answer as a decimal or fraction, not as a percent.)
questions.whyCorrect: "Given that the participant is at least 10" throws away the 0-9 column entirely, so your denominator is only the 10-19 and 20+ columns: 60 + 60 = 120. Group A contributes 19 + 27 = 46 of those, so the probability is \( \frac{46}{120} = \frac{23}{60} \approx 0.383 \). Using 180 as the denominator is the mistake to avoid — the condition has already ruled out a third of the participants.
questions.note: Grid-in; 23/60 and 46/120 reduce to the same value, and .3833 also fits.

questions.stem:
\[ x(13x+27)+c=5 \]
In the given equation, \(c\) is a constant. A solution to the equation is \(-\frac{27+\sqrt{261}}{26}\). What is the value of \(c\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Put the equation in standard form: \(13x^2+27x+(c-5)=0\). The quadratic formula gives \(x=\frac{-27\pm\sqrt{729-52(c-5)}}{26}\), and the denominator 26 already matches, so the radicands must match: \(729-52c+260=261\). That gives \(52c=728\) and \(c=14\).

whyWrong.B: \(c=9\) makes the radicand \(989-468=521\), not 261.
whyWrong.C: \(c=5\) removes the constant entirely; the radicand becomes 729, whose square root is the whole number 27, so the solutions would not involve a radical at all.
whyWrong.D: \(c=4\) makes the radicand \(989-208=781\).

questions.stem:
\( y \le x + 3 \)
\( y \ge -3x - 7 \)
Which point (x, y) is a solution to the given system of inequalities in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: A point must satisfy both inequalities. For (14, 0): \( 0 \le 14 + 3 = 17 \) holds, and \( 0 \ge -3(14) - 7 = -49 \) holds.

whyWrong.A: (0, -14) passes the first but fails the second: -3(0) - 7 = -7, and -14 is below -7.
whyWrong.B: (0, 14) fails the first: 14 is not less than or equal to 3.
whyWrong.C: (-14, 0) fails the first: -14 + 3 = -11, and 0 is not less than or equal to -11.

questions.note: Same template as satmath-ma2-linear-inequalities-10 and -13; do not place these together in one test.

questions.stem: In right triangle RST, the sum of the measures of angle R and angle S is 90 degrees. The value of \( \sin(R) \) is \( \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{9} \). What is the value of \( \cos(S) \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Angles R and S add to 90 degrees, so they are complementary, and the sine of an angle always equals the cosine of its complement. That means cos(S) = sin(R) with no computation at all, so \( \cos(S) = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{9} \). In the triangle itself, the side opposite R is the side adjacent to S, and both ratios use the same hypotenuse.

whyWrong.B: Changing the denominator from 9 to 7 would require a different hypotenuse; nothing here changes it.
whyWrong.C: \( \frac{7\sqrt{2}}{8} \approx 1.24 \), and no sine or cosine can exceed 1. It borrows the 7 from cos(R) = 7/9 but attaches the wrong radical and denominator.
whyWrong.D: A sine or cosine can never exceed 1, and \( \frac{9\sqrt{2}}{8} \approx 1.59 \), so this can be ruled out on sight.

questions.stem: The result of increasing the quantity \(x\) by 600% is 126. What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Increasing by 600% means adding 6 times the original to the original, so the result is \(x + 6x = 7x\), not \(6x\). From \(7x = 126\) you get \(x = 18\).

whyWrong.B: 21 is \(\frac{126}{6}\). That treats "increased by 600%" as "is 600% of", forgetting that the original quantity is still there.
whyWrong.C: 474 is \(126 \times 6 - 282\)-type arithmetic; more simply, it comes from working backwards with subtraction. Increasing \(x\) must make it bigger, so \(x\) has to be smaller than 126.
whyWrong.D: 756 is \(126 \times 6\); you multiplied when the 126 is already the increased amount.

questions.stem: Which expression is a factor of \( x^{5} + x^{4}y + xy^{8} + y^{9} \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Factor by grouping the four terms in pairs. The first pair gives \( x^{4}(x + y) \) and the second gives \( y^{8}(x + y) \) , so the whole expression is \( (x + y)(x^{4} + y^{8}) \) . That makes \( x^{4} + y^{8} \) a factor.

whyWrong.B: \( x^{4} + y^{9} \) mixes the exponent from one group with the exponent from the other; multiplying it by \( (x + y) \) does not reproduce the original terms.
whyWrong.C: \( x^{5} + y^{8} \) keeps the degree-5 term instead of the \( x^{4} \) pulled out of the first group.
whyWrong.D: \( x^{5} + y^{9} \) is just the first and last terms of the expression, which is not a factor of it.

questions.stem: A circle in the xy-plane has its center at \((-2, -4)\). Line k is tangent to this circle at the point \((-5, -5)\). What is the slope of line k?
questions.whyCorrect: The radius drawn to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line. That radius goes from \((-2,-4)\) to \((-5,-5)\), so its slope is \(\frac{-5-(-4)}{-5-(-2)} = \frac{-1}{-3} = \frac{1}{3}\). The tangent's slope is the negative reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{3}\), which is -3.

whyWrong.B: This only changes the sign of the radius slope. A negative reciprocal has to flip the fraction as well.
whyWrong.C: This is the slope of the radius, not the tangent.
whyWrong.D: This flips the fraction but keeps the sign. Perpendicular slopes must multiply to -1, and \(\frac{1}{3} \times 3 = 1\).

questions.stem:
1, 4, 7, 10, 33

What is the mean of the data shown?
questions.whyCorrect: Add all five values and divide by 5: 1 + 4 + 7 + 10 + 33 = 55, and 55 ÷ 5 = 11. The single large value, 33, pulls the mean above the middle value, which is why the mean here is not the same as the median.

whyWrong.A: 7 is the median — the middle value once the list is ordered — not the mean.
whyWrong.C: 17 is the mean of just the smallest and largest values, (1 + 33) ÷ 2; it ignores the other three numbers.
whyWrong.D: 33 is the largest value, i.e. the maximum, not an average.

questions.stem: A family has money in an account for renting movies online. Each time the family rents a movie, the cost of the rental is withdrawn from the account, and each rental costs the same amount of money. The function f(m) = 30 − 6m gives the amount of money, in dollars, in the account after the family has rented m movies. Which of the following represents the amount of money, in dollars, withdrawn from the account each time the family rents a movie?
questions.whyCorrect: Each extra rental increases m by 1 and drops the balance by 6, so the cost of one rental is the coefficient of m: 6 dollars. The question asks for the amount per rental, which is a fixed number, not something that depends on m.

whyWrong.A: 6m is the total withdrawn after m rentals, not the cost of a single one.
whyWrong.C: 30 is the starting balance, the value when m = 0, before any movie is rented.
whyWrong.D: This is the whole function — the money left in the account, not the money taken out.

questions.stem: \[ y = -\frac{1}{4}x^{2} + x + 28 \] The given equation models a company's active projects over 6 months, where y is the estimated number of active projects x months after the end of April 2012, where 0 ≤ x ≤ 6. Which statement is the best interpretation of the y-intercept of the graph of this equation in the xy-plane?

choices.label: A
choices.content: At the end of April 2012, the estimated number of active projects was 0.

choices.label: B
choices.content: At the end of April 2012, the estimated number of active projects was 28.

choices.label: C
choices.content: At the end of May 2012, the estimated number of active projects was 0.

choices.label: D
choices.content: At the end of May 2012, the estimated number of active projects was 28.

questions.whyCorrect: The y-intercept is the value of y when x = 0, and substituting x = 0 leaves only the constant, 28. The stem defines x as months after the end of April 2012, so x = 0 is the end of April 2012 itself.

whyWrong.A: 0 is the x-value at the intercept, not the y-value. The y-intercept is the point (0, 28).
whyWrong.C: This gets the number right in the wrong direction and the date wrong too: the end of May is x = 1, where the model gives 28.75.
whyWrong.D: 28 is correct but the date is not. The end of May 2012 is one month later, x = 1.

questions.stem: The function k is defined by \[ k(s) = \sqrt{s + 110}. \]If k(53p) = p, where p is a constant, what is the value of p?
questions.whyCorrect: Substitute 53p for s: \( \sqrt{53p + 110} = p \) . Square both sides to get \( p^{2} = 53p + 110 \) , so \( p^{2} - 53p - 110 = 0 \) , which factors as (p - 55)(p + 2) = 0. Squaring can create false roots, so check both: a square root output cannot be negative, so p = -2 fails and p = 55 is the answer.

questions.stem:
16x - 20y = 6y + 8
\(ty = 8x + \frac{1}{5}\)

In the given system of equations, \(t\) is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of \(t\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Tidy the first equation before comparing: \(16x - 26y = 8\), or \(y = \frac{8}{13}x - \frac{4}{13}\). Write the second the same way: \(y = \frac{8}{t}x + \frac{1}{5t}\). No solution means parallel lines, so the slopes match: \(\frac{8}{t} = \frac{8}{13}\), giving \(t = 13\). The intercepts \(\frac{1}{65}\) and \(-\frac{4}{13}\) differ, so the lines really are parallel and distinct.

questions.stem: \[ 0 = (x-k)(7x+t) - (x-k) \]In the given equation, k and t are positive constants. A solution to the equation is \( x = -\frac{22}{7} \) . What is the value of t ?
questions.whyCorrect: Factor out the common \( (x-k) \) instead of expanding: the equation becomes \( (x-k)(7x+t-1) = 0 \) . One solution is x = k, but k is positive and the given solution is negative, so the given solution must come from the other factor: \( 7\left(-\frac{22}{7}\right) + t - 1 = 0 \) , which is \( -22 + t - 1 = 0 \) , so t = 23.

questions.stem:
n(x) = 2(x + 8) + (x − 8)

The function n is defined as shown. For what value of x is n(x) = 35?
questions.whyCorrect: Expand and collect before solving. 2(x + 8) = 2x + 16, so n(x) = 2x + 16 + x − 8 = 3x + 8. Setting 3x + 8 = 35 gives 3x = 27 and x = 9. Check: 2(17) + 1 = 35.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is a quadratic function. In the xy-plane, the graph of \(y = f(x)\) has a vertex at \((1, 7)\) and passes through the points \((2, 53)\) and \((-1, 191)\). What is the value of \(f(-2) - f(0)\)?

whyWrong.A: This is what you get from \(191 - 46\), mixing a given \(y\)-value with the leading coefficient rather than evaluating the function at \(-2\) and 0.
whyWrong.B: This is \(f(-2) - 184\), i.e. subtracting the squared term instead of \(f(0)\). You need the full value \(f(0) = 53\).
whyWrong.D: This is \(f(-2)\) by itself. The question asks for the difference, so you still have to subtract \(f(0) = 53\).

questions.stem: A landscaper will plant two types of shrubs, hydrangeas and winter hazels, in a park. There will be no more than 244 total shrubs planted, and the number of hydrangeas planted will be at most three times the number of winter hazels planted. Which of the following systems of inequalities best represents this situation, where h is the number of hydrangeas that will be planted and w is the number of winter hazels that will be planted?
questions.whyCorrect: "No more than 244 total" caps the sum, so \( h + w \le 244 \). "Hydrangeas at most three times the winter hazels" puts the multiplier on w and the cap on h: \( h \le 3w \). Watch which quantity gets tripled — it is the winter hazels.

whyWrong.B: The total is right, but \( 3h \ge w \) triples the hydrangeas instead of the winter hazels, which is a different condition.
whyWrong.C: The second inequality is right, but \( h + w \ge 244 \) sets a minimum number of shrubs when the stem sets a maximum.
whyWrong.D: Both parts are reversed — a minimum total instead of a maximum, and the wrong variable tripled.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 42(0.24)^x\). For any positive integer n, the value of \(f(n)\) is p% less than the value of \(f(n-1)\). What is the value of p?
questions.whyCorrect: Each step of 1 in x multiplies the value by 0.24, so \(f(n)\) is 24% of \(f(n-1)\) — not 24% less than it. What is left after the drop is 24%, so the drop itself is 100 - 24 = 76%.

whyWrong.B: 58 is not related to either 0.24 or 42 by any percent-change step.
whyWrong.C: 42 is the initial value \(f(0)\), which does not affect the percent change — it cancels in the ratio.
whyWrong.D: 24 is the percentage that remains. The question asks how much is lost.

questions.stem:
The table summarizes the number of objects in each group.

GroupNumber of objects
A325
B68
C572
D102
Total1067

The number of objects in group \(C\) is \(p\%\) of the number of objects in group \(A\). What is the value of \(p\)?
questions.whyCorrect: "\(C\) is \(p\%\) of \(A\)" means \(\frac{C}{A} = \frac{p}{100}\), so divide the group C count by the group A count: \(\frac{572}{325} = 1.76\). Multiply by 100 to express it as a percent: \(p = 176\). Group C is larger than group A, so the percent must exceed 100 — that is the check on which number goes on the bottom. The total 1,067 is not used.

questions.stem:
If
\[ a = 3k + 4r \quad \text{and} \quad b = 9k - 12r + 6, \]which expression is equivalent to \( a - b \)?
questions.whyCorrect: The subtraction sign applies to every term of \( b \), not just the first: \( a - b = 3k + 4r - 9k + 12r - 6 \). Combining like terms gives \( -6k + 16r - 6 \). The place people lose the question is the \( -12r \), which becomes \( +12r \).

whyWrong.B: The \( k \) and \( r \) terms are right, but the constant kept its sign: subtracting \( +6 \) must give \( -6 \).
whyWrong.C: This subtracts only the first term of \( b \) and then adds \( -12r \) unchanged, giving \( 4r - 12r = -8r \), and it also keeps \( +6 \).
whyWrong.D: This distributes the minus sign to the constant but not to the \( -12r \) term, so both the \( r \) coefficient and the reasoning are inconsistent.

questions.stem:
y = −0.5
\(y=x^2+8x+a\)

In the given system of equations, \(a\) is a positive integer constant. The system has no real solutions. What is the least possible value of \(a\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Substituting the line into the parabola gives \(x^2+8x+a=-0.5\), i.e. \(x^2+8x+(a+0.5)=0\). No real solution means a negative discriminant: \(64-4(a+0.5)<0\), so \(62<4a\) and \(a>15.5\). The least integer above 15.5 is 16.

whyWrong.A: \(a=13\) gives a discriminant of \(62-52=10>0\), so the graphs still cross twice.
whyWrong.B: \(a=14\) gives \(62-56=6>0\) — still two intersections.
whyWrong.C: \(a=15\) gives \(62-60=2>0\). It is close, but the parabola's minimum \(-1\) is still below \(-0.5\), so they meet.

questions.stem: A hemisphere is half of a sphere. If a hemisphere has a radius of 70 inches, which of the following is closest to the volume of this hemisphere?
questions.whyCorrect: Take half the sphere's volume: \(\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}\). With \(r = 70\), \(r^{3} = 343{,}000\), so the volume is \(\frac{2}{3}\pi(343{,}000) \approx 718{,}378\) cubic inches, closest to 718,400.

whyWrong.A: About \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^{2}\) — the radius was squared instead of cubed, so this is not even a volume.
whyWrong.B: Four times choice A, still built on \(r^{2}\) rather than \(r^{3}\).
whyWrong.C: About \(\frac{1}{2}\pi r^{3}\): you halved \(\pi r^{3}\) but dropped the \(\frac{4}{3}\) from the sphere formula.

questions.stem: A group of 40 employees selected at random from all the employees at a company were surveyed about the number of books they read last year. From the data collected, it was estimated that the mean number of books employees at the company read last year is 6.8, with an associated margin of error of 1.1. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.content: It is plausible that the actual mean number of books employees at the company read last year is less than 5.7.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It is plausible that the actual mean number of books employees at the company read last year is between 5.7 and 7.9.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It is plausible that every employee at the company read between 6.8 and 10.1 books last year.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It is plausible that the actual mean number of books employees at the company read last year is greater than 7.9.

questions.whyCorrect: The interval runs from 6.8 − 1.1 = 5.7 to 6.8 + 1.1 = 7.9, and it is a statement about the mean for all employees. Watch that last part: the margin of error bounds the average, not the individual readers.

whyWrong.A: 5.7 is the bottom of the plausible interval, so means below it are the ones the estimate makes unlikely.
whyWrong.C: Two errors at once: the interval describes the company-wide mean, not what each employee did, and 6.8 to 10.1 is not the interval the numbers give.
whyWrong.D: 7.9 is the top of the interval, so means above it fall outside the plausible range.

questions.stem: What value of \(n\) is the solution to the equation 9n - 10 = 2n + 25?
questions.whyCorrect: Move the variable terms to one side and the numbers to the other: \(9n - 2n = 25 + 10\), so \(7n = 35\) and \(n = 5\).

whyWrong.B: 7 is the combined coefficient \(9 - 2\), not the solution — you still divide 35 by it.
whyWrong.C: 9 is the leading coefficient from the original equation.
whyWrong.D: This comes from \(9n - 2n = 25 - 10\) mis-signed, or from adding rather than subtracting somewhere; check by substituting: \(9(11) - 10 = 89\) but \(2(11) + 25 = 47\).

questions.stem:
\[ \sqrt{w} + 22 = 28 \]

What is the solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Isolate the radical before undoing it: \( \sqrt{w} = 28 - 22 = 6 \) . Squaring both sides gives w = 36. Check: \( \sqrt{36} + 22 = 6 + 22 = 28 \) .

whyWrong.A: 2 comes from mishandling the arithmetic entirely; \( \sqrt{2} + 22 \) is nowhere near 28.
whyWrong.B: 3 would work only if the equation asked for \( \sqrt{w} = 3 \) ; here the radical equals 6.
whyWrong.C: 12 doubles 6 instead of squaring it.

questions.stem: The measure of angle G is \( \frac{\pi}{10} \) radians. If the measure of angle G is 9n in degrees, where n is a constant, what is the value of n?
questions.whyCorrect: Convert first, then solve. Since \( \pi \) radians is 180°, \( \frac{\pi}{10} \) radians is \( \frac{180}{10} = 18 \) degrees. The same angle is written as 9n degrees, so 9n = 18 and n = 2.

whyWrong.B: 9 is the coefficient already in the expression 9n, not the value of n.
whyWrong.C: 10 is the denominator of the radian measure; it is not what n multiplies out to.
whyWrong.D: 18 is the angle's measure in degrees. n is that measure divided by 9.

questions.stem:
Data set A: 5, 8, 11, 11, 14, 20
Data set B: 5, 8, 11, 11, 14, 20, 41

Two data sets are shown. Which statement best compares the medians of the data sets?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The median of data set A is greater than the median of data set B.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The median of data set A is less than the median of data set B.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The medians of data sets A and B are equal.

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is not enough information to compare the medians.

questions.whyCorrect: Data set A has 6 values, so its median is the average of the 3rd and 4th: (11 + 11) ÷ 2 = 11. Data set B is the same list plus 41, giving 7 values, so its median is the single 4th value, which is also 11. The extra value lands at the far right and moves the middle position only half a step, and both 11s are sitting there, so nothing changes.

whyWrong.A: This would need B's middle value to be smaller, but adding a large value can never pull the median down.
whyWrong.B: A natural guess — 41 is much bigger than everything else — but that affects the mean, not the median. The middle of B is still 11.
whyWrong.D: Both data sets are listed in full, so both medians can be computed exactly.

questions.stem:
y = −2x + 70

Which table gives the values of x and the corresponding values of y for the given equation?

choices.label: A
choices.content:
xy
00
12
24

choices.label: B
choices.content:
xy
00
172
274

choices.label: C
choices.content:
xy
00
172
2144

choices.label: D
choices.content:
xy
070
168
266

questions.whyCorrect: Test x = 0 first, since it is quickest: y = −2(0) + 70 = 70, so the table must start at 70. Only one table does. Confirm with the next rows: at x = 1, y = 68, and at x = 2, y = 66 — the values drop by 2 each time, matching the slope −2.

whyWrong.A: This table starts at y = 0 and climbs by 2. It ignores the +70 entirely and gets the sign of the slope wrong.
whyWrong.B: At x = 0 this gives 0, but the equation gives 70. It also rises by 2 per step instead of falling.
whyWrong.C: The y-values double rather than change by a fixed amount, so the relationship is not even linear, let alone this line.

questions.stem: At the time of posting a video, a social media channel had 88 subscribers. Each day after the video was posted, the number of subscribers doubled from the number of subscribers on the previous day. Which equation gives the total number of subscribers, \(n\), to the channel \(d\) days after the video was posted?
questions.whyCorrect: "Doubled from the previous day" is a constant multiplier of 2 per day, so the model is \(n = 88(2)^{d}\) — starting value 88, growth factor 2, exponent counting days. Substituting \(d = 0\) returns the original 88 subscribers.

whyWrong.A: Putting 88 in the base makes the count explode: \(d = 2\) would give 7,744.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{1}{2}\) as the base halves the audience each day, the opposite of doubling.
whyWrong.D: This grows by exactly one subscriber per day and starts at 7,744, neither of which matches the description.

questions.note: Same question as satmath-ma2-exponential-functions-23 with 88 subscribers instead of 95 - do not place both in one test.

questions.stem: A circle in the xy-plane has its center at \((14, 19)\) and has a radius of 7k. Which equation represents this circle?
questions.whyCorrect: In standard form the number on the right is the radius squared, and squaring a product squares every factor: \((7k)^{2} = 49k^{2}\). Since all four choices share the same left side, the only decision is how to square 7k.

whyWrong.A: This squares only the 7 and leaves k unsquared.
whyWrong.C: This leaves the radius unsquared entirely.
whyWrong.D: This squares only the k and leaves the 7 as it is.

questions.note: Same question as Circles #25 (October 2024) in this book with a different center, (14, 19) instead of (16, 17); the answer choices are otherwise identical.

questions.stem: Cristina was elected to the city council. Each city council person is required to attend at least 21 of the 27 scheduled meetings in a year to keep their position. Which inequality represents the number of city council meetings, x, Cristina must attend in a year to keep her position on the city council?
questions.whyCorrect: She must attend at least 21, so 21 is the lower bound. Only 27 meetings exist, so she cannot attend more than 27, which is the upper bound. Both bounds are needed.

whyWrong.A: This allows attending 0 meetings and forbids attending more than 21 — both backwards.
whyWrong.B: 48 is 21 + 27, a sum with no meaning here, and there are only 27 meetings to attend.
whyWrong.D: This starts at 27, which would require perfect attendance, and again 48 exceeds the number of meetings that exist.

questions.stem: Julia purchased 800 feet of fencing. She used 60% of this fencing to surround a vegetable garden. How many feet of fencing did Julia use to surround a vegetable garden?
questions.whyCorrect: 60% of 800 is 0.60 × 800 = 480 feet. Turn the percent into a decimal and multiply by the total amount.

whyWrong.A: 12 comes from dividing rather than multiplying (800 ÷ 60 ≈ 13); the answer must be a large share of 800.
whyWrong.B: 30 is half of 60. You worked with the percent number itself instead of applying it to 800.
whyWrong.D: 740 is 800 − 60; you subtracted the percent as though it were a number of feet.

questions.stem: \[ x^{2} - x - 12 = 0 \] What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Factoring gives \( (x - 4)(x + 3) = 0 \) , so the solutions are 4 and -3 and their sum is 1. You can skip the factoring: for \( ax^{2} + bx + c = 0 \) the sum of the solutions is \( -\frac{b}{a} = -\frac{-1}{1} = 1 \) .

whyWrong.A: -7 adds -4 and -3, which flips the sign of the solution 4. Check by substituting: -4 does not satisfy the equation.
whyWrong.B: -1 is the coefficient b copied straight out of the equation. The sum is \( -\frac{b}{a} \) , so the sign flips.
whyWrong.D: 7 adds 4 and 3, which flips the sign of the solution -3. Their product would then be 12, not -12.

questions.stem: The polynomial \[ 8x^4+50x^2+63 \]can be factored, and one of the factors is of the form \( (ax^2+b) \). What is one possible value of the product \( a \cdot b \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Treat it as a quadratic in \( x^2 \): with \( u = x^2 \) you are factoring \( 8u^2+50u+63 \). Look for two numbers multiplying to \( 8 \times 63 = 504 \) and adding to 50 — those are 14 and 36. Splitting gives \( 8u^2+14u+36u+63 = 2u(4u+7)+9(4u+7) = (4u+7)(2u+9) \), so the polynomial is \( (4x^2+7)(2x^2+9) \). Taking the first factor, \( a \cdot b = 4 \times 7 = 28 \).
questions.note: The other factor gives a valid answer too: 2 x 9 = 18. Both 28 and 18 should be accepted.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \( f(x) = a^x-b \) where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. In the xy-plane, the graph of \( y = f(x) \) passes through the points \( (c,7) \) and \( (2c,117) \), where \(c\) is a constant. Which of the following could be the value of \(b\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The two points give \( a^c = b+7 \) and \( a^{2c} = b+117 \). The key step is that \( a^{2c} = (a^c)^2 \), so \( (b+7)^2 = b+117 \). Expanding gives \( b^2+13b-68 = 0 \), which factors as \( (b+17)(b-4) = 0 \), so \( b = 4 \) or \( b = -17 \). Of these, only 4 is offered (check: \( a^c = 11 \), \( a^{2c} = 121 = 117+4 \)).

whyWrong.B: 17 is the other root with the sign flipped — the equation gives \( b = -17 \), not \( +17 \).
whyWrong.C: 110 is \( 117-7 \), the difference of the two y-values, which is not what the exponent relationship produces.
whyWrong.D: 124 is \( 117+7 \); adding the outputs ignores that doubling the input squares \( a^c \).

questions.stem:
\(\frac{1}{4}(s + 4t) = 544\)
7s - 8t = 1,192

The solution to the given system of equations is \((s, t)\). What is the value of \(s - t\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Clear the fraction first: multiplying by 4 gives \(s + 4t = 2{,}176\). Doubling that gives \(2s + 8t = 4{,}352\), which adds to the second equation to eliminate \(t\): \(9s = 5{,}544\), so \(s = 616\). Then \(4t = 2{,}176 - 616 = 1{,}560\), so \(t = 390\) and \(s - t = 226\).

questions.stem: The graphs of functions f and g are parabolas, such that g(x) = 6f(x). The vertex of f(x) is at (2, 10). The y-intercepts of f(x) and g(x) are at (0, b) and (0, c), respectively. If the point (3, 78) is on the graph of g(x), what is the value of \( b - c \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Write f in vertex form, \( f(x) = a(x-2)^{2} + 10 \) , so \( g(x) = 6a(x-2)^{2} + 60 \) . Put (3, 78) into g: 6a + 60 = 78, so a = 3. Then \( b = f(0) = 3(4) + 10 = 22 \) and \( c = g(0) = 6b = 132 \) , giving b - c = 22 - 132 = -110. Notice the shortcut: c is always 6b, so \( b - c = -5b \) .

whyWrong.A: -60 is the value of \( -5b \) if you take b = 12, which comes from forgetting the vertex shift and reading f(0) as 3(4) instead of 3(4) + 10.
whyWrong.C: -130 comes from computing c correctly but subtracting the wrong way round or slipping on b = 26.
whyWrong.D: -200 corresponds to b = 40, which follows from using the point (3, 78) on f rather than on g and getting a = 17 or similar.

questions.stem:
5x + 4y = 3
15x + 12y = 9

For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
questions.whyCorrect: The second equation is the first tripled, so both graphs are the same line and any point on it satisfies the system. Notice that the expression \(-\frac{4r}{5} + \frac{3}{5}\) has a 5 underneath, which is the coefficient of x — that means r stands for y here. Set y = r and solve 5x + 4r = 3 to get \(x = -\frac{4r}{5} + \frac{3}{5}\), which is choice C.

whyWrong.A: The correct x-expression is placed in the y slot. Substituting gives \(\frac{9r}{5} + \frac{12}{5}\), which equals 3 at only one value of r, not for every r.
whyWrong.B: This solves for y but flips the sign and inverts the fraction: solving 5r + 4y = 3 gives \(y = -\frac{5r}{4} + \frac{3}{4}\). The printed version substitutes to 10r + 3.
whyWrong.D: The constants 3 and 9 come straight off the right-hand sides of the two equations. Substituting gives \(\frac{r}{3} + 51\), not 3.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \[ f(x) = ax^2+bx+c \]where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are constants. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane passes through the points \( (13,0) \) and \( (-6,0) \). Which of the following is the value of \( a+b \) in terms of \(a\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The two points are the zeros, so the sum of the roots is \( 13+(-6) = 7 \). For \( ax^2+bx+c \) the sum of the roots is \( -\frac{b}{a} \), so \( -\frac{b}{a} = 7 \) and \( b = -7a \). Then \( a+b = a-7a = -6a \).

whyWrong.A: \( 7a \) is what you get from \( b = 7a \) — forgetting the minus sign in \( -\frac{b}{a} \) — and then also dropping the \(a\) you started with.
whyWrong.B: \( 6a \) is \( a + 7a \) with a sign slip, or \( a - (-7a) \); the sum is \( a + (-7a) \).
whyWrong.D: \( -7a \) is \(b\) itself, not \( a+b \).

questions.stem: The graph of line \(g\) is shown in the xy-plane. Line \(k\) is defined by 165x + py = w, where \(p\) and \(w\) are constants. If line \(k\) is graphed in this xy-plane, resulting in the graph of a system of two linear equations, the system of two linear equations will have infinitely many solutions. What is the value of \(p + w\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Infinitely many solutions means line \(k\) is line \(g\), so read \(g\) off the graph and force the coefficients to match. From the two marked points, \(g\) has slope \(\frac{1-12}{0-(-9)} = -\frac{11}{9}\) and \(y\)-intercept 1, so \(g\) is \(y = -\frac{11}{9}x + 1\), i.e. 11x + 9y = 9. Line \(k\) is 165x + py = w, and 165 = 15 × 11, so multiply the whole equation of \(g\) by 15: 165x + 135y = 135. That gives p = 135 and w = 135, so p + w = 270.
questions.note: Depends on a graph. Verified data for rebuilding it: line g passes through the marked points (-9, 12) and (0, 1); grid spans x from -15 to 1 and y from 0 to 15.
questions.imageAlt: Coordinate grid in the xy-plane with the x-axis marked from −14 to −2 and the y-axis marked from 2 to 14, showing a single straight line with two points on it marked by dots.

questions.stem: For the positive quantities h, j, and k, 94% of h is equivalent to 47% of j, and j is equivalent to 30% of k. What percentage of k is h? (Disregard the % sign when entering your answer. For example, if your answer is 39%, enter 39).
questions.whyCorrect: Write each statement as an equation. \(0.94h=0.47j\), and since 0.94 is exactly twice 0.47, this says \(j=2h\). The second statement is \(j=0.30k\). Substituting, \(2h=0.30k\), so \(h=0.15k\) - h is 15% of k. Notice the first relation makes j the larger quantity, which is the step people reverse.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \[ f(x) = 3x^2-5x+10 \]If the function \( f(x-2) \) is written in the form \( ax^2+bx+c \), what is the value of \( a+b+c \)?
questions.whyCorrect: There is a shortcut: \( a+b+c \) is the value of the new quadratic at \( x = 1 \), and the new quadratic at \( x=1 \) is \( f(1-2) = f(-1) \). So \( a+b+c = 3(-1)^2-5(-1)+10 = 3+5+10 = 18 \). Expanding confirms it: \( f(x-2) = 3(x-2)^2-5(x-2)+10 = 3x^2-17x+32 \), and \( 3-17+32 = 18 \).

questions.stem: The graph of line \(h\) is shown in the xy-plane. Line \(k\) (not shown) is defined by sx + 40y = t, where s and t are constants. If line \(k\) is graphed in this xy-plane, the result is a graph of two linear equations. This system of two linear equations has no solution. Which of the following is NOT a possible value of t?
questions.whyCorrect: No solution means line \(k\) is parallel to \(h\) but is not the same line — that second half is what the question turns on. Line \(h\) runs through (-5, 0) and (0, -8), so its slope is \(-\frac{8}{5}\) and h is 8x + 5y = -40. Matching slopes in sx + 40y = t forces \(-\frac{s}{40} = -\frac{8}{5}\), so s = 64, and multiplying h by 8 gives 64x + 40y = -320. That single value of t makes k identical to h (infinitely many solutions), so t = -320 is the one value ruled out.

whyWrong.A: With s = 64, t = 200 gives a line parallel to h and distinct from it, so the system has no solution — exactly what the question allows.
whyWrong.B: 64 is the value of s, not a forbidden t. As a t value it gives a distinct parallel line, which is fine.
whyWrong.C: t = -8 also gives a distinct parallel line. Any t except -320 works.

questions.note: Depends on a graph. Verified data for rebuilding it: line h passes through (-5, 0) and (0, -8), drawn as a segment across roughly -5 <= x <= 0; grid spans x from -13 to 3 and y from -13 to 7.
questions.imageAlt: Coordinate grid in the xy-plane, x-axis marked from −12 to 2 and y-axis from −12 to 6, showing a single straight line segment.

questions.stem: A regular hexagonal prism has a volume of 350 cubic inches and a height of 14 inches. What is the perimeter of each of the hexagonal bases, in inches? Round your answer to the nearest tenth of an inch.
questions.whyCorrect: The base area is \(\frac{350}{14} = 25\) square inches. A regular hexagon of side s has area \(\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}s^2\), so \(s^2 = \frac{50}{3\sqrt{3}} = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{9}\) and \(s = \frac{5\sqrt{2}\,\sqrt[4]{3}}{3}\). The perimeter is \(6s = 10\sqrt{2}\,\sqrt[4]{3} = 10\sqrt[4]{12} \approx 18.6\) inches.

whyWrong.B: \(10\sqrt{3} \approx 17.3\) comes from \(s^2 = \frac{25}{3}\) — dividing the area by 3 but dropping the \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) in the hexagon formula.
whyWrong.C: This treats the base as a square: \(s^2 = 25\) gives \(s = 5\) and a perimeter of 30. A hexagon of area 25 has a shorter side than that.
whyWrong.D: \(25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3\) multiplies by \(\sqrt{3}\) where the formula divides by it, giving a hexagon more than five times too big in area.

questions.note: The book prints choice D as "25 \u221a3 66"; the trailing 66 is the page number.

questions.stem: To determine the effect of magnesium supplementation on the sleep quality of adults, a researcher selected 190 adults at random from a community center to participate in a study. Each participant was randomly assigned to take a magnesium supplement or a placebo each day for 6 weeks. At the end of the 6 weeks, the researcher found that the magnesium supplement caused statistically significant improved sleep quality. What feature of this study allowed the researcher to conclude that the magnesium supplement caused the improved sleep quality?

choices.label: A
choices.content: There were more than 100 participants in the study.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The participants were selected at random from the community center.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The sleep efficiency of each participant was measured again at the end of 6 weeks.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Each participant was randomly assigned to take a magnesium supplement or a placebo.

questions.whyCorrect: Cause comes from random assignment, not random selection. Because a coin flip decided who took the supplement, the two groups start out alike on everything else — diet, age, existing sleep habits — so a difference at the end can be pinned on the treatment.

whyWrong.A: A large sample makes an estimate more precise; it does nothing about the possibility that the two groups differed to begin with.
whyWrong.B: Random selection is what lets the findings be generalized to the community center population. It is a separate property from causation.
whyWrong.C: Measuring again supplies the data but creates no comparison; without the randomly assigned placebo group there is nothing to compare the change against.

questions.note: The book prints the stem starting mid-word ("ffect of magnesium supplementation..."); restored to "To determine the effect of...".

questions.stem: An acceptable noise criterion rating for the background noise in a school classroom is 30. For a noise criterion rating of 30, the equation \[ y = 19(0.978)^{x-50} + 37 \]gives the estimated sound pressure level, y in decibels, as a function of the octave band center frequency, x, in hertz, where \( x \ge 50 \) . Which of the following is the best interpretation of 37 in this context?

choices.label: A
choices.content: 37 is 19 less than the estimated sound pressure level, in decibels, at an octave band frequency of 50

choices.label: B
choices.content: 37 is 19 less than the estimated sound pressure level, in decibels, at an octave band frequency of 0

choices.label: C
choices.content: 37 is the estimated sound pressure level, in decibels, at an octave band frequency of 50

choices.label: D
choices.content: 37 is the estimated sound pressure level, in decibels, at an octave band frequency of 0

questions.whyCorrect: Find the input that makes the exponent 0, because that is where the exponential term collapses. Here x - 50 = 0 at x = 50, and \( (0.978)^{0} = 1 \) , so y = 19 + 37 = 56 at that frequency. The 37 is therefore 19 below the level at x = 50 — it is the value the curve settles toward as x grows, not a value the curve actually takes.

whyWrong.B: x = 0 is outside the stated domain \( x \ge 50 \) , and the shift in the exponent is anchored at 50, not 0.
whyWrong.C: The level at x = 50 is 19 + 37 = 56. The 19 does not disappear there; that is exactly where it counts in full.
whyWrong.D: Both parts fail: 37 is not the level at any frequency in the domain, and x = 0 is not in the domain.

questions.stem:
\[ (x + k) + \frac{9}{2}(y + t) + 19 = 0 \]
\[ (x + k) - \frac{9}{2}(y + t) - 19 = 0 \]

In the given system of equations, k and t are constants. The solution to this system is \( (x, y) \) . What is the value of \( 18(y + t) \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Do not try to find x, y, k and t separately - treat \( (x+k) \) and \( (y+t) \) as single blocks. Subtracting the second equation from the first eliminates the \( (x+k) \) block and gives \( 9(y+t) + 38 = 0 \) , so \( (y+t) = -\frac{38}{9} \) . Multiplying by 18 gives \( 18(y+t) = -76 \) .

whyWrong.B: You would get 0 only if the two equations were identical; they differ in the sign of both the \( (y+t) \) term and the constant, so the difference is not zero.
whyWrong.C: 38 is the constant left after subtracting, before you divide by 9 and multiply by 18, and it also has the wrong sign.
whyWrong.D: 9 is the coefficient that appears after subtracting, not the value of \( 18(y+t) \) .

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((3x^{3} - x^{2} + 4)(5x^{2} + 8x)\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Distribute every term: \(3x^{3}(5x^{2}+8x) = 15x^{5} + 24x^{4}\), \(-x^{2}(5x^{2}+8x) = -5x^{4} - 8x^{3}\), and \(4(5x^{2}+8x) = 20x^{2} + 32x\). Combining \(24x^{4} - 5x^{4}\) gives \(19x^{4}\), leaving \(15x^{5} + 19x^{4} - 8x^{3} + 20x^{2} + 32x\). Note that every term of the second factor has an \(x\), so the product cannot have a constant term.

whyWrong.A: The last two terms have lost a power of \(x\); \(4 \cdot 5x^{2} = 20x^{2}\), not \(20x\), and \(4 \cdot 8x = 32x\), not 32.
whyWrong.B: The \(20x^{2}\) term is negative here, but it comes from \(+4 \cdot 5x^{2}\), and the constant 32 again drops an \(x\).
whyWrong.D: \(29x^{4}\) comes from adding \(24x^{4} + 5x^{4}\) instead of subtracting; the \(-x^{2}\) term makes that contribution negative.

questions.stem:
\[ f(x)=x^2-4x-320 \]
The function \(f\) is defined by the given equation. Which of the following equivalent forms of the equation displays the minimum value of the function as a constant or coefficient?
questions.whyCorrect: The minimum value of an upward parabola is the \(y\)-coordinate of its vertex, so you need vertex form \(a(x-h)^2+k\), where \(k\) is that minimum. Completing the square gives \((x-2)^2-324\), and \(-324\) is the minimum value (check: \(f(2)=4-8-320=-324\)).

whyWrong.A: This is just a partial factoring; \(-320\) is hidden inside a product and nothing in it is the minimum.
whyWrong.C: \(-320\) is the \(y\)-intercept, the value at \(x=0\), not the minimum. The graph dips lower, to \(-324\).
whyWrong.D: Factored form displays the \(x\)-intercepts, \(-16\) and 20, not the minimum value.

questions.stem: A machine fills bags with approximately 10 ounces of cranberries. To test the accuracy of the filling process, 148 bags of cranberries were selected at random and weighed. Based on the sample, it is estimated that the average weight of all bags of cranberries filled by the machine in an 8-hour period is 9.89 ounces, with an associated margin of error of 0.14 ounce. Which of the following is the best interpretation of this estimate?

choices.label: A
choices.content: Plausible values for the average weight of all bags of cranberries filled by the machine are between 9.75 ounces and 10.03 ounces.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Plausible values for the average weight of all bags of cranberries filled by the machine are less than 9.75 ounces or greater than 10.03 ounces.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The average weight of all bags of cranberries filled by the machine is greater than 9.99 ounces.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The average weight of all bags of cranberries filled by the machine is less than 9.99 ounces.

questions.whyCorrect: A margin of error marks off an interval on either side of the estimate, and the values inside that interval are the plausible ones. Here that is 9.89 − 0.14 = 9.75 up to 9.89 + 0.14 = 10.03 ounces.

whyWrong.B: This has the interval inside out. Values further than 0.14 from the estimate are the implausible ones.
whyWrong.C: 9.99 is 9.89 + 0.10, which is not either endpoint, and a margin of error never lets you claim the true average lies on one side of a single number.
whyWrong.D: Same problem: the estimate supports a two-sided interval, not a one-sided claim, and 9.99 is not an endpoint of it.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, ∠B is a right angle and the length of \( \overline{BC} \) is 248 millimeters. If \( \cos A = \frac{3}{5} \), what is the length, in millimeters, of \( \overline{AB} \)?
questions.whyCorrect: With the right angle at B, the hypotenuse is AC; relative to angle A, side AB is adjacent and BC is opposite. Since cos A = 3/5, the triangle is a 3-4-5 family triangle, so the opposite side is 4 parts and the adjacent side 3 parts, and tan A = 4/3. The known side BC is the opposite one, so \( AB = 248 \times \frac{3}{4} = 186 \).

whyWrong.A: 62 is 248 divided by 4 — one part of the ratio, not three.
whyWrong.C: 248 is the given side BC; the legs are not equal unless the acute angles are both 45 degrees.
whyWrong.D: 310 is the hypotenuse AC, found from \( 248 \times \frac{5}{4} \). It is what you get by mistaking AB for the hypotenuse; AB is a leg because the right angle is at B.

questions.stem:
Distance (miles)Average time (minutes)
0.063
0.2814
0.3417
The table gives the average time t, in minutes, it takes Adriana to travel a certain distance d, in miles. Which equation could represent this linear relationship?
questions.whyCorrect: Every choice passes through the origin, so you only need the constant of proportionality \(\frac{t}{d}\). Use any row: \(\frac{3}{0.06} = 50\), and the other rows agree (\(\frac{14}{0.28} = 50\), \(\frac{17}{0.34} = 50\)). So t = 50d. A sanity check helps: the times are much larger than the distances, so the multiplier must be large.

whyWrong.A: This divides distance by 50 instead of multiplying. At d = 0.06 it gives t = 0.0012 minutes, not 3.
whyWrong.B: At d = 0.06 this gives t = 0.03 minutes. The ratio \(\frac{t}{d}\) in the table is 50, not \(\frac{1}{2}\).
whyWrong.C: At d = 0.06 this gives t = 0.12 minutes. You may have divided in the wrong direction: \(\frac{0.06}{3} = 0.02\), and its reciprocal 50 is the number you want.

questions.stem: The circumference of the base of a right circular cylinder is \(6\pi\) meters, and the height of the cylinder is 19 meters. What is the volume, in cubic meters, of the cylinder?
questions.whyCorrect: The circumference gives you the radius: \(2\pi r = 6\pi\), so \(r = 3\). Then \(V = \pi r^{2} h = \pi(3)^{2}(19) = 171\pi\) cubic meters. The whole question turns on not using 6 as the radius.

whyWrong.A: \(57\pi = \pi(3)(19)\) — the radius was used once instead of squared.
whyWrong.B: \(114\pi = \pi(6)(19)\), which uses the diameter as if it were \(r^{2}\).
whyWrong.D: \(684\pi = \pi(6)^{2}(19)\): the 6 from \(6\pi\) was taken as the radius, but it is the diameter.

questions.stem: \[ -3x + 15px = 30 \]In the given equation, p is a constant. The equation has no solution. What is the value of p ?
questions.whyCorrect: Factor x out of the left side: \( (-3 + 15p)x = 30 \) . An equation of the form (number)x = 30 fails to have a solution only when that number is 0, since 0 times anything cannot equal 30. So \( 15p = 3 \) and \( p = \frac{1}{5} \) .

whyWrong.A: This does not make the coefficient zero — at \( p=\frac{2}{3} \) the coefficient is 7, and the equation has the solution \( x=\frac{30}{7} \) .
whyWrong.B: With p = 0 the equation is \( -3x = 30 \) , which solves to x = −10.
whyWrong.C: With p = 2 the coefficient is 27, so there is one solution, not none.

questions.note: The book prints the stem with two typos ("equatoin", "had no solution") and shows choice A as an unclosed "(2/3"; both have been cleaned up here. The item is also filed in the Mean/Median/Mode/Range chapter but is a linear-equation question.

questions.stem: The graph of the function f in the xy-plane, where \( y = f(x) \), has x-intercepts of (-5, 0), (3, 0), and (6, 0). Which of the following must be true?
questions.whyCorrect: At an x-intercept the output is 0, so each listed point (a, 0) tells you f(a) = 0. Since (6, 0) is one of them, \( f(6) = 0 \).

whyWrong.A: f(0) is the value where the graph crosses the y-axis, which is not given anywhere in the problem.
whyWrong.B: Again this reads an x-intercept as a y-value. The 3 is an input with output 0, so f(3) = 0.
whyWrong.C: The intercept is at -5, not 5. Nothing says f(5) is 0.

questions.note: Near-identical template to satmath-ma2-polynomials-3; do not place both in one test.

questions.stem: In the given equation, \(p\) is a positive constant. The product of the solutions to the equation \[ (3x-7p)(5x^2+8x-4p)(x^3+3x^2-16x-48) = 0 \]is \( -\frac{560}{9} \). What is the value of \(p\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Handle each factor separately. \( 3x-7p=0 \) gives the single root \( \frac{7p}{3} \). For \( 5x^2+8x-4p \), you do not need the roots themselves — their product is \( \frac{-4p}{5} \). The cubic factors by grouping: \( x^2(x+3)-16(x+3) = (x+3)(x-4)(x+4) \), whose roots multiply to \( (-3)(4)(-4) = 48 \). So the total product is \( \frac{7p}{3} \cdot \left(-\frac{4p}{5}\right) \cdot 48 = -\frac{448}{5}p^2 \). Setting that equal to \( -\frac{560}{9} \) gives \( p^2 = \frac{25}{36} \), so \( p = \frac{5}{6} \).

questions.stem:
\[ (3x + p)(5x^{2} - 45)(2x^{2} - 16x + 6p) = 0 \]

In the given equation, p is a positive constant. The sum of the solutions to the equation is \( \frac{20}{3} \) . What is the value of p?
questions.whyCorrect: Handle each factor separately and add the sums; you never need the individual roots of the last one. From \( 3x + p = 0 \) the solution is \( -\frac{p}{3} \) . From \( 5x^{2} - 45 = 0 \) the solutions are 3 and −3, which contribute 0. For \( 2x^{2} - 16x + 6p = 0 \) , the sum of the roots is \( \frac{16}{2} = 8 \) . So \( -\frac{p}{3} + 0 + 8 = \frac{20}{3} \) , which gives \( \frac{p}{3} = \frac{4}{3} \) and p = 4. Check that the last factor still has real roots: with p = 4 it is \( 2(x - 2)(x - 6) \) .

questions.stem:
\[ x^{2} + y^{2} = 36 \]
\[ y = mx + \frac{b}{4} \]

In the given system of equations, m and b are negative constants. In the xy-plane, the graphs of the equations in the given system intersect at the point \( (-5, y) \) , where \( y < 0 \) . Which expression represents the value of b?
questions.whyCorrect: Use the circle first: at x = −5, \( 25 + y^{2} = 36 \) gives \( y^{2} = 11 \) , and since \( y < 0 \) you take \( y = -\sqrt{11} \) , not the positive root. Substituting into the line, \( -\sqrt{11} = -5m + \frac{b}{4} \) , so \( \frac{b}{4} = 5m - \sqrt{11} \) . Multiplying both sides by 4 gives \( b = 20m - 4\sqrt{11} \) .

whyWrong.A: This keeps the positive root \( +\sqrt{11} \) and divides by 4 instead of multiplying, so both the sign and the scale are wrong.
whyWrong.B: This solves for \( \frac{b}{4} \) and stops, dividing by 4 rather than multiplying by it.
whyWrong.C: This uses \( y = +\sqrt{11} \) , which the condition \( y < 0 \) rules out, flipping the sign of every term.

questions.stem:
The functions \(f\), \(g\) and \(h\) are defined by the given equations, where \( x \ge 0 \). Which of the following equations displays, as a constant or coefficient, the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines, where \( x \ge 0 \)?
I. \( f(x) = (x-3)^2+6 \)
II. \( g(x) = (x+3)^2+6 \)
III. \( h(x) = (x-5)^2+8 \)
questions.whyCorrect: All three open upward, so each has a minimum at its vertex — but only if the vertex is in the allowed region \( x \ge 0 \). \(f\) has vertex \( x=3 \) and \(h\) has vertex \( x=5 \), both allowed, so their displayed constants 6 and 8 really are the minimum values. \(g\) has vertex \( x=-3 \), which is excluded; on \( x \ge 0 \) it increases, so its smallest value is \( g(0) = 15 \), and 15 appears nowhere in the equation.

whyWrong.A: III passes the same test as I — its vertex \( x=5 \) is in \( x \ge 0 \), so the 8 is a genuine minimum.
whyWrong.C: II fails: the vertex at \( x=-3 \) is outside the domain, so \(g\) never takes the value 6 there.
whyWrong.D: Two of the three do display their minimum; the check is whether the vertex lies in \( x \ge 0 \).

questions.stem:
\[ f(x) = -2(x-a)(x-b)(x-c) \]The function \(f\) is defined by the given equation, where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are distinct constants. When \( b < x < c \), the value of \( f(x) \) is positive. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane contains the point \( (m,n) \), where \(m\) and \(n\) are constants. If \(n\) is equal to -5, which of the following could be true?
I. \( m < a \)
II. \( a < m < b \)
III. \( m > c \)
questions.whyCorrect: The leading coefficient is negative, so the cubic is positive to the left of its smallest zero and then alternates: negative, positive, negative. For the positive stretch to be the interval \( (b,c) \), that must be the second gap, so the order of the zeros is \( a < b < c \). Then \(f\) is negative exactly on \( (a,b) \) and on \( x > c \). Since \( n = -5 \) is negative, \(m\) must lie in one of those two regions — statements II and III.

whyWrong.A: Left of the smallest zero a negative-leading cubic is positive, so \( m < a \) cannot give \( n = -5 \).
whyWrong.B: II works, but so does III: past the largest zero the graph is negative again.
whyWrong.D: III works, but I does not, for the sign reason above.

questions.stem: 80 people each bowled one game at Brick Alley Bowling last Friday. 60 people scored between 50 and 100, 18 people scored between 101 and 185, and the remaining two players bowled a score between 280 and 300. Which of the following statements about the mean and median of the 80 scores is true?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The mean is less than the median.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The median is less than the mean.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The median and mean are equal.

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is not enough information to determine whether the mean or median is greater.

questions.whyCorrect: The median is the average of the 40th and 41st scores, and since 60 scores fall between 50 and 100, both of those sit in that lowest band. The mean, by contrast, feels the two scores near 300: each is roughly 200 points above the bulk of the data, which drags the average upward. A right-skewed set has mean above median.

whyWrong.A: That happens when the outliers are on the low side. Here every unusual score is high.
whyWrong.C: Mean and median coincide only for a symmetric distribution; two extreme high scores with nothing to balance them on the left break the symmetry.
whyWrong.D: You do not need the exact scores. Knowing all the outliers lie far above the bulk is enough to fix the direction.

questions.stem:
Which of the following below has a factor of \( 4x+7b \), where \(b\) is a non-positive integer?
I. \( 16x^2-49 \)
II. \( 16x^2+56x+49 \)
III. \( 64x^3+343 \)
questions.whyCorrect: The constraint that \(b\) is non-positive is the whole question — the factor has to be \( 4x+7b \) with \( 7b \le 0 \), i.e. \( 4x-7 \), \( 4x-14 \), \( 4x \), and so on. I is a difference of squares, \( 16x^2-49 = (4x-7)(4x+7) \), and \( 4x-7 \) is \( 4x+7b \) with \( b = -1 \). II is the perfect square \( (4x+7)^2 \) and III is the sum of cubes \( (4x+7)(16x^2-28x+49) \); both have only \( 4x+7 \), which needs \( b = 1 \), a positive integer.

whyWrong.B: Both II and III factor with \( 4x+7 \) only, requiring \( b=1 \); III's quadratic factor \( 16x^2-28x+49 \) has a negative discriminant, so it contributes no other linear factor.
whyWrong.C: I qualifies but III does not, since \( 64x^3+343 = (4x+7)(16x^2-28x+49) \) forces \( b=1 \).
whyWrong.D: Only I contains a factor of the form \( 4x+7b \) with \(b\) non-positive.

questions.stem: In the figure above, O is the center of the circle and AC is tangent to the circle at D. If triangle ABC is equilateral, what is the ratio \(\frac{FE}{AC}\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Put D at the origin with AC along the x-axis, so \(A=(-\tfrac{s}{2},0)\), \(C=(\tfrac{s}{2},0)\) and \(B=(0,\tfrac{s\sqrt{3}}{2})\) for side s. The circle is tangent to AC at D, so its center is straight above D and its radius r satisfies 2r = height of the triangle, giving \(r=\frac{s\sqrt{3}}{4}\). Substituting the line AB into \(x^{2}+y^{2}-2ry=0\) gives \(4t^{2}-5t+1=0\) for the parameter t, whose roots are t = 1 (the point B) and \(t=\frac{1}{4}\) (the point F). So F is a quarter of the way from A to B, at \(x=-\frac{3s}{8}\), and by symmetry E is at \(x=\frac{3s}{8}\). Then \(FE=\frac{3s}{4}\) and \(\frac{FE}{AC}=\frac{3}{4}\).
questions.note: Figure needed: equilateral triangle ABC with base AC horizontal at the bottom and apex B at the top, and a circle passing through B and tangent to AC at D, the midpoint of AC. O is the circle's centre, on segment BD. The circle cuts AB at F and BC at E, and the horizontal chord FE is drawn; the angle between FO and FE at F is marked 30 degrees. Points D, E and F exist only in the figure.
questions.imageAlt: An equilateral triangle A B C with a circle through the apex B that touches the base at D; the circle's centre O lies on the segment from B to D. The circle crosses the two slanted sides at F and E, and the chord FE and the segment from F to O are drawn, with one angle at F marked in degrees.

questions.stem: A researcher conducted a study to determine if certain memorization strategies could improve the performance of chess players. For the study, the researcher selected a random sample of adults who are competing in a chess tournament. At the end of the study, 80% of those sampled reported that they did not find the memorization strategies to be useful during their chess games. Which of the following is the largest population to which the results of this study can be applied?

choices.label: A
choices.content: All chess players who compete in tournaments

choices.label: B
choices.content: All adults who compete in chess tournaments

choices.label: C
choices.content: All chess players competing in the tournament

choices.label: D
choices.content: All adults competing in the tournament

questions.whyCorrect: The sample was drawn at random from one specific group: the adults competing in that one tournament. Results extend to exactly that group. Both restrictions matter — adults, and this tournament.

whyWrong.A: Two steps too far: it drops the adults-only restriction and covers every tournament everywhere, none of whose players could have been sampled.
whyWrong.B: Keeps "adults" but covers all chess tournaments. Players at other tournaments had no chance of selection.
whyWrong.C: Right tournament but wrong people: it includes the under-18 competitors, who were never in the sampling pool.

questions.stem: A piece of string with a length of 35 inches is cut into two parts. One part has a length of \( x \) inches, and the other part has a length of \( y \) inches. The value of \( x \) is 5 more than 2 times the value of \( y \). What is the value of \( x \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Two facts give two equations: the pieces make up the whole string, so x + y = 35, and "5 more than 2 times y" means x = 2y + 5. Substitute the second into the first: (2y + 5) + y = 35, so 3y = 30 and y = 10. Then x = 2(10) + 5 = 25. Check: 25 + 10 = 35.

questions.stem:
xy

The table shows two values of x and their corresponding values of y. The graph of the linear equation representing this relationship passes through the point \((\frac{1}{4}, a)\). What is the value of a?
questions.whyCorrect: Get the equation from the two rows first. The slope is \(\frac{52 - (-33)}{6 - (-11)} = \frac{85}{17} = 5\) — both differences involve a double negative, which is where sign errors creep in. Using (6, 52): 52 = 5(6) + b gives b = 22, so y = 5x + 22. Then \(a = 5 \cdot \frac{1}{4} + 22 = \frac{5}{4} + 22 = \frac{93}{4}\), or 23.25.
