questions.whyCorrect: Work out the boundary value 5x - 4 at each x: 16 at x = 4, 26 at x = 6, and 41 at x = 9. Every y must be strictly greater than the matching boundary. Only 21, 31 and 46 clear all three.

whyWrong.A: At x = 4 the boundary is 16 and y is 11, which is below it, so the table fails on its first row.
whyWrong.B: These y-values equal 5x - 4 exactly. The inequality is strict, so points on the line are not solutions.
whyWrong.D: At x = 6 the boundary is 26 and y is 21, and at x = 9 the boundary is 41 and y is 41 — neither is strictly greater.

questions.stem:
\[ 3x^2-5x-5=0 \]
What is the greatest solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: With \(a=3\), \(b=-5\), \(c=-5\), the discriminant is \((-5)^2-4(3)(-5)=25+60=85\), so \(x=\frac{5\pm\sqrt{85}}{6}\). The greatest solution takes the plus sign.

whyWrong.A: Same two terms with a minus sign, which gives the smaller root.
whyWrong.C: The denominator must be \(2a=6\), not 3.
whyWrong.D: Same denominator error as C; using \(a\) rather than \(2a\) doubles the value.

questions.stem: If 5(2x + 9) = 3(2x + 9) + 74, what is the value of 2x + 9?
questions.whyCorrect: Let \(u = 2x + 9\). Then \(5u = 3u + 74\), so \(2u = 74\) and \(u = 37\). The step people miss is that the coefficients differ by 2, not by 1, so you must divide.

whyWrong.A: This skips the division: \(2u = 74\) gives \(u = 37\), not 74.
whyWrong.C: This is \(37 - 9\), an attempt to strip the 9 that is already inside the quantity you were asked for.
whyWrong.D: This is \(x\), from \(2x + 9 = 37\). The question asks for \(2x + 9\).

questions.stem: A town manager selected 2 random samples of residents in the town to estimate the percentage of all residents that planned to vote in favor of a new business in the downtown area. Based on the first sample, he estimated that 75% of the residents in town planned to vote in favor, with an associated margin of error of 8.3%. Based on the second sample, he estimated that 83% of the residents in the town planned to vote in favor, with an associated margin of error of 6.7%. Assuming the margins of error were calculated the same way, which of the following best explains why the first sample obtained a larger margin of error than the second sample?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The first sample contained fewer residents than the second sample.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The first sample contained more residents than the second sample.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The first sample contained a lower percentage of residents that planned to vote in favor of a new business in the downtown area.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The first sample contained a higher percentage of residents that planned to vote in favor of a new business in the downtown area.

questions.whyCorrect: Margin of error shrinks as the sample gets bigger — more people surveyed means a more precise estimate. The first sample's margin of error is the larger one (8.3% against 6.7%), so the first sample must have been the smaller one.

whyWrong.B: This has the relationship backwards. A larger sample produces a smaller margin of error, not a larger one.
whyWrong.C: The estimated percentage itself is not what drives the size of the margin of error here; the question says the margins were calculated the same way, leaving sample size as the explanation.
whyWrong.D: Same issue, and it is also false as stated — the first sample's percentage was 75%, lower than the second sample's 83%.

questions.stem: In a triangle ABC, the measure of angle A is 48°, the measure of angle B is 90°, and the measure of angle C is \( \left(\frac{k}{2}\right)^{\circ} \). What is the value of k?
questions.whyCorrect: The angles sum to 180°, so angle C measures 180 - 48 - 90 = 42 degrees. That 42 is \( \frac{k}{2} \), not k, so double it: k = 84. Forgetting the last step is the whole point of the question.

whyWrong.A: 42 is the measure of angle C in degrees, which is k/2.
whyWrong.B: 45 assumes the two acute angles are equal, which would require angle A to be 45° as well.
whyWrong.D: 96 is twice 48, doubling angle A instead of angle C.

questions.stem: On average, a certain tree grows 51 centimeters every \( m \) months. At this rate, which expression represents the number of centimeters, on average, the tree grows every \( k \) years?
questions.whyCorrect: Get a monthly rate first: \( \frac{51}{m} \) centimeters per month. Then convert the time, since \( k \) years is \( 12k \) months. Multiplying gives \( \frac{51}{m} \cdot 12k = \frac{612k}{m} \). Skipping the year-to-month conversion is what produces the wrong choices.

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{17m}{4k} \) has \( m \) on top and \( k \) underneath, so more months per 51 cm would mean more growth — backwards. It is also \( \frac{51}{12} \) reduced, i.e. a division by 12 instead of a multiplication.
whyWrong.B: \( \frac{17k}{4m} \) is \( \frac{51k}{12m} \), which divides by 12 instead of multiplying — that converts months to years, the wrong direction.
whyWrong.C: \( \frac{612m}{k} \) uses the right factor of 12 but inverts the variables, so the rate rises when the tree takes longer to grow 51 cm.

questions.stem:
\(y=x^2+17x+4\)
y = x + 4

The graphs of the equations in the given system intersect at the point \((x,y)\) in the \(xy\)-plane. What is a possible value of \(x\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Set the expressions equal: \(x^2+17x+4=x+4\). The 4s cancel and subtracting \(x\) leaves \(x^2+16x=0\), so \(x(x+16)=0\) and \(x=0\) or \(x=-16\). Only \(-16\) is offered.

whyWrong.B: \(-15\) does not satisfy either side: the parabola gives \(225-255+4=-26\) while the line gives \(-11\). Only 0 and \(-16\) solve \(x^2+16x=0\).
whyWrong.C: 13 has no route; the equation \(x^2+16x=0\) has only the roots 0 and \(-16\).
whyWrong.D: 15 is the positive version of a root that does not exist here. Both real intersections have \(x\le 0\).

questions.stem: A sphere has a radius of \(\frac{8}{3}\) feet. What is the volume, in cubic feet, of the sphere?
questions.whyCorrect: Use \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\) and cube numerator and denominator: \(\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)^3 = \frac{512}{27}\). Then \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot \frac{512}{27} = \frac{2048\pi}{81}\).

whyWrong.A: This is \(\pi\) times the reciprocal of the radius; the formula was not used.
whyWrong.B: \(\frac{32\pi}{9}\) is \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r\) with the radius left uncubed.
whyWrong.C: Nothing in the formula produces \(\frac{17}{3}\); check that you cubed \(\frac{8}{3}\).

questions.stem:
Data set A: 2, 2, 2, 5, 5, 8, 11, 11, 14, 14, 14
Data set B: 2, 5, 5, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 11, 11, 14

Data set A and data set B each have 11 values. Which of the following statements best compares the median of data set A and the median of data set B?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The median of data set A is greater than the median of data set B.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The median of data set A is less than the median of data set B.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The medians of data sets A and B are equal.

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is not enough information to compare the medians.

questions.whyCorrect: Both lists are already in increasing order and both have 11 values, so the median of each is simply the 6th entry. Counting in from the left, A's 6th value is 8 and B's 6th value is 8, so the medians are equal. The two sets look very different — A is spread to both ends, B is bunched at 8 — but that affects the standard deviation, not the median.

whyWrong.A: Counting to the 6th value in A gives 8, not something larger. A's three 14s sit past the middle and do not move it.
whyWrong.B: B's crowd of 8s does not raise its median above 8; the 6th value is still 8.
whyWrong.D: Every value in both sets is listed, so both medians can be found exactly.

questions.stem: For the linear function \(f\), the graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the xy-plane has a slope of \(\frac{4}{5}\) and passes through the point (20, 19). Which equation defines \(f\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Every choice already has the right slope, so all you need is b. Substitute the point into \(y = \frac{4}{5}x + b\): \(19 = \frac{4}{5}(20) + b = 16 + b\), so b = 3.

whyWrong.A: \(\frac{19}{20}\) is the two coordinates divided. A point is substituted into the equation, not turned into a fraction.
whyWrong.B: \(\frac{24}{5}\) is what you get with the coordinates swapped: \(20 - \frac{4}{5}(19) = \frac{24}{5}\). The point is (20, 19), so x = 20.
whyWrong.C: This uses the y-coordinate 19 as the intercept, which is only valid if the point sits on the y-axis. Here x = 20, so you must subtract the 16 that the slope contributes.

questions.stem: For the polynomial function \(f\), the graph of \(y=f(x)\) in the xy-plane passes through the points \((-3, 0)\), \((1, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\). Which of the following must be a factor of \(f(x)\)?
questions.whyCorrect: A point \((r,0)\) on the graph means \(f(r)=0\), and the factor theorem turns each zero \(r\) into the factor \(x-r\). The zeros are −3, 1 and 4, giving factors \(x+3\), \(x-1\) and \(x-4\). Only \(x-1\) is offered.

whyWrong.A: \(x+1\) corresponds to a zero at \(x=-1\), which is not one of the given points.
whyWrong.B: \(x+4\) matches a zero at −4; the graph crosses at \(+4\), so the factor is \(x-4\).
whyWrong.D: \(x-3\) matches a zero at \(+3\); the given zero is −3, so the factor is \(x+3\).

questions.note: Book prints “grapf”; corrected to “graph”.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by \( f(x) = \frac{|x|}{a} - 14 \) , where \( a < 0 \) . What is the product of \( f(15a) \) and \( f(8a) \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: The whole question turns on a being negative. Since \( a < 0 \) , \( 15a \) is negative, so \( |15a| = -15a \) and \( \frac{|15a|}{a} = \frac{-15a}{a} = -15 \) , giving \( f(15a) = -15 - 14 = -29 \) . The same reasoning gives \( f(8a) = -8 - 14 = -22 \) , and the product of the two negatives is \( (-29)(-22) = 638 \) . If you drop the bars and write \( \frac{15a}{a} = 15 \) you get +15 instead of -15 and the answer comes out wrong.

questions.stem: \[ \frac{5}{9}(5x+9)\left(x + \sqrt{5k+9}\,\right)\left(x - \sqrt{5k+9}\,\right) = 0 \]In the given equation, k is a positive constant. The product of the solutions to the equation is 72. What is the value of k ?
questions.whyCorrect: The three solutions are \( x = -\frac{9}{5} \) and \( x = \pm\sqrt{5k+9} \) . The two radical solutions multiply to \( -(5k+9) \) , so the whole product is \( -\frac{9}{5} \cdot \left(-(5k+9)\right) = \frac{9}{5}(5k+9) \) . Setting that equal to 72 gives \( 5k+9 = 40 \) , so \( k = \frac{31}{5} = 6.2 \) . The leading \( \frac{5}{9} \) contains no x, so it contributes no solution.

questions.stem:
\[ \frac{1}{cx}=\frac{x}{148}+\frac{1}{c} \]
In the given equation, \(c\) is a constant. If the equation has only one solution, what is the value of \(c\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Multiply every term by \(148cx\) to clear the fractions: the left side becomes 148 and the right becomes \(cx^2+148x\), so \(cx^2+148x-148=0\). One solution means the discriminant is zero: \(148^2-4(c)(-148)=0\), so \(21904+592c=0\) and \(c=-37\). (\(c\) cannot be 0, since \(\frac{1}{cx}\) would be undefined.)

questions.stem: For a set of three consecutive integers, the result of subtracting the greatest integer from the sum of the other two integers is 48. What is the value of the greatest of the three integers?
questions.whyCorrect: Call the integers n, n + 1 and n + 2, so the greatest is n + 2. The described quantity is \( [n + (n+1)] - (n+2) = n - 1 \), which equals 48, so n = 49. The question asks for the greatest, which is 49 + 2 = 51 — stopping at 49 is the trap.

questions.stem: A computer repair specialist charges $160 for the first two hours of repair plus an hourly fee for each additional hour. The total cost for 4 hours of repair is $240. Which function f gives the total cost, in dollars, for x hours of repair, where x ≥ 2?
questions.whyCorrect: The hourly fee is not given, so work it out: going from 2 hours to 4 hours costs 240 − 160 = $80 for 2 extra hours, so $40 per hour. The cost is then 160 + 40(x − 2) = 40x + 80. Check both anchors: f(2) = 160 and f(4) = 240.

whyWrong.B: This adds the full $160 on top of $40 for every hour including the first two. f(2) = 240, but two hours should cost $160.
whyWrong.C: This is 240 ÷ 4, treating the cost as proportional to hours. Then f(2) = 120, not the stated $160 for the first two hours.
whyWrong.D: Both the rate and the constant are too big: f(2) = 280 and f(4) = 400, neither matching the given costs.

questions.stem: The minimum value of x is 11 less than 8 times another number n. Which inequality shows the possible values of x?
questions.whyCorrect: Translate the phrase in two parts. "11 less than 8 times n" is 8n - 11, with the subtraction in that order. And a minimum is a lower bound, so x can equal it or be larger: \( x \ge 8n - 11 \).

whyWrong.A: This treats the value as a maximum. A minimum bounds x from below, so the inequality points the other way.
whyWrong.C: \( 11 - 8n \) reverses the subtraction. "11 less than" something means you take 11 away from that something.
whyWrong.D: The direction of the inequality is right but the expression is reversed; it should be 8n - 11.

questions.stem: \[ q(x) = 44(4^{x}) \] Which table gives three values of \(x\) and their corresponding values of \(q(x)\) for function \(q\)?

choices.label: A
choices.content:
x\(-1\)01
q(x)1760176

choices.label: B
choices.content:
x\(-1\)01
q(x)\(\frac{1}{11}\)4176

choices.label: C
choices.content:
x\(-1\)01
q(x)\(\frac{1}{11}\)44176

choices.label: D
choices.content:
x\(-1\)01
q(x)1144176

questions.whyCorrect: Evaluate all three inputs. \(q(-1) = 44 \cdot 4^{-1} = \frac{44}{4} = 11\), \(q(0) = 44 \cdot 1 = 44\), and \(q(1) = 44 \cdot 4 = 176\). A negative exponent divides by the base once; it does not make the whole output a reciprocal or a negative number.

whyWrong.A: \(q(0) = 44\), not 0, and \(q(-1)\) is not the same as \(q(1)\) — an exponential is not symmetric about the y-axis.
whyWrong.B: \(q(0)\) is shown as 4, which reads off the base instead of evaluating \(4^{0}=1\); \(q(-1)\) is wrong too.
whyWrong.C: \(q(0)\) and \(q(1)\) are right, but \(q(-1) = \frac{44}{4} = 11\). The \(\frac{1}{11}\) comes from taking the reciprocal of the whole value instead of dividing by the base once.

questions.stem: The positive number \(a\) is 3,700% of the number \(c\), and \(c\) is 20% of the number \(b\). If \(a - b = wc\), where \(w\) is a constant, what is the value of \(w\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Divide each percent by 100. From the first statement \(a = 37c\). The second says \(c = 0.20b\), and since the answer must be in terms of \(c\), solve for \(b\): \(b = \frac{c}{0.2} = 5c\). Then \(a - b = 37c - 5c = 32c\), so \(w = 32\).

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((6t^{4} - 3t^{2} + 3t - 6) - (2t^{4} - 4t^{3} + 6t^{2} - 6)\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Change the sign of every term in the second bracket: \(-2t^{4} + 4t^{3} - 6t^{2} + 6\). Then combine: \(6t^{4}-2t^{4}=4t^{4}\), \(0+4t^{3}=4t^{3}\), \(-3t^{2}-6t^{2}=-9t^{2}\), \(3t\) stays, and \(-6+6=0\), so there is no constant term.

whyWrong.A: The \(3t\) changed sign even though it appears only in the first bracket, and \(-6-6=-12\) treats the second \(-6\) as if it were being added.
whyWrong.C: \(t^{3}\) instead of \(4t^{3}\) drops the coefficient, and the \(t^{2}\) and \(t\) terms have been merged.
whyWrong.D: Both the \(t^{3}\) coefficient and the \(t^{2}\) terms are wrong; \(-3t^{2}-6t^{2}\) does not vanish.

questions.stem: Which quadratic equation has exactly one distinct real solution?
questions.whyCorrect: Exactly one distinct solution means the discriminant is 0. For D, \((-16)^2-4(1)(64)=256-256=0\); it is the perfect square \((x-8)^2=0\), whose only root is 8.

whyWrong.A: \(x^2=16\) gives \(x=\pm 4\), two solutions.
whyWrong.B: \(x^2=-16\) has no real solution at all, which is not the same as exactly one.
whyWrong.C: The discriminant is \(256-224=32\), positive, so there are two distinct real solutions.

questions.stem: The volume of a right rectangular prism with a square base is 1,792 cubic centimeters. If the area of the square base is 64 square centimeters, what is the area, in square centimeters, of one of the four lateral faces of the prism?
questions.whyCorrect: The base edge is \(\sqrt{64} = 8\), and the height is volume ÷ base area = 1,792 ÷ 64 = 28. A lateral face is a rectangle 8 by 28, so its area is 224.

whyWrong.A: 28 is the height alone, not an area. It still has to be multiplied by the 8 cm base edge.
whyWrong.C: 416 is not produced by any correct combination here; the two numbers you need are 8 and 28.
whyWrong.D: 896 is the four lateral faces added together, 4 × 224. Only one face was asked for.

questions.stem: A company that produces only one type of item wants to estimate the percent of the items produced in a typical week that are defective. A random sample of 400 of the items produced in a certain week were tested. Based on the sample, it is estimated that 8.5% of all items produced by the company in this week were defective, with an associated margin of error of 2.73%. Based on the estimate and associated margin of error, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion about all items produced by the company during this week?

choices.label: B
choices.content: It is plausible that between 5.77% and 11.23% of the items are defective.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It is plausible that more than 11.23% of the items are defective.

questions.whyCorrect: The estimate plus and minus the margin of error gives the interval of plausible values: 8.5 − 2.73 = 5.77% and 8.5 + 2.73 = 11.23%. The conclusion has to be stated as a plausible range, because a sample can only narrow the possibilities, never pin down the true percent.

whyWrong.A: 2.73% is the margin of error, the width on either side of the estimate — not a defect rate.
whyWrong.C: 8.5% is the sample's estimate. Reporting it as the exact figure for all items throws away the margin of error, which exists precisely because the sample may miss.
whyWrong.D: 11.23% is the top of the plausible range, so values above it are the implausible ones.

questions.stem:
4x = 16
-3x + y = -5

The solution to the given system of equations is \((x, y)\). What is the value of x + y?
questions.whyCorrect: The first equation gives \(x = 4\) straight away. Substituting into the second: \(-12 + y = -5\), so \(y = 7\). Then \(x + y = 11\).

whyWrong.A: A sign error: solving \(-12 + y = -5\) as \(y = -17\) gives \(-13\); nothing in the system produces \(-21\) except adding all the negatives.
whyWrong.B: This is the correct magnitude with the wrong sign — both \(x\) and \(y\) are positive here.
whyWrong.D: This comes from \(y = 17\), i.e. adding 12 to 5 instead of solving \(y = -5 + 12\).

questions.stem: The estimated number of a certain bacteria \(B(t)\) in a petri dish is given by the equation \(B(t) = 6700(2)^{t}\), where \(t\) is the time, in hours, after the bacteria were added to the petri dish. Which statement is the best interpretation of \(B(4) = 107200\) in this context?

choices.label: A
choices.content: 0 hours after the bacteria were added to the petri dish, the estimated number of bacteria in the petri dish is 4.

choices.label: B
choices.content: 0 hours after the bacteria were added to the petri dish, the estimated number of bacteria in the petri dish is 107,200.

choices.label: C
choices.content: 4 hours after the bacteria were added to the petri dish, the estimated number of bacteria in the petri dish is 4.

choices.label: D
choices.content: 4 hours after the bacteria were added to the petri dish, the estimated number of bacteria in the petri dish is 107,200.

questions.whyCorrect: The input is hours and the output is the bacteria count, so \(B(4) = 107{,}200\) says: at 4 hours there are about 107,200 bacteria. It checks out, since \(6700 \cdot 2^{4} = 6700 \cdot 16 = 107{,}200\).

whyWrong.A: At 0 hours the count is \(B(0) = 6{,}700\); the 4 is a time, not a population.
whyWrong.B: The time is wrong — 107,200 is the count at 4 hours, and at 0 hours the dish holds 6,700.
whyWrong.C: This reads the output as the input. The population is 107,200, not 4.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 inches. If the sum of the lengths of three sides of the rectangle is 21 inches, what is the length, in inches, of the fourth side?
questions.whyCorrect: The perimeter is the sum of all four sides, so the fourth side is whatever is left after the other three: 36 − 21 = 15. You never need the individual length and width, which is the trap — setting up 2L + 2W = 36 wastes time here.

whyWrong.A: 3 is the other dimension of the rectangle, which is 3 by 15. It is a side, but not the one left out of the 21.
whyWrong.B: 57 comes from adding 36 and 21 instead of subtracting. The three sides are part of the perimeter, so the result must be smaller than 36.
whyWrong.D: 36 is the whole perimeter, which is all four sides together.

questions.stem:
TaskTime (minutes)
A8
B6
C14
D11
E11
The table shows the amount of time it took a participant in a study to complete each of 5 tasks. What was the mean time, in minutes, for this participant to complete a task?
questions.whyCorrect: Add the five times and divide by 5: 8 + 6 + 14 + 11 + 11 = 50, and 50 ÷ 5 = 10 minutes. Every task counts once, including the repeated 11.

whyWrong.A: 8 is task A's time, not an average.
whyWrong.C: 11 is the median (the middle value once the times are ordered 6, 8, 11, 11, 14) and also the repeated value, but the mean is 10.
whyWrong.D: 9.5 is not reachable here: the five times total 50, so dividing by 5 gives exactly 10. A mean of 9.5 would need a total of 47.5.

questions.stem: For the linear function \(f\), the graph \(y = f(x)\) in the xy-plane has a slope of \(\frac{2}{3}\) and passes through the point (6, 5). Which equation defines \(f\)?
questions.whyCorrect: All four choices share the slope, so only the constant is in question. Substitute the point into \(y = \frac{2}{3}x + b\): \(5 = \frac{2}{3}(6) + b = 4 + b\), so b = 1.

whyWrong.A: \(\frac{5}{6}\) is the coordinates divided into a fraction, which is not what substitution does.
whyWrong.B: \(\frac{8}{3}\) comes from swapping the coordinates: \(6 - \frac{2}{3}(5) = \frac{8}{3}\). In (6, 5) the 6 is x.
whyWrong.C: This treats the y-coordinate 5 as the intercept. That only works for a point already on the y-axis; here you must subtract the 4 the slope contributes.

questions.stem: Which expression is a factor of \( 3x^{2} + 57x + 15 \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: A factor has to divide every term. All three coefficients 3, 57 and 15 are multiples of 3, so \( 3x^{2} + 57x + 15 = 3(x^{2} + 19x + 5) \) and 3 is a factor.

whyWrong.A: \( 3x^{2} \) is only the first term; the constant 15 has no \( x^{2} \) in it, so it cannot be divided by \( 3x^{2} \) .
whyWrong.B: 5 does not divide 3 or 57, and the constant term has no x, so 5x divides none of the expression evenly.
whyWrong.D: 57x is only the middle term, and again the constant 15 contains no x.

questions.stem: A circle has a radius of 19 meters. What is the area, in square meters, of the circle?
questions.whyCorrect: Area of a circle is \(A=\pi r^2\), so with \(r=19\) the area is \(\pi(19)^2=361\pi\). The radius is squared, not multiplied by 2.

whyWrong.A: \(\frac{19\pi}{2}\) halves the radius instead of squaring it.
whyWrong.B: \(19\pi\) uses \(\pi r\), leaving out the square.
whyWrong.C: \(38\pi\) is \(2\pi r\), the circumference, not the area.

questions.stem: A soccer team’s goal is to earn at least $1,320 by selling coupon books. The team earns $12 from selling each coupon book. Which of the following inequalities describes the possible values for the number of coupon books, n, the team can sell to meet the goal?
questions.whyCorrect: Earnings are $12 per book times n books, so the total is 12n. "At least $1,320" makes 1,320 a lower bound, so \( 12n \ge 1320 \).

whyWrong.A: Adding 12 to the number of books does not give money, and the inequality caps the total instead of requiring it.
whyWrong.B: The direction is right but n + 12 is not the amount earned; it would require selling 1,308 books to reach the goal instead of 110.
whyWrong.C: The expression 12n is correct, but this stops the team from earning more than $1,320 rather than requiring at least that much.

questions.stem: If \(x > 0\) and \(x\) is 33% of \(y\), which expression represents \(y\) in terms of \(x\)?
questions.whyCorrect: "\(x\) is 33% of \(y\)" means \(x = \frac{33}{100}y\). Solve for \(y\) by multiplying both sides by \(\frac{100}{33}\): \(y = \frac{100}{33}x\). Since \(x\) is only a third of \(y\), \(y\) must be about three times \(x\), which rules out any choice smaller than \(x\).

whyWrong.B: This is about \(0.3x\), smaller than \(x\). \(y\) has to be larger.
whyWrong.C: This divides by 33 without restoring the 100 from the percent, giving a \(y\) tiny compared to \(x\).
whyWrong.D: 67% is the part of \(y\) that is not \(x\); it is not a way to recover \(y\), and again gives a value below \(x\).

questions.note: In the book the fourth choice is misprinted with the label 'C' (two choices labelled C); relabelled D.

questions.stem: An object is kicked from a platform. The equation \( h = -4.9t^{2} + 13t + 15 \) represents this situation, where h is the height of the object above the ground, in meters, t seconds after it is kicked. Which number represents the height, in meters, from which the object was kicked?
questions.whyCorrect: "From which it was kicked" means the height at t = 0. Substituting 0 kills both t terms and leaves 15, so the constant term is the starting height.

whyWrong.A: 0 is the time of the kick, not the height. The object starts on a platform, so its height then is not 0.
whyWrong.B: 4.9 comes from gravity and controls how fast the object slows and falls. It carries the units of the \( t^{2} \) term.
whyWrong.C: 13 is the initial upward speed in meters per second, the coefficient of t, not a height.

questions.stem: A quadratic function can be used to model the height, in meters, of an object above the ground in terms of time, in seconds, after the object was launched into the air. The object reached a height of 148 meters 2 seconds after it was launched and a maximum height of 340 meters 10 seconds after it was launched. Based on the model, what was the longest time, in seconds, at which the object was at a height of 97 meters?
questions.whyCorrect: The maximum gives the vertex, so \( h(t) = a(t - 10)^{2} + 340 \) . Use the other data point: \( h(2) = 64a + 340 = 148 \) , so a = -3 and \( h(t) = -3(t-10)^{2} + 340 \) . Setting h(t) = 97 gives \( (t-10)^{2} = 81 \) , so t = 1 on the way up and t = 19 on the way down. The later of the two is 19.
questions.note: The book's wording is "what was the longest time period when the object reached a height of 97 meters". Read as the later of the two times, 19 s. If it were instead read as the length of the interval between the two crossings, the answer would be 18; flag for a human if the printed key says 18.

questions.stem: The exponential function f is defined by \[ f(x) = ab^{x} \]where a and b are positive. If \( f(n-1) = f(n) + \frac{61}{100}f(n-1) \) , where n is a constant, what is the value of b?
questions.whyCorrect: Collect the two f(n-1) terms on one side: \( f(n) = f(n-1) - \frac{61}{100}f(n-1) = \frac{39}{100}f(n-1) \) . For an exponential, stepping the input up by 1 multiplies the output by b, so \( \frac{f(n)}{f(n-1)} = b \) . Therefore \( b = \frac{39}{100} = 0.39 \) . The a cancels, so it never matters.
questions.note: 39/100 is equally acceptable as the grid-in form.

questions.stem: The equation \( N(m) = 63(Q)^{\frac{m}{6}} \) gives the predicted population \( N(m) \), in thousands, of a certain bacteria colony \(m\) minutes after the initial measurement, where \(Q\) is a constant greater than 1. The predicted population increases by \(p\)% every 180 seconds. What is the value of \(p\) in terms of \(Q\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Convert the units first: \(m\) is in minutes, and 180 seconds is 3 minutes. Over 3 minutes the population is multiplied by \( Q^{\frac{3}{6}} = Q^{\frac{1}{2}} \). A growth factor of \( Q^{\frac{1}{2}} \) is an increase of \( Q^{\frac{1}{2}}-1 \) as a decimal, so as a percent \( p = 100\left(Q^{\frac{1}{2}}-1\right) \).

whyWrong.A: \( Q^{30} \) treats 180 as a count of minutes and divides by 6; the 180 is in seconds, so it is 3 minutes, not 180.
whyWrong.C: Two errors: the wrong exponent, and adding 1 instead of subtracting. The percent increase is factor minus 1.
whyWrong.D: The exponent is right but the sign is not: \( Q^{\frac{1}{2}}+1 \) would be the percent increase only if the population had started from zero.

questions.stem: For the polynomial function \(v\), \( v(2) = 3 \) and \( v(0) = -13 \). The graph of \( y = v(x) \) in the xy-plane passes through the points \( (-2,7) \) and \( (6,0) \). Which of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.content: When \( v(x) \) is divided by \( (x+13) \), the remainder is 0.

choices.label: B
choices.content: When \( v(x) \) is divided by \( (x+7) \), the remainder is -2.

choices.label: C
choices.content: When \( v(x) \) is divided by \( (x+2) \), the remainder is 7.

choices.label: D
choices.content: When \( v(x) \) is divided by \( (x-6) \), the remainder is -13.

questions.whyCorrect: The remainder theorem says dividing by \( x-r \) leaves the remainder \( v(r) \) — so you need the sign flipped when the divisor is written as \( x+r \). Dividing by \( x+2 \) means \( r = -2 \), and the point \( (-2,7) \) tells you \( v(-2) = 7 \), so the remainder is 7.

whyWrong.A: This asks for \( v(-13) \). The \(-13\) you were given is an output, \( v(0) = -13 \), not an input, so nothing is known about \( v(-13) \).
whyWrong.B: This asks for \( v(-7) \), which is never given; the 7 in the data is the output at \( x=-2 \).
whyWrong.D: Dividing by \( x-6 \) leaves \( v(6) \), and the point \( (6,0) \) makes that 0, not \(-13\).

questions.stem: John and Karen work at the bakery. John works 7 hours per day, and Karen works 6 hours per day. John produces x brownies per hour and Karen produced y brownies per hour. Which of the following expressions gives the average number of brownies John and Karen produce per hour?
questions.whyCorrect: An average rate is total output divided by total time, not the average of the two rates. John bakes \(7x\) brownies and Karen bakes \(6y\), for \(7x + 6y\) in \(7 + 6 = 13\) hours, so the average is \(\frac{7x+6y}{13}\). Because John works more hours, his rate carries more weight, which is why a plain average of x and y is wrong.

whyWrong.A: \(x + y\) adds the two hourly rates, which is not a number of brownies. Dividing that by 13 hours does not produce a rate either.
whyWrong.C: Multiplying the two rates has no meaning here; the units come out as brownies squared per hour squared.
whyWrong.D: The hours are attached to the wrong people: John works 7 hours and produces at rate x, so the 7 belongs with x.

questions.stem: When the polynomial \( P(x) = 2x^3-5x^2+ax+b \) is divided by \( x-2 \), the remainder is 10. When \( P(x) \) is divided by \( x+1 \), the remainder is 1. What is the value of \( a+b \)?
questions.whyCorrect: By the remainder theorem the two facts are \( P(2) = 10 \) and \( P(-1) = 1 \). Substituting gives \( 16-20+2a+b = 10 \), i.e. \( 2a+b = 14 \), and \( -2-5-a+b = 1 \), i.e. \( b-a = 8 \). Adding \( b = a+8 \) into the first equation gives \( 3a+8 = 14 \), so \( a = 2 \) and \( b = 10 \), and \( a+b = 12 \).

questions.stem:
In the figure shown, points A, B, C, and E lie on the circle, and AB < BC. Segment AC is perpendicular to segment BE at point D, and \( BD = \sqrt{346} \) . The diameter of the circle is 175. If \( \frac{CD}{AD} = r \) , what is the value of r?

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
questions.whyCorrect: The figure marks a right angle at B, and an inscribed right angle stands on a diameter, so AC is the diameter: AD + DC = 175. BD is then the altitude to the hypotenuse of right triangle ABC, and the geometric-mean relation gives \( BD^{2} = AD \cdot DC \) , so \( AD \cdot DC = 346 \) . Two numbers with sum 175 and product 346 are the roots of \( t^{2} - 175t + 346 = 0 \) , namely 2 and 173. Since AB < BC, AD is the shorter piece, so AD = 2, DC = 173 and \( r = \frac{173}{2} = 86.5 \) .
questions.note: Measured reading of the figure: A, B, C and E lie on the circle with B upper left, C at the right, A at the left and E at the lower left; chords AC and BE cross at D inside the circle at a right angle, and a right-angle mark is drawn at vertex B in triangle ABC. That right angle at B is what makes AC the diameter, so the figure is load-bearing. 173/2 is an equally acceptable grid-in form.
questions.imageAlt: A circle with four labelled points on it; two chords are drawn inside the circle, crossing at a labelled interior point, with right-angle marks at two of the vertices.

questions.whyCorrect: Look for the table that piles its values onto one number. A has 55 of its 75 values sitting exactly at 5 and the remaining 20 only one unit away, giving a standard deviation near 0.52; the others spread their counts across all five values.

whyWrong.B: A wide mound: 22 of its 75 values are two units from the center, giving about 1.27.

questions.stem: \[ \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{x^2-c^2}} = \frac{c^2}{\sqrt{x^2-c^2}} + 39 \]In the given equation, \(c\) is a positive constant. Which of the following is one of the solutions to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Both fractions have the same denominator, so move them together: \( \frac{x^2-c^2}{\sqrt{x^2-c^2}} = 39 \). A quantity divided by its own square root is that square root, so this is just \( \sqrt{x^2-c^2} = 39 \). Squaring gives \( x^2 = c^2+39^2 \), so \( x = \pm\sqrt{c^2+39^2} \), and the negative one is listed.

whyWrong.A: \( x = -c \) makes \( x^2-c^2 = 0 \), so both denominators are zero and the expression is undefined.
whyWrong.B: This is \( x^2 \) with a sign error, not \(x\); you still have to take a square root, and \( -c^2-39^2 \) is negative, so its square cannot equal \( c^2+39^2 \).
whyWrong.C: Subtracting instead of adding: squaring gives \( x^2 = 39^2-c^2 \), which makes \( x^2-c^2 = 39^2-2c^2 \), not \( 39^2 \).

questions.note: DEFECT in the book's typesetting: the +39 is printed under the right-hand radical, as c^2/sqrt(x^2-c^2+39). Taken literally that equation has no real solutions for any positive c (checked with sympy for c = 1, 5, 13, 20, 50 — all four roots complex), and none of the choices satisfies it. Transcribed with the 39 as a separate term, which is the only reading under which a listed choice works and which the choices themselves (all built on 39^2) confirm.

questions.stem: Two identical rectangular prisms each have a height of 90 centimeters (cm). The base of each prism is a square, and the surface area of each prism is K cm<sup>2</sup>. If the prisms are glued together along a square base, the resulting prism has a surface area of \(\frac{92}{47}K\) cm<sup>2</sup>. What is the side length, in cm, of each square base?
questions.whyCorrect: With base side s, one prism has \(K=2s^{2}+4(90s)=2s^{2}+360s\). Gluing them base to base makes a single prism \(s\times s\times 180\), whose surface area is \(2s^{2}+720s\) - the two square faces that got glued are now interior and disappear, which is why the answer is less than 2K. Setting \(2s^{2}+720s=\frac{92}{47}(2s^{2}+360s)\) and clearing the fraction gives \(94s^{2}+33{,}840s=184s^{2}+33{,}120s\), so \(90s^{2}=720s\) and s = 8.

whyWrong.A: s = 4 makes the ratio \(\frac{4+360}{4+180}=\frac{91}{46}\), not \(\frac{92}{47}\). The two differ by little, so check the ratio rather than eyeballing it.
whyWrong.C: s = 9 makes the ratio \(\frac{369}{189}=\frac{41}{21}\).
whyWrong.D: s = 16 makes the ratio \(\frac{376}{196}=\frac{94}{49}\), which looks deceptively like \(\frac{92}{47}\) but is not equal to it.

questions.stem: The positive number a is 2,800% of the number c, and c is 20% of the number b. What is the value of \(a - b\) in terms of c?
questions.whyCorrect: 2,800% is 28 times, so \(a = 28c\). The other relationship runs backwards: c is 20% of b, so \(c = 0.2b\), which means \(b = 5c\). Then \(a - b = 28c - 5c = 23c\).

whyWrong.B: \(140 = 28 \times 5\); this multiplies where the question asks you to subtract.
whyWrong.C: \(560 = 28 \times 20\); it uses the number 20 rather than converting 20% into \(\frac{1}{5}\).
whyWrong.D: This chains the two percentages as raw numbers instead of subtracting the two quantities.

questions.note: Exact duplicate of problem-solving-6 in the same book.

questions.stem:
\[ f(x) = ax^{2} + 6x + c \]

In the given quadratic function, a and c are constants. The graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane is a parabola that opens upward and has a vertex at the point (h, k), where h and k are constants. If \( k > 0 \) and \( f(-7) = f(5) \) , which of the following must be true?

I. \( c > 3 \)
II. \( a > 3 \)
questions.whyCorrect: Equal outputs at −7 and 5 mean those points are mirror images, so the axis of symmetry is halfway between them: \( h = \frac{-7 + 5}{2} = -1 \) . Since \( h = -\frac{6}{2a} = -\frac{3}{a} \) , this forces a = 3 exactly. Then \( k = f(-1) = 3 - 6 + c = c - 3 \) , and \( k > 0 \) gives \( c > 3 \) . So I must be true and II cannot be, because a equals 3 rather than exceeding it.

whyWrong.B: a is pinned to exactly 3 by the symmetry condition, so "a > 3" is false, not merely unproven.
whyWrong.C: I holds but II does not, so they cannot both be true.
whyWrong.D: I does follow: the vertex height is c − 3, and it is given to be positive.

questions.note: The slice records this as free response; the book prints four choices.

questions.stem: In the figure above, the area of triangle ABC is equal to \(2x^{2}\). What is the cosine of angle BCP?
questions.whyCorrect: BP is the height of triangle ABC onto base AC, and both BP and AP equal x. So \(\frac{1}{2}(AC)(x)=2x^{2}\) gives AC = 4x, and therefore PC = 4x − x = 3x. Now work inside right triangle BPC, right-angled at P: the legs are BP = x and PC = 3x, so \(BC=\sqrt{x^{2}+9x^{2}}=x\sqrt{10}\). Cosine of the angle at C is adjacent over hypotenuse, \(\frac{3x}{x\sqrt{10}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\).

whyWrong.A: This is \(\frac{BP}{BC}\), the side opposite the angle over the hypotenuse - that is the sine of angle BCP, not the cosine.
whyWrong.C: This is \(\frac{BP}{PC}\), opposite over adjacent, which is the tangent.
whyWrong.D: This is \(\frac{PC}{BP}\), the reciprocal of the tangent. A cosine can never exceed 1, so this can be ruled out on sight.

questions.note: Figure needed: triangle ABC with A at the lower left, C at the lower right and B above, between them but nearer A. The altitude BP is drawn from B perpendicular to AC, meeting it at P; the segment AP is labelled x and the segment BP is labelled x. Both x labels appear only in the figure.
questions.imageAlt: A triangle A B C with base AC horizontal and apex B above a point P near A; the altitude from B meets AC at a right angle at P. The part of the base from A to P and the altitude itself are both labelled.

questions.stem: The composition of an animal is defined as the muscles, bones, and fat of the animal. A scientist studied the composition of one young swamp buffalo and determined that the buffalo had 139.2 kilograms of muscle, which made up approximately 67.7% of its composition. Of the remaining composition of this buffalo, approximately 51.4% was bone, and the remainder was fat. Based on these approximations, to the nearest tenth, how many kilograms of this buffalo's composition was bone?
questions.whyCorrect: The 51.4% is taken of what is left after the muscle, not of the whole animal. Total composition \(= \frac{139.2}{0.677} \approx 205.61\) kg, so the remaining part is \(205.61 - 139.2 \approx 66.41\) kg. Bone is \(0.514 \times 66.41 \approx 34.1\) kg. Applying 51.4% to the full 205.61 kg gives about 105.7 and is the trap.

questions.stem: \[b - 22 = \frac{x}{y}\]The given equation relates positive numbers \(b\), \(x\), and \(y\). Which equation correctly expresses \(x\) in terms of \(b\) and \(y\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Multiply both sides by \(y\). The \(y\) must multiply the whole left side, not just part of it: \(x = y(b-22) = by - 22y\).

whyWrong.A: Dividing by \(y\) is the wrong direction — \(x\) is already divided by \(y\) in the original, so undoing that multiplies.
whyWrong.B: Here \(y\) was multiplied onto \(b\) only. Distribute it over both terms of \(b-22\).
whyWrong.D: This divides by \(y\) instead of multiplying, which would be right if the original read \(b - 22 = xy\).

questions.stem: If 9 + x = 6, what is the value of -18 - 2x?
questions.whyCorrect: From \(9 + x = 6\), \(x = -3\). Then \(-18 - 2(-3) = -18 + 6 = -12\). The sign trap is subtracting a negative: \(-2x\) is positive when \(x\) is negative. (Shortcut: \(-18 - 2x = -2(9 + x) = -2(6)\).)

whyWrong.B: This is \(-18 + 16\), which needs \(x = -8\). But \(9 + x = 6\) gives \(x = -3\).
whyWrong.C: 6 is the right side of the given equation, not the value of the new expression.
whyWrong.D: This is \(18 + 6\) with the leading minus sign dropped. The expression starts at \(-18\), so the result is negative.

questions.stem: Line r is defined by the equation 4x − 7y = 3. Line s is parallel to line r in the xy-plane. What is the slope of line s?
questions.whyCorrect: Parallel lines have the same slope, so find r's. Solving for y: −7y = −4x + 3, then dividing by −7 gives \(y = \frac{4}{7}x - \frac{3}{7}\). The slope is \(\frac{4}{7}\), so line s has slope \(\frac{4}{7}\) as well.

whyWrong.A: This is the reciprocal, from putting the y-coefficient over the x-coefficient. In Ax + By = C the slope is \(-\frac{A}{B}\).
whyWrong.C: This reads the slope off the x-term without dividing by the y-coefficient. You still have to isolate y first.
whyWrong.D: This is the coefficient of y. Here \(-\frac{A}{B} = -\frac{4}{-7} = \frac{4}{7}\), and the two negatives cancel.

questions.note: Same item as Linear Functions question 40 in this book with 7 in place of 5; use only one of the pair in a test.

questions.stem:
\( y \le x + 9 \)
\( y \ge -2x - 9 \)
Which point (x, y) is a solution to the given system of inequalities in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: Test each point in both inequalities; a solution has to satisfy both. For (7, 0): the first needs \( 0 \le 7 + 9 = 16 \), true, and the second needs \( 0 \ge -14 - 9 = -23 \), also true.

whyWrong.A: (0, -10) passes the first inequality but fails the second: -10 is not greater than or equal to -9.
whyWrong.B: (0, 10) fails the first: 10 is not less than or equal to 0 + 9 = 9.
whyWrong.C: (-7, 0) passes the first but fails the second: -2(-7) - 9 = 5, and 0 is not greater than or equal to 5.

questions.stem: Which system of linear equations has no solution?
questions.whyCorrect: Test each pair by trying to scale one equation into the other. In D, multiply −2x + 8y = 5 by −2: the left side becomes 4x − 16y, matching the second equation, but the right side becomes −10, not 10. Same coefficients, different constant — parallel distinct lines, so no solution.

whyWrong.A: Multiplying the first equation by −1 gives 2x − 8y = 5, exactly the second equation. Same line, so infinitely many solutions.
whyWrong.B: The coefficient ratios differ (\(\frac{2}{3} \ne \frac{-8}{9}\)), so these lines have different slopes and cross at exactly one point.
whyWrong.C: Multiplying the first equation by −3 gives −6x + 24y = −15, the second equation exactly. Same line again, so infinitely many solutions.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(11(x^{2} - 100y^{2})\)?
questions.whyCorrect: \(x^{2} - 100y^{2}\) is a difference of squares, since \(100y^{2} = (10y)^{2}\). So it factors as \((x-10y)(x+10y)\), and the 11 stays outside.

whyWrong.A: Multiplying out gives \(x^{2} - 52xy + 100y^{2}\) — both the middle term and the sign of the last term are wrong.
whyWrong.B: This expands to \(x^{2} + 48xy - 100y^{2}\); the \(xy\) term must cancel, which only happens when the two numbers are equal and opposite.
whyWrong.C: This is \((x-10y)^{2} = x^{2} - 20xy + 100y^{2}\), a perfect square, not a difference of squares.

questions.stem:
\[ (x-42)^2=1 \]
What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both signs: \(x-42=\pm 1\), so \(x=43\) or \(x=41\). Their sum is 84. The two solutions sit symmetrically either side of 42, so the sum is always twice 42.

whyWrong.A: 42 is the center of symmetry, the average of the two solutions, not their sum.
whyWrong.B: 43 is only one of the two solutions — the one from the \(+1\) branch.
whyWrong.D: 85 adds 42 and 43, mixing the center with one solution instead of adding the two solutions.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by f(x) = 10x + 8. What is the value of \(f(x)\) when x = 7?
questions.whyCorrect: Substitute 7 for x: 10(7) + 8 = 70 + 8 = 78. Multiply before you add.

whyWrong.A: This adds 10 + 8 + 7. The 10 multiplies x, it does not get added to it.
whyWrong.B: An arithmetic slip: 10(7) is 70, and 70 + 8 is 78, not 66.
whyWrong.D: This swaps the 8 and the 7, computing 10(8) + 7. The value substituted for x is 7.

questions.stem: The expression \[ 12x^2+41x+35 \]can be rewritten as \( (4x+r)(3x+s) \), where \(r\) and \(s\) are integers, or as \( (4x+t)(3x+v) \), where \(t\) and \(v\) are not integers. What is the value of \( s+v \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Expanding \( (4x+r)(3x+s) \) gives \( 12x^2+(4s+3r)x+rs \), so you need \( rs = 35 \) and \( 4s+3r = 41 \). The integer pair is \( r=7 \), \( s=5 \) (the other order gives 43). For the non-integer pair, substitute \( v = \frac{35}{t} \) into \( 4v+3t = 41 \) to get \( 3t^2-41t+140 = 0 \), whose roots are \( t = 7 \) and \( t = \frac{20}{3} \); the non-integer one gives \( v = \frac{21}{4} \). So \( s+v = 5+\frac{21}{4} = \frac{41}{4} \).

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{41}{3} \) is \( t+? \)-style bookkeeping on the wrong pair — it is what you get by adding the two t-values \( 7+\frac{20}{3} \) and dividing, not \( s+v \).
whyWrong.C: 12 is the leading coefficient, not a sum of the two second constants.
whyWrong.D: 35 is the product \( rs \), the constant term.

questions.stem: For the function f, for each increase in the value of x by 4, the value of f(x) increases by a factor of m. Which of the following forms displays m as a constant or coefficient?
questions.whyCorrect: You want the exponent written so that a step of 4 in x moves it by exactly 1, because then the base is m. Only choice D has the coefficient \( \frac{1}{4} \) on x. Check that its base is a genuine constant: \( 100000 = 10^{5} \) , so \( 100000^{\frac{6}{5}} = 10^{6} \) , and \( f(x) = 13\left(10^{6}\right)^{\frac{x}{4}} \) . Raising x by 4 multiplies f by \( 10^{6} \) , which is the displayed base.

whyWrong.A: Exponent 2x means the base 100 is the factor for half a unit of x; a step of 4 would multiply by \( 100^{8} \) .
whyWrong.B: Exponent \( \frac{x}{3} \) makes 1,000 the factor for a step of 3, not 4.
whyWrong.C: Exponent 6x makes the base the factor for a step of \( \frac{1}{6} \) , far from 4.

questions.note: The book calls these "equivalent forms", but the four expressions are not equal to one another (they reduce to 13*10^(4x), 13*10^x, 13*10^(7.2x) and 13*10^(1.5x)). Exactly one choice satisfies the stated property, so the item is answerable; the word "equivalent" should be dropped. Same defect as Advanced Math #22.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by \[ f(x) = ab^{x} \]where a and b are integer constants. If f(2) = 6 and f(5) = 162, what is the value of f(7)?
questions.whyCorrect: Divide the two given outputs: \( \frac{f(5)}{f(2)} = b^{3} = \frac{162}{6} = 27 \) , so b = 3. Then step forward from f(5) rather than solving for a: f(7) is two steps on, so \( f(7) = 162 \cdot 3^{2} = 1458 \) .
questions.note: The book writes "where a, b, and x are constants, and a, b, and x are integers", which is wrong for x (the input). Same template as Advanced Math #68 in this book; do not place both in one test.

questions.stem: \[ x(9x-2a) + b(9x-2a) - (x+b) = 0 \]In the given equation, \(a\) and \(b\) are positive constants. A solution to the equation is \( x = 42 \). What is the value of \(a\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Do not expand — factor. The first two terms share \( 9x-2a \), giving \( (x+b)(9x-2a) \), and the third term is \( -(x+b) \), so the whole left side is \( (x+b)(9x-2a-1) \). The solutions are therefore \( x = -b \) and \( x = \frac{2a+1}{9} \). Since \(b\) is positive, \( -b \) cannot be 42, so \( \frac{2a+1}{9} = 42 \), giving \( 2a+1 = 378 \) and \( a = 188.5 \).

questions.stem: A clothing store buys shirts at a wholesale price of 5.00 dollars each and resells them each at a price that is 270% of the wholesale price. At the end of the season, any remaining shirts are marked at a discounted price that is 70% of the retail price. What is the discounted price of each remaining shirt, in dollars?
questions.whyCorrect: Apply the two percentages in order, each to the price it refers to. Retail \(= 2.70 \times 5.00 = \$13.50\), and the discounted price is 70% of that: \(0.70 \times 13.50 = \$9.45\). Note that 70% of the retail price is the new price itself, not the amount taken off.

questions.stem: For a polynomial function \(f\), the graph of \( y = f(x) \) in the xy-plane contains the points \( (-6,0) \), \( (7,0) \), \( (0,0) \), and \( (4,0) \). Which of the following must be a factor of \( f(x) \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Each listed point has y-coordinate 0, so \(-6\), 7, 0 and 4 are all zeros of \(f\), and a quadratic can only be a factor if both of its own zeros are on that list. Factor each choice: \( x^2-7x = x(x-7) \) has zeros 0 and 7, both on the list, so it divides \( f(x) \).

whyWrong.A: \( x^2-2x-24 = (x-6)(x+4) \), with zeros 6 and \(-4\) — the signs of the given zeros \(-6\) and 4 are flipped.
whyWrong.B: \( x^2-x+42 \) has discriminant \( 1-168 < 0 \), so it has no real zeros at all and cannot be built from these x-intercepts. It looks plausible only because \( -6 \times 7 = -42 \), and even that sign is wrong.
whyWrong.C: \( x^2-11x-28 \) does not factor over the integers; its zeros are \( \frac{11\pm\sqrt{233}}{2} \), neither of which is a listed zero.

questions.stem:
RadiusHeight
Cylinder ARH
Cylinder B4R3H + 24
Cylinders A and B are similar. The volume of cylinder A is \(1176\pi\) cm3. If the surface areas of cylinder B and A are \(n\pi\) cm2 and \(k\pi\) cm2, respectively, what is the value of \(n-k\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Similar cylinders scale every length by the same factor, and the radii show that factor is 4. So the heights must scale by 4 too: \(3H+24=4H\), giving H = 24. Then \(\pi R^{2}(24)=1176\pi\) gives \(R^{2}=49\) and R = 7. Cylinder A's surface area is \(2\pi(49)+2\pi(7)(24)=98\pi+336\pi=434\pi\), so k = 434. Areas scale by \(4^{2}=16\), so \(n=16(434)=6{,}944\) and \(n-k=6{,}944-434=6{,}510\).

questions.stem: Each of the three data sets represented by the three dot plots has 18 values. The median of data sets A, B, and C are a, b, and c respectively. What is the relationship between a, b, and c?
questions.whyCorrect: With 18 values, each median is the average of the 9th and 10th values. Counting up from the left in each plot, the 9th and 10th dots all land on 5 in all three data sets, so \(a = b = c = 5\). The plots differ in spread — A has a stray value at 9, C is spread across 1 through 9 — but spread does not move the middle.

whyWrong.A: This reads the widths of the plots rather than their centers. C is the most spread out, but its middle two values are still 5.
whyWrong.B: Same error in reverse: A's long right tail at 9 pulls the mean up, not the median.
whyWrong.C: There is no ordering at all here; all three middles coincide.

questions.imageAlt: Three dot plots, one for Data Set A, one for Data Set B and one for Data Set C, each showing a stack of dots above the values 1 through 10 on a number line.

questions.stem: In the xy-plane above, the function \(f\) is defined by \( f(x) = 2x^3+3x^2+ax+b \), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. If the graph of \(f\) intersects the x-axis at three points, what is the value of \(a\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Read the two labelled zeros, \( x = -3 \) and \( x = 2 \), off the graph. For \( 2x^3+3x^2+ax+b \) the three zeros sum to \( -\frac{3}{2} \), so the third zero is \( -\frac{3}{2}-(-3)-2 = -\frac{1}{2} \). That makes \( f(x) = 2(x+3)(x-2)\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right) = (x+3)(x-2)(2x+1) \); expanding gives \( 2x^3+3x^2-11x-6 \), so \( a = -11 \) (and \( b = -6 \), matching the labelled y-intercept).
questions.note: Depends on the graph: the cubic is drawn with x-intercepts labelled -3 and 2, a third unlabelled crossing between them, and y-intercept -6.
questions.imageAlt: The xy-plane showing a single cubic curve labelled y = f(x); two of its x-axis crossings and its y-intercept are marked with values on the axes.

questions.stem: If \(\frac{j}{k} = 62\) and \(\frac{96j}{12xk} = 62\), what is the value of \(x\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Separate the constants from the ratio: \(\frac{96j}{12xk} = \frac{96}{12x} \cdot \frac{j}{k} = \frac{8}{x} \cdot 62\). Setting that equal to 62 gives \(\frac{8}{x} = 1\), so \(x = 8\). You never need \(j\) or \(k\) individually.

whyWrong.A: \(\frac{1}{8}\) is the reciprocal — it solves \(8x = 1\) instead of \(\frac{8}{x} = 1\).
whyWrong.B: \(\frac{6}{31}\) comes from dividing 12 by 62 and simplifying; the 62s cancel and never enter the answer.
whyWrong.D: 96 uses only the numerator's constant and ignores the 12 in the denominator.

questions.stem: A baker has a total of 15 cups of flour and enough other ingredients to make banana pancakes and apple pancakes. The baker needs 1.25 cups of flour for a batch of banana pancakes and 0.75 cups of flour for a batch of apple pancakes. If the baker makes 8 batches of banana pancakes, what is the greatest number of whole batches of apple pancakes the baker can make?
questions.whyCorrect: The banana batches use \(8 \times 1.25 = 10\) cups, leaving \(15 - 10 = 5\) cups. Dividing, \(5 \div 0.75 = 6.\overline{6}\), and the question asks for whole batches, so round down to 6 — there is not enough flour for a seventh.

whyWrong.B: This rounds \(6.\overline{6}\) up. A seventh batch needs 5.25 cups and only 5 are left.
whyWrong.C: 8 is the number of banana batches, not apple batches.
whyWrong.D: This is roughly \(\frac{15 - 8}{0.75}\) — you subtracted the number of batches instead of the flour they use.

choices.content:
x51015
y840

questions.whyCorrect: Substitute one x-value and see which table survives. At x = 0: −4y = −20, so y = 5. Two tables start at x = 0, and only one of those pairs it with 5. Confirm the rest: at x = 4, 20 − 4y = −20 gives y = 10, and at x = 8, y = 15.

whyWrong.B: The x-values are right but the y-values run backwards. The coefficient of x is positive and of y is negative, so y increases as x increases.
whyWrong.C: Testing x = 5, y = 0 gives 25, not −20. This table has the pairs from choice A with the roles of x and y swapped.
whyWrong.D: Testing x = 5, y = 8 gives 25 − 32 = −7, not −20. The columns are swapped and reversed.

questions.stem: In a set of three consecutive integers, where the integers are ordered from least to greatest, the first integer is represented by \(x\). The sum of 4 and the second integer is less than the product of 17 and the third integer. Which inequality represents this situation?
questions.whyCorrect: If the first integer is \(x\), the second is \(x+1\) and the third is \(x+2\). “The sum of 4 and the second” is \(4+(x+1)\); “the product of 17 and the third” is \(17(x+2)\); and “is less than” points the symbol from the first expression to the second.

whyWrong.A: The terms are right but the inequality is reversed — “is less than” means \(<\).
whyWrong.C: This treats \(x+2\) as the second integer and \(x+3\) as the third, shifting the whole set by one, and reverses the symbol.
whyWrong.D: Correct symbol, but the second and third integers are again labelled one too high.

questions.stem:
8x + 7y = 58
8x + 21y = 142

The solution to the system is \((x, y)\). What is the value of 14y?
questions.whyCorrect: The \(x\) terms are identical, so subtract the first equation from the second: \(21y - 7y = 142 - 58\), which is exactly \(14y = 84\). The question asks for \(14y\), so you are already done — no need to find \(y\) or \(x\).

whyWrong.A: 2 is a plausible-looking small number but neither \(y\) nor \(14y\); here \(y = 6\).
whyWrong.B: 6 is the value of \(y\). Multiply by 14 as the question asks.
whyWrong.D: This is \(142 + 58\) — you added the equations instead of subtracting, which does not eliminate \(x\).

questions.stem:
\[ m(t)=-0.0274\left(\frac{t}{7}\right)^2+7.3873\left(\frac{t}{7}\right)+75.032 \]
The function \(m\) gives the predicted body mass \(m(t)\), in kilograms (kg), of a male giraffe \(t\) days after it was born in a wildlife reserve, where \(t\le 390\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of the statement “\(m(140)\) is approximately equal to 212” in this context?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The predicted body mass of a male giraffe was approximately 140 kg 212 days after it was born.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The predicted body mass of a male giraffe was approximately 212 kg 140 days after it was born.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The predicted body mass of a male giraffe was approximately 212 kg \(\frac{140}{7}\) days after it was born.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The predicted body mass of a male giraffe was approximately \(\frac{140}{7}\) kg 212 days after it was born.

questions.whyCorrect: The stem defines \(t\) as days and \(m(t)\) as kilograms, so the number in the parentheses is the time and the number it equals is the mass: 212 kg at 140 days. The \(\frac{t}{7}\) inside the formula converts days to weeks internally — it does not change what the input \(t\) means.

whyWrong.A: The two numbers are swapped: 140 is the time, 212 the mass.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{140}{7}=20\) is the number of weeks the model works with internally, but the input is still 140 days.
whyWrong.D: Both errors at once — the numbers swapped and the internal division applied to the reported value.

questions.stem: To estimate the proportion of a population that has a certain characteristic, a random sample was selected from the population. Based on the sample, it is estimated that the proportion of the population that has the characteristic is 0.2, with an associated margin of error of 0.08. Based on this estimate and margin of error, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion about the proportion of the population that has the characteristic?

choices.label: A
choices.content: It is plausible that the proportion is between 0.12 and 0.28.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It is plausible that the proportion is less than 0.12.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It is plausible that the proportion is greater than 0.28.

questions.whyCorrect: Subtract and add the margin of error to the estimate: 0.2 − 0.08 = 0.12 and 0.2 + 0.08 = 0.28. Everything inside that interval is plausible; everything outside it is not supported by the sample.

whyWrong.B: 0.12 is the bottom end of the plausible interval, so proportions below it are the ones the estimate argues against.
whyWrong.C: 0.2 is a sample estimate, not a measurement of the whole population. If it were exact there would be no reason to report a margin of error.
whyWrong.D: 0.28 is the top end of the interval, so values above it fall outside the plausible range.

questions.stem: In right triangle ABC, angles A and B are acute, side AC has a length of 21.7, and \( \tan B = \frac{1}{8} \). What is the length of side BC, rounded to the nearest tenth?
questions.whyCorrect: If A and B are the acute angles, the right angle is at C, so AC and BC are the two legs. Relative to angle B, side AC is opposite and BC is adjacent, so \( \tan B = \frac{AC}{BC} = \frac{1}{8} \). That makes BC eight times AC: \( BC = 8(21.7) = 173.6 \).

whyWrong.A: 470.9 is 21.7 times 21.7, multiplying the side by itself instead of by 8.
whyWrong.C: 4.7 comes from taking the square root of 21.7, which no relationship here calls for.
whyWrong.D: 2.7 is 21.7 divided by 8 — the ratio applied upside down. Since tan B is less than 1, the side opposite B is the shorter one, so BC must be larger than AC, not smaller.

questions.stem: If \(\frac{42}{x} = 7x\), what is the value of \(7x^{2}\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Multiply both sides by \(x\): \(42 = 7x^{2}\). That is exactly what the question asks for, so the answer is 42 — there is no need to find \(x\) itself.

whyWrong.A: 6 is the value of \(x^{2}\), one factor of 7 short of what was asked.
whyWrong.B: 7 is just the coefficient in the expression, not its value.
whyWrong.D: 294 is \(42 \times 7\); the 7 is already included once you multiply \(\frac{42}{x}=7x\) by \(x\).

questions.stem: The edge length, in inches, of cube \(Y\) is \(\frac{3}{86}\) the edge length, in inches, of cube \(X\). The surface area, in square inches, of cube \(Y\) is n times the surface area, in square inches, of cube \(X\). What is the value of n?
questions.whyCorrect: Surface area is made of squares of the edge, so scaling every edge by a factor scales the area by that factor squared: \(n = \left(\frac{3}{86}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{7396}\). Square the denominator too — \(86^2 = 7{,}396\).

whyWrong.B: This cubes the numerator but not the denominator. Cubing is for volume, and it would have to apply to both parts of the fraction.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{3}{86}\) is the edge ratio, which still has to be squared for areas.
whyWrong.D: This squares the numerator but only doubles the denominator, halving \(86^2\) incorrectly.

questions.stem:
The table shows the frequency of values in a data set.
ValueFrequency
206
261
326
383
What is the minimum value of the data set?
questions.whyCorrect: Only the Value column contains data; the Frequency column says how many copies of each value there are. The smallest number in the Value column is 20, and it appears 6 times, so the minimum is 20.

whyWrong.A: 1 is the smallest frequency, the number of times 26 occurs.
whyWrong.B: 6 is a frequency, not a value.
whyWrong.D: 26 is in the data set but 20 is smaller.

questions.stem: Scientists collected fallen acorns that each housed a colony of the ant species P. ohioensis and analyzed each colony's structure. For any of these colonies, if the colony has x worker ants, the equation y = 0.67x + 2.6, where 20 ≤ x ≤ 110, gives the predicted number of larvae y in the colony. If one of these colonies has 46 worker ants, which of the following is closest to the predicted number of larvae in the colony?
questions.whyCorrect: x is the number of worker ants, so substitute 46: y = 0.67(46) + 2.6 = 30.82 + 2.6 = 33.42. The closest choice is 33.

whyWrong.B: 49 is roughly 46 + 2.6 with the 0.67 ignored, treating the ant count as if it carried straight over.
whyWrong.C: 65 is about 46 ÷ 0.67 — dividing by the rate instead of multiplying by it. That would answer the reverse question, how many workers go with 46 larvae.
whyWrong.D: 150 is far outside the model's range for x = 46; no combination of the given numbers produces it.

questions.note: The book misprints the fourth choice's letter as C, so two choices are labelled C; the value 150 is transcribed here as D.

questions.stem: \[ x^{2} = 2{,}601 \] How many distinct real solutions does the given equation have?
questions.whyCorrect: Any positive number has two real square roots, one positive and one negative. Here \( x = 51 \) and \( x = -51 \) , since \( 51^{2} = 2{,}601 \) , so there are two distinct real solutions. You do not need the exact value of the root to answer, only that 2,601 is positive.

whyWrong.A: Zero solutions would need the right side to be negative, since no real number squares to a negative.
whyWrong.B: Exactly one happens only for \( x^{2} = 0 \) . Taking only the positive root is the usual reason for landing here.
whyWrong.D: An equation like this has at most two solutions; infinitely many would require an identity such as \( x^{2} = x^{2} \) .

questions.stem: For the linear function p, \( p(c) = -2 \) , where c is a constant, \( p(5) = 34 \) , and the slope of the graph of \( y = p(x) \) in the xy-plane is 6. For the linear function t, \( t(c) = -4 \) and \( t(6) = 52 \) . What is the slope of the graph of \( y = t(x) \) in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: You cannot find t's slope until you know c, and c comes from p. Using p's two points, \( \frac{34 - (-2)}{5 - c} = 6 \) , so \( 5 - c = 6 \) and \( c = -1 \) . Now t passes through \( (-1, -4) \) and (6, 52), giving slope \( \frac{52 - (-4)}{6 - (-1)} = \frac{56}{7} = 8 \) .

whyWrong.A: -1 is the value of c, the input the two functions share, not a slope.
whyWrong.B: 4 comes from an incorrect c. Check that \( 6(5 - c) = 36 \) gives \( c = -1 \) , not a positive value.
whyWrong.C: 6 is the slope of p. The two functions only share the input c; nothing forces them to have the same slope.

questions.stem: Which expression is a factor of \( 36x^{2}(x+12) - 36(x+12)^{3} \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Both terms share \( 36(x+12) \) , so factor it out: \( 36(x+12)\left[x^{2} - (x+12)^{2}\right] \) . The bracket is a difference of squares, \( \left(x-(x+12)\right)\left(x+(x+12)\right) = (-12)(2x+12) \) . So the expression equals \( -432(x+12)(2x+12) \) , and \( 2x + 12 \) is a factor. Expanding \( (x+12)^{3} \) is the slow route and is where most people lose the question.

whyWrong.A: This is \( -12(x-12) \) . The constant −12 does appear, but paired with \( x-12 \) , which is not one of the factors.
whyWrong.C: This is \( 6(x+1) \) , and \( x+1 \) never appears — the only linear pieces are \( x+12 \) and \( 2x+12 \) .
whyWrong.D: This is \( 24(x-6) \) ; \( x-6 \) is not a factor either.

questions.stem:
\[ x(kx - 40) = -8 \]

In the given equation, \(k\) is an integer constant. If the equation has two distinct real solutions, what is the greatest possible value of \(k\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Put it in standard form first: \(kx^2 - 40x + 8 = 0\). Two distinct real solutions means a strictly positive discriminant: \((-40)^2 - 4(k)(8) > 0\), so \(1600 - 32k > 0\) and \(k < 50\). The inequality is strict — at \(k = 50\) the discriminant is 0 and there is only one solution — so the greatest integer that works is \(k = 49\).

questions.stem: If \(2 + \frac{(1-x)}{2} = -\frac{2(1-x)}{3}\) , what is the value of \(1 - x\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Treat \(1 - x\) as a single unknown \(u\): \(2 + \frac{u}{2} = -\frac{2u}{3}\). Multiply every term by 6 to clear the denominators: \(12 + 3u = -4u\). Then \(7u = -12\), so \(1 - x = -\frac{12}{7}\).

questions.stem: A carpenter charges a flat rate of $234 for the first 3 hours of work and $65 for each additional hour of work. Which equation gives the total amount y, in dollars, that the carpenter charges for x hours of work, where x > 3?
questions.whyCorrect: The $234 covers the first 3 hours, and only the hours past the third are billed at $65, so there are x − 3 of them: y = 234 + 65(x − 3). Expanding gives 65x + 234 − 195 = 65x + 39. Check at x = 3: 195 + 39 = 234.

whyWrong.B: This multiplies the flat rate by every hour and adds one extra hour's fee. At x = 3 it gives 702 + 65 = $767 instead of $234.
whyWrong.C: This is the most tempting version, but it forgets that the flat $234 already paid for 3 hours. At x = 3 it gives 195 + 234 = $429 — you have been billed for those hours twice.
whyWrong.D: Both numbers are too large; at x = 3 it gives 702 + 429 = $1,131.

In B every \(y\) is smaller than its \(x\) (4<6, 5<7, 6<8), and each \(y\) clears \(-5x-10\), which is deeply negative for positive \(x\) (at \(x=6\) that bound is −40). One failing row rules a whole table out, so check the easier inequality first.

questions.stem: \[ q(x) = 12(3)^{x} \] Which table gives three values of \(x\) and their corresponding values of \(q(x)\) for function \(q\)?

choices.label: A
choices.content:
x\(-1\)01
q(x)41236

choices.label: B
choices.content:
x\(-1\)01
q(x)\(\frac{1}{4}\)1236

choices.label: C
choices.content:
x\(-1\)01
q(x)\(\frac{1}{4}\)336

choices.label: D
choices.content:
