q(x)\(-36\)036

questions.whyCorrect: Evaluate each input: \(q(-1) = 12 \cdot 3^{-1} = \frac{12}{3} = 4\), \(q(0) = 12 \cdot 1 = 12\), \(q(1) = 12 \cdot 3 = 36\). A negative exponent divides by the base once — it does not flip the sign of the output or invert the whole value.

whyWrong.B: \(q(-1)\) is 4, not \(\frac{1}{4}\); the reciprocal was taken of the whole output instead of just the power.
whyWrong.C: Two values are wrong: \(q(0) = 12\) (any base to the 0 is 1, times the coefficient 12), and \(q(-1) = 4\).
whyWrong.D: An exponential function with a positive coefficient is never 0 or negative, so \(q(0)=0\) and \(q(-1)=-36\) are impossible.

questions.stem: For the positive quantities \(h\), \(j\), and \(k\), 27% of \(h\) is the equivalent of 24% of \(j\), and \(j\) is equivalent to 45% of \(k\). What percentage of \(k\) is \(h\)? (Disregard the % sign when entering your answer. For example, if your answer is 39%, enter 39.)
questions.whyCorrect: The first sentence is \(0.27h = 0.24j\), so \(h = \frac{0.24}{0.27}j = \frac{8}{9}j\). The second is \(j = 0.45k\). Substituting, \(h = \frac{8}{9}(0.45k) = 0.4k\), so \(h\) is 40% of \(k\).
questions.note: Same template as this book's #24 with different percentages — do not place both in one test.

questions.stem: The expression \(72y^{5} - 48y^{4}\) is equivalent to \(ry^{4}(12y - 8)\), where \(r\) is a constant. What is the value of \(r\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Expand the target form: \(ry^{4}(12y-8) = 12ry^{5} - 8ry^{4}\). Matching the \(y^{5}\) terms gives \(12r = 72\), so \(r = 6\); the \(y^{4}\) terms confirm it, since \(8 \times 6 = 48\).

questions.stem:
\[ f(x)=-0.0038400x^2+15.236x-15{,}103 \]
The model shown gives the predicted average Arctic sea ice area \(f(x)\), in millions of square kilometers, for September of each year \(x\), where \(x\) represents a year and \(1979\le x\le 2012\). Based on the model, what is the positive difference, in millions of square kilometers, between the predicted average Arctic sea ice area for September of the year 1991 and the predicted average Arctic sea ice area for September of the year 1992? (Round your answer to the nearest thousandth.)
questions.whyCorrect: You can subtract before evaluating, which avoids losing precision in two large numbers. \(f(1992)-f(1991)=-0.00384\left(1992^2-1991^2\right)+15.236\), and \(1992^2-1991^2=(1992+1991)(1)=3983\). So the difference is \(-0.00384(3983)+15.236=-15.29472+15.236=-0.05872\), and the positive difference rounds to 0.059.

questions.stem: A rectangular banner has an area of 2,300 square inches. A copy of the banner is made in which the length and width of the original banner are each increased by 20%. What is the area of the copy, in square inches?
questions.whyCorrect: Each dimension is multiplied by 1.20, so the area — a product of the two dimensions — is multiplied by \(1.20^{2} = 1.44\). That gives 2,300 × 1.44 = 3,312 square inches.

whyWrong.A: This adds 20 to the area once, treating the percent as a fixed number of square inches.
whyWrong.B: This adds 20 twice, once per dimension. Percent increases multiply the area, they do not add to it.
whyWrong.C: \(2{,}300 \times 1.20 = 2{,}760\) increases the area by 20%. But it is each dimension that grows by 20%, so the factor 1.20 applies twice.

questions.stem: The manager of a gym selected a sample of 139 members at random to estimate the percentage of the gym's members that would continue to pay for a membership if the price increased. From the survey, the manager estimates that 82% of the gym's members would continue to pay for membership if the price increased, with an associated margin of error of 6.39%. If the survey is repeated with a random sample of 278 members and the results are calculated in the same way, which of the following will be the most likely effect of using the larger random sample compared to the smaller random sample?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The margin of error will be lower

choices.label: B
choices.content: The margin of error will be higher

choices.label: C
choices.content: The estimate of the percentage of the gym's members that would continue to pay for a membership if the price increased will be lower

choices.label: D
choices.content: The estimate of the percentage of the gym's members that would continue to pay for a membership if the price increased will be higher

questions.whyCorrect: Surveying more people gives a more precise estimate, and precision is exactly what the margin of error measures. Doubling the sample from 139 to 278 therefore shrinks the margin of error. Note the direction: bigger sample, smaller margin.

whyWrong.B: This is the relationship inverted. Small samples are the unreliable ones, so they carry the larger margins of error.
whyWrong.C: A larger sample changes how precise the estimate is, not which way it points. There is no reason for the percentage itself to fall.
whyWrong.D: Same reason — the estimate could come out slightly higher or slightly lower, so neither direction is "most likely". Only the margin of error has a predictable direction.

questions.stem:
10x = 110
8x - 86 = y

The solution to the given system of equations is \((x, y)\). What is the value of \(y\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The first equation gives \(x = 11\). Substituting into the second, \(y = 8(11) - 86 = 88 - 86 = 2\).

whyWrong.A: 86 is the constant subtracted in the second equation, not \(y\).
whyWrong.B: 11 is the value of \(x\).
whyWrong.C: 10 is the coefficient in the first equation.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = 5^{x} + 3 \] If the given function \(f\) is graphed in the xy-plane, where \(y = f(x)\), what is the y-intercept of the graph?
questions.whyCorrect: The y-intercept is the value at \(x = 0\). Any nonzero base to the power 0 is 1, so \(f(0) = 5^{0} + 3 = 1 + 3 = 4\), giving \((0, 4)\).

whyWrong.A: This treats \(5^{0}\) as 0. An exponential term is never 0; at \(x=0\) it equals 1.
whyWrong.C: This reads off the base 5 instead of evaluating the function.
whyWrong.D: This treats \(5^{0}\) as 5, adding the base itself rather than 1.

questions.stem: The length of each side of triangle \(A\) is 270 millimeters. The length of each side of triangle \(B\) is double the length of each side of triangle \(A\). What is the length, in millimeters, of each side of triangle \(B\)?
questions.whyCorrect: "Double" means multiply by 2, so each side of triangle \(B\) is \(2 \times 270 = 540\) millimeters.

whyWrong.A: This leaves the length unchanged.
whyWrong.B: This adds 2 rather than multiplying by 2.
whyWrong.D: This doubles twice (multiplies by 4).

questions.stem:
28, 28, 29, 30, 32, 33, 37

What is the mean of the data set shown?
questions.whyCorrect: Add all seven values and divide by 7: 28 + 28 + 29 + 30 + 32 + 33 + 37 = 217, and 217 ÷ 7 = 31. The repeated 28 counts twice.

whyWrong.A: 28 is the mode and the minimum, not the mean.
whyWrong.B: 30 is the median, the fourth value in the ordered list. The two larger values 33 and 37 pull the mean above it.
whyWrong.D: 37 is the maximum value.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = 5x + b \]For the linear function \(f\), b is a constant and \(f(7) = 35\). What is the value of b?
questions.whyCorrect: Substitute x = 7 and set the result equal to 35: 5(7) + b = 35, so 35 + b = 35 and b = 0. A constant of 0 is a legitimate answer — it just means the line passes through the origin.

whyWrong.B: 1 would make f(7) = 36. Check by substituting back.
whyWrong.C: 5 is the slope, already accounted for by the 5x term.
whyWrong.D: 7 is the input value, not the constant; it is what you substitute for x.

questions.stem: \[9x+x=7x+x+9\]Which of the following equations has the same solution as the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Combine like terms on each side: the left is \(10x\) and the right is \(8x+9\). Subtracting \(8x\) from both sides leaves \(2x=9\), which has the same solution \(x=4.5\).

whyWrong.A: 16 comes from adding the \(x\) terms across the equals sign instead of subtracting, and the sign is wrong as well.
whyWrong.B: Same error — the \(x\) terms must be subtracted from one side, not added together.
whyWrong.D: This is an expression, not an equation, so it has no solution to compare.

questions.note: Choice D is printed as “2x − 9” with no equals sign, so it is an expression rather than an equation. Presumably intended as 2x = −9.

questions.stem: Circle N has a radius of 6 millimeters (mm). Circle M has an area of \(121\pi\) mm<sup>2</sup>. What is the total area, in mm<sup>2</sup>, of circles N and M?
questions.whyCorrect: Circle N's area is \(\pi(6)^{2} = 36\pi\). Circle M's area is handed to you as \(121\pi\), so its radius of 11 never has to be found. The total is \(36\pi + 121\pi = 157\pi\).

whyWrong.A: This adds the radii, 6 + 11, and attaches \(\pi\). Areas do not add that way.
whyWrong.B: This adds circle N's circumference, \(12\pi\), to circle M's area instead of adding two areas.
whyWrong.C: This adds \(24\pi\) to \(121\pi\); \(24\pi\) is twice circle N's circumference, still not its area.

questions.stem: Sabrina has a goal to save at least 240 USD. Sabrina has already saved 180 USD. If x represents the additional amount of money, in dollars, Sabrina needs to save to meet her goal, which inequality represents this situation?
questions.whyCorrect: The money she ends up with is what she already has plus what she still saves, so the total is 180 + x. Her goal is "at least" 240, which makes 240 a lower bound.

whyWrong.A: Dividing by 180 does not describe adding to savings; it would require x to be over 43,000 dollars.
whyWrong.B: Multiplying the two amounts is not how savings accumulate. Additional savings are added to the existing balance.
whyWrong.D: Subtracting x means spending rather than saving, and it can never reach 240 starting from 180.

questions.stem: Jasmin grows bean pods in her garden. This year, she harvested 330 bean pods and saved 10% of them to plant next year. How many of the harvested bean pods did Jasmin save to plant next year?
questions.whyCorrect: 10% of a number is that number divided by 10: \(330 \div 10 = 33\). Equivalently 0.10 × 330 = 33.

whyWrong.A: 23 is \(33-10\); you found 10% and then subtracted 10 again.
whyWrong.C: 41 does not follow from any correct step here; 10% of 330 must end in a 3 because 330 divided by 10 is exact.
whyWrong.D: 43 is \(33+10\), adding the percent number on top of the correct answer.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by \[ f(x) = -5x^{2} - 7. \] What is the value of \( f(-1) \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Square before applying the minus sign in front: \( (-1)^{2} = 1 \) , so \( -5(1) - 7 = -5 - 7 = -12 \) . The negative input disappears in the squaring, so the -5 stays negative.

whyWrong.B: -2 comes from \( 5 - 7 \) , which happens if you let the input's minus sign survive the squaring and turn \( -5x^{2} \) into +5.
whyWrong.C: 2 is \( 7 - 5 \) , the same slip with the subtraction also reversed.
whyWrong.D: 12 has the correct size but the wrong sign; both terms here are negative, so the result cannot be positive.

questions.stem: The graph of \( y = a(x+1)(x-5) \) is shown in the xy-plane above, where \(a\) is a constant. If the graph with vertex \( (h,k) \) intersects the y-axis at point \( (0,5) \), which of the following is equal to \(k\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Find \(a\) from the given point: substituting \( (0,5) \) gives \( a(1)(-5) = 5 \), so \( a = -1 \). The vertex sits halfway between the zeros \(-1\) and 5, at \( h = 2 \). Then \( k = -(2+1)(2-5) = -(3)(-3) = 9 \).

whyWrong.A: 7 does not come from any consistent value of \(a\); with \( a = -1 \) the vertex height is fixed at 9.
whyWrong.B: 8 would be the vertex value if the zeros were \(-1\) and 5 with \( a \approx -0.89 \); the point \( (0,5) \) pins \( a = -1 \) exactly.
whyWrong.D: 10 is the result of using \( h = 2 \) but computing \( k \) as \( 5+5 \), adding the y-intercept to itself instead of evaluating the function at the vertex.

questions.note: The graph is shown in the book (downward parabola through (-1,0), (5,0) and (0,5) with vertex labelled (h,k)), but every number needed is stated in the text.
questions.imageAlt: A downward-opening parabola drawn in the xy-plane, crossing the x-axis at two labelled points, meeting the y-axis at a marked point, and with its vertex labelled (h, k).

questions.stem: In the xy-plane above, the graph of a quadratic function \( y = f(x) \) intersects the x-axis at points \(O\) and \(Q\), and has a vertex at point \(P\). If line \( \ell \) passes through points \(P\) and \(Q\), what is the y-intercept of line \( \ell \)?
questions.whyCorrect: \(O\) is the origin, so one zero is \( x=0 \), and the vertex \( P(3,5) \) sits halfway between the zeros — that puts \(Q\) at \( (6,0) \). The line through \( (3,5) \) and \( (6,0) \) has slope \( \frac{0-5}{6-3} = -\frac{5}{3} \). Going from \( P \) back to \( x=0 \) is 3 more units left, raising \(y\) by another 5, so the y-intercept is \( 5+5 = 10 \).
questions.note: Depends on the graph: the parabola through the origin and (6,0) with vertex labelled P(3,5), and line l drawn through P and Q.
questions.imageAlt: An xy-plane showing a downward-opening parabola that meets the x-axis at the origin and at one labelled point, together with a straight line drawn through the parabola's labelled vertex and that x-intercept; the y-axis carries numbered tick marks.

questions.stem: In the xy-plane, the graph of function f, where y = f(x), has exactly 8 x-intercepts. One of these x-intercepts is (17, 0). The rational function g is defined by \[ g(x) = \frac{f(x)}{x - 17}. \]In the xy-plane, how many x-intercepts does the graph of y = g(x) have?
questions.whyCorrect: At each of the other 7 zeros of f the numerator is 0 while the denominator x - 17 is not, so g is 0 there and each stays an x-intercept. At x = 17 the denominator is 0, so g is undefined — there is no point on the graph at all, which means that intercept is lost rather than kept. That leaves 8 - 1 = 7.

questions.stem:
\[ \sqrt{k - x} = 32 - x \]

In the given equation, \(k\) is a constant. The equation has exactly one real solution. What is the minimum possible value of \(4k\)?
questions.whyCorrect: A square root cannot be negative, so any solution needs \(32 - x \ge 0\). Substitute \(u = 32 - x\) with \(u \ge 0\); squaring gives \(k - x = u^2\), so \(k = u^2 + x = u^2 - u + 32\). Count how many \(u \ge 0\) produce a given \(k\): the parabola bottoms out at \(u = \tfrac{1}{2}\) with \(k = 31.75\), and equals 32 at \(u = 0\). So exactly one allowed \(u\) occurs at \(k = 31.75\) or for \(k > 32\), and the smallest of those is \(31.75\), giving \(4k = 127\).
questions.note: Same template as this book's Quadratics #79 (which uses 57 instead of 32) — do not place both in the same test.

questions.stem: A juice mixture has a total volume of 125 liters and is 45% juice by volume. The mixture was created by mixing two different solutions (solution A and solution B). Solution A was 24% juice by volume. Solution B was 64% juice by volume. The volume, in liters, of juice in solution A is equal to a. The volume, in liters, of juice in solution B is equal to b. The numbers a, b, and p are all positive constants. If a is p% less than b, what is the value of p? (Round your answer to the nearest hundredth)
questions.whyCorrect: Let x be the liters of solution A. The juice balances: \(0.24x + 0.64(125 - x) = 0.45(125) = 56.25\), which gives \(0.4x = 23.75\) and \(x = 59.375\) liters of A, leaving 65.625 liters of B. So \(a = 0.24(59.375) = 14.25\) and \(b = 0.64(65.625) = 42\). "a is p% less than b" compares the gap to b: \(p = \frac{42 - 14.25}{42}(100) \approx 66.07\).

questions.stem: The expression \( \frac{\sqrt[7]{p^{5}}}{\sqrt{p^{t+3}}} \) , where t is a constant, is equivalent to \( \sqrt[7]{p^{2}} \) for all positive values of p. What is the value of t?
questions.whyCorrect: Convert every radical to a fractional exponent: the expression is \( p^{5/7} \div p^{(t+3)/2} = p^{\frac{5}{7} - \frac{t+3}{2}} \) , and the target is \( p^{2/7} \) . Setting the exponents equal gives \( \frac{5}{7} - \frac{t+3}{2} = \frac{2}{7} \) , so \( \frac{t+3}{2} = \frac{3}{7} \) and \( t + 3 = \frac{6}{7} \) . Therefore \( t = \frac{6}{7} - 3 = -\frac{15}{7} \) . The step people miss is that the square root halves the whole exponent \( t + 3 \) , not just t.

whyWrong.B: \( -\frac{27}{7} \) results from subtracting 3 twice, or from halving after subtracting instead of before.
whyWrong.C: \( -\frac{24}{7} \) comes from using \( t + 3 = -3 \) , i.e. dropping the \( \frac{6}{7} \) .
whyWrong.D: \( -\frac{18}{7} \) comes from setting \( \frac{t+3}{2} = \frac{3}{7} \) but then forgetting to double before subtracting 3.

questions.stem:
For triangles PQR and KLM, the angles Q and L are equivalent and \(PR = \frac{3}{4}KM\). Which of the following information is enough to claim that PQR and KLM are similar?
I. The length of PQ is \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the length of KL.
II. The length of LM is \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the length of QR.
questions.whyCorrect: Angle Q sits between QP and QR, while PR is the side opposite it. Statement I adds PQ, so you have an angle plus one adjacent side plus the opposite side — that is SSA, which does not fix a triangle's shape (e.g. \(\angle Q = 30^\circ\), \(PQ = 10\), \(PR = 6\) allows \(QR \approx 11.98\) or \(QR \approx 5.34\), and KLM may take either shape scaled up). Statement II runs the ratio the wrong way: the given \(PR = \frac{3}{4}KM\) makes PQR the smaller triangle, but \(LM = \frac{3}{4}QR\) makes KLM the smaller one, so it actually rules similarity out. Neither statement establishes it.

whyWrong.A: Statement I is the ambiguous SSA case — the equal angle is not between the two sides whose ratio you know, so two differently shaped triangles satisfy it.
whyWrong.B: Adding II makes things worse, not better: its ratio contradicts the given \(PR = \frac{3}{4}KM\), so the two statements together describe triangles that cannot be similar.
whyWrong.C: Statement II alone gives \(\frac{LM}{QR} = \frac{3}{4}\) while the stem gives \(\frac{PR}{KM} = \frac{3}{4}\); those point in opposite directions, so no common scale factor exists.

questions.note: Disagreement with the obvious 'consistent ratio' reading is likely: statement I looks sufficient until you notice the known angle is not included between the two known sides. Question 96 in the same book turns on exactly this SSA point.

questions.stem: A set of five consecutive even integers is ordered from least to greatest. The sum of the first and fourth even integers is 5,860% more than the quotient of the fifth even integer and 30. The first even integer is p% less than the fifth even integer, where p is a constant. What is the value of p?
questions.whyCorrect: Call the integers \(n, n+2, n+4, n+6, n+8\). The first and fourth sum to \(2n+6\), and the quotient of the fifth and 30 is \(\frac{n+8}{30}\). "5,860% more than" means 59.6 times as much, not 58.6 times: \(2n+6=59.6\cdot\frac{n+8}{30}\). Multiplying by 30 gives \(60n+180=59.6n+476.8\), so \(0.4n=296.8\) and n = 742, making the fifth integer 750. Check: 742 + 748 = 1,490 and \(59.6\times 25=1{,}490\). Finally, \(p=\frac{750-742}{750}\times 100=\frac{800}{750}=\frac{16}{15}\), about 1.07.
questions.note: The answer is 16/15, roughly 1.0667 - an unusually small and untidy value for a grid-in, though it is exactly what the stated numbers give.

questions.stem:
\[ -(3x - 7)^2 = p + 16 \]

In the equation, \(p\) is an integer constant. The equation has no real solution. What is the least possible value of \(p\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The left side is the negative of a square, so it is at most 0, and it does reach 0 when \(x = \tfrac{7}{3}\). A real solution therefore exists exactly when \(p + 16 \le 0\). For no real solution you need \(p + 16 > 0\), that is \(p > -16\). The least integer strictly greater than \(-16\) is \(-15\).

whyWrong.A: At \(p = -18\) the right side is \(-2\), and \(-(3x-7)^2 = -2\) does have real solutions \(\left(3x - 7 = \pm\sqrt{2}\right)\).
whyWrong.B: At \(p = -17\) the right side is \(-1\), which the left side reaches; there are real solutions.
whyWrong.C: This is the boundary case. At \(p = -16\) the right side is 0 and \(x = \tfrac{7}{3}\) is a real solution, so \(-16\) must be excluded.

questions.stem: Right triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle with angle B = 90 degrees, BC > AB, and AC is a diameter of the circle. BD is perpendicular to AC with point D on AC. AC = 113 and \(BD = \sqrt{222}\). What is the ratio of CD/AD?
questions.whyCorrect: The altitude to the hypotenuse satisfies \(BD^2 = AD \cdot DC\), so \(AD \cdot DC = 222\), and \(AD + DC = AC = 113\). Those two facts make AD and DC the roots of \(t^2 - 113t + 222 = 0\), which factor to \(t = 2\) and \(t = 111\). Because \(BC > AB\), the longer piece is on C's side, so \(DC = 111\), \(AD = 2\), and the ratio is \(\frac{111}{2}\).

whyWrong.B: This is \(\frac{AD}{CD}\) — the ratio upside down. The condition \(BC > AB\) is what tells you 111 goes with C.
whyWrong.C: This mixes the altitude into the ratio. \(\sqrt{222}\) is BD; the ratio asked for involves only the two pieces of the hypotenuse.
whyWrong.D: 111 is the length CD itself, not the ratio \(\frac{CD}{AD}\); dividing by \(AD = 2\) is still required.

questions.stem: A digital marketing agency has three groups of clients. The first group consists of 8 clients who are charged a monthly fee of at least $170 but no more than $190. The second group consists of 11 clients who are charged a monthly fee of at least $200 but no more than $230. The third group consists of 21 clients who are charged a monthly fee of at least $240 but no more than $300. If a new client who is charged a monthly fee of $250 is added to the third group, what will be the effect on the mean monthly fee charged by the agency?

choices.label: C
choices.content: The mean will remain the same.

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is not enough information to determine how the mean will change.

questions.whyCorrect: Adding one value pushes the mean up if that value is above the current mean and down if it is below, so the question is where $250 sits. Only ranges are given, so bound the current mean: the smallest possible total is \(8(170)+11(200)+21(240) = 8600\), a mean of $215, and the largest is \(8(190)+11(230)+21(300) = 10350\), a mean of $258.75. Since $250 lies inside $215 to $258.75, the mean could rise or fall depending on the actual fees.

whyWrong.A: True only if the current mean is below $250. It can be as high as $258.75, in which case adding a $250 client lowers it.
whyWrong.B: True only if the current mean is above $250, which is equally not guaranteed — it can be as low as $215.
whyWrong.C: This needs the current mean to be exactly $250, one particular case out of many.

questions.stem:
\[ g(x) = \frac{1}{11}\left(6(2)^{x} + 7\right) \]

The function g is defined by the given equation. For all values of x, the value of g(x) is greater than k, where k is a constant. What is the greatest possible value of k?
questions.whyCorrect: As x becomes very negative, \( 2^{x} \) shrinks toward 0 without ever reaching it, so \( 6(2)^{x} + 7 \) stays just above 7. Dividing by 11, g(x) stays just above \( \frac{7}{11} \) and can be made as close to it as you like, so the largest constant the function always exceeds is \( \frac{7}{11} \) .

whyWrong.A: 0 is a value g(x) always exceeds, but it is not the greatest such value - \( \frac{7}{11} \) is larger and still works.
whyWrong.B: \( \frac{13}{11} \) uses 6 + 7 = 13, which assumes \( 2^{x} = 1 \) ; that is only the value at x = 0, not the limit.
whyWrong.D: 7 forgets the division by 11; g(0) is already only about 1.18, well below 7.

questions.stem: In the diagram, OB = OA, AB = BC, the measure of angle FAO is 30°, DE is parallel to AC, and AB = 58. What is the length of BE?
questions.whyCorrect: Put F at the origin with A = (-a, 0), C = (a, 0), B = (0, b) and O = (0, t) on BF. Angle FAO = 30° gives \(t=\frac{a}{\sqrt{3}}\), and OA = OB gives \(a^{2}+t^{2}=(b-t)^{2}\), i.e. \(t=\frac{b^{2}-a^{2}}{2b}\). Setting those equal reduces to \(\tan 2\varphi=-\sqrt{3}\) for the base angle \(\varphi\) at A, so \(\varphi = 60^{\circ}\) and the triangle is in fact equilateral with every side 58. Then \(a = 29\), \(b=29\sqrt{3}\) and \(t=\frac{29}{\sqrt{3}}\), which is one third of the way up from AC to B. Since DE is parallel to AC, E sits two thirds of the way down BC from B, so \(BE=\frac{2}{3}(58)=\frac{116}{3}\).

whyWrong.B: 29 is half of 58, the answer if you assume O is the midpoint of BF and so E the midpoint of BC. O is one third of the way up, not halfway.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{87}{2}=\frac{3}{4}(58)\), which comes from placing DE a quarter of the way down from B rather than two thirds.
whyWrong.D: 58 is the whole of BC. E is an interior point of that side, so BE must be shorter.

questions.note: Figure needed: triangle ABC with B at the top, A at the lower left and C at the lower right. A vertical segment BF runs from B to F on AC. O lies on BF, and the horizontal segment DE through O meets AB at D and BC at E. Segment AO is also drawn from A to O. All of D, E, F and O exist only in the figure.
questions.imageAlt: A triangle A B C with apex B at the top; a vertical segment runs from B to a point F on AC, a horizontal segment DE crosses it at O with D on AB and E on BC, and a segment is drawn from A to O.

questions.stem: A chemist mixed x liters of a 2% saline solution with y liters of a 5% saline solution to produce a 3% saline solution. Which equation best represents this situation? (Assume the volumes of the solutions are additive.)
questions.whyCorrect: Track the salt, not the solution. The two sources contribute \(0.02x\) and \(0.05y\) liters of salt, and the mixture has volume \(x + y\) at 3%, so it holds \(0.03(x+y)\) liters of salt. Setting the salt in equal to the salt out gives choice B. Convert each percent to a decimal by dividing by 100: 2% is 0.02, not 0.2.

whyWrong.A: The right side uses 3 instead of 0.03, so it claims the mixture is 300% salt — three times more salt than there is liquid.
whyWrong.C: Both sides are wrong: the left uses 20% and 50% and the right uses 300%.
whyWrong.D: Every percent here is ten times too large (20%, 50%, 30%). It happens to be choice B multiplied through by 10, so it has the same solutions, but it does not represent the stated concentrations.

questions.note: DEFECT: choice D is exactly choice B with both sides multiplied by 10, so the two equations have identical solution sets. B is the literal translation of the percentages; D is arithmetically equivalent.

questions.stem: Which equation has no solution?
questions.whyCorrect: Expand the right side of each choice and compare. In C, 9(7x + 16) = 63x + 144, so the equation says 63x + 360 = 63x + 144. The x terms cancel and leave 360 = 144, which is false, so nothing solves it.

whyWrong.A: 9(7x + 4) = 63x + 36, exactly the left side, so every x works — infinitely many solutions.
whyWrong.B: The coefficients 63 and 7 differ, so the x terms survive: 56x = 0 and x = 0.
whyWrong.D: The coefficients are 63 and −63, which differ, so there is one solution, \( x = -\frac{102}{126} \).

questions.stem:
The table gives the number of hours, \(h\), of labor and a plumber’s total charge \(f(h)\), in dollars, for two different jobs.
hf(h)
1125
3225
There is a linear relationship between \(h\) and \(f(h)\). Which equation represents this relationship?
questions.whyCorrect: The hourly rate is \(\frac{225-125}{3-1}=50\) dollars per hour. Substituting the 1-hour job gives \(125=50+b\), so the fixed charge is \$75 and \(f(h)=50h+75\).

whyWrong.A: It fits the 1-hour job but gives \$175 at 3 hours; all four choices agree at \(h=1\), so the second row is the test.
whyWrong.B: At 3 hours this gives \$325.
whyWrong.D: At 3 hours this gives \$275; the rate and the fixed fee have been swapped.

questions.note: Same template as this section’s question 5 (plumber charge table) with 125/225 in place of 120/220 — dedupe candidate if both are used in one test.

questions.stem:
y < x
y > −4x − 9
For which of the following tables are all the values of \(x\) and their corresponding values of \(y\) solutions to the given system of inequalities?
