questions.whyCorrect: The mean of a frequency table is \(\frac{\sum (\text{value} \times \text{frequency})}{\sum \text{frequency}}\). Choice A gives \(\frac{30+80+150+240}{18} = \frac{500}{18} \approx 27.8\), while the other three all work out to exactly 25. A is the only table whose frequencies rise with the values, which is what pulls its mean above the midpoint 25.

whyWrong.B: \(\frac{550}{22} = 25\). The frequencies are symmetric (7, 4, 4, 7), so the mean sits at the center of the values.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{500}{20} = 25\). Equal frequencies make the mean the plain average of 10, 20, 30, 40.
whyWrong.D: \(\frac{550}{22} = 25\). Again symmetric frequencies (6, 5, 5, 6) give the center value.

questions.stem:
The table below gives the number of hours, \(h\), of labor and a plumber’s total charge \(f(h)\), in dollars, for two different jobs.
Hours (h)Total charge f(h)
1120
3220
There is a linear relationship between \(h\) and \(f(h)\). Which equation represents this relationship?
questions.whyCorrect: The hourly rate is the slope: \(\frac{220-120}{3-1}=\frac{100}{2}=50\) dollars per hour. The fixed charge follows from either row: \(120=50(1)+b\) gives \(b=70\), so \(f(h)=50h+70\).

whyWrong.A: It matches the 1-hour job but gives \$160 for 3 hours instead of \$220 — every wrong choice here fits the first row, so you must test the second.
whyWrong.B: It also matches 1 hour but predicts \$320 at 3 hours.
whyWrong.D: It matches 1 hour and gives \$260 at 3 hours; the slope 70 is the fixed fee and the intercept 50 is the rate, swapped.

questions.stem: A hemisphere is half of a sphere. If a hemisphere has a radius of 50 inches, which of the following is closest to the volume, in cubic inches, of this hemisphere?
questions.whyCorrect: A sphere has volume \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), so a hemisphere is half of that: \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3\). With r = 50, \(r^3 = 125{,}000\), and \(\frac{2}{3}\pi(125{,}000) \approx 261{,}799\), closest to 261,800.

whyWrong.A: This is about \(2\pi r^2\) ÷ 3-ish, an area-sized quantity. Volume needs the radius cubed, not squared.
whyWrong.B: This is roughly \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^2 \times 4\); it still uses \(r^2\). Cubing 50 gives 125,000, which is far larger.
whyWrong.C: This is three quarters of the correct value, from using \(\frac{1}{2}\pi r^3\) instead of \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3\). Halving \(\frac{4}{3}\) gives \(\frac{2}{3}\), not \(\frac{1}{2}\).

questions.stem: A shopper is purchasing oranges that cost $0.67 each. If the shopper has a coupon for $2 off the entire purchase and there is no sales tax, which inequality represents the number of oranges, x, that the shopper can purchase for no more than $12?
questions.whyCorrect: The oranges cost 0.67x before the coupon, and the coupon takes $2 off that total, so the amount paid is 0.67x - 2. "No more than $12" caps it, giving \( 0.67x - 2 \le 12 \).

whyWrong.A: Adding 2 treats the coupon as a surcharge. A coupon reduces what is owed.
whyWrong.B: Two errors: the coupon is added instead of subtracted, and the inequality demands spending at least $12.
whyWrong.D: The expression is right but the direction is wrong — this requires the shopper to spend at least $12 rather than at most.

questions.stem: \[ g(x) = 2(16x - 17) \]What is the y-intercept of the graph of y = g(x) - 3 in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: A y-intercept is the output at x = 0, so evaluate the whole expression there. g(0) = 2(16 · 0 - 17) = 2(-17) = -34, and the graph is y = g(x) - 3, so the value is -34 - 3 = -37.

whyWrong.B: -34 is g(0) on its own. You still have to subtract the 3 that the equation y = g(x) - 3 applies.
whyWrong.C: -20 comes from subtracting 3 inside the bracket before doubling, or from -17 - 3 then doubling incorrectly. The 2 multiplies only what is inside the parentheses.
whyWrong.D: -17 is the constant inside the parentheses. It has not been doubled and the 3 has not been subtracted.

questions.stem:
The table summarizes the UV index value recorded by a research assistant at noon each day for 49 days.
UV indexNumber of days
19
215
312
413
According to the table, a UV index value of 1 was recorded on how many days?
questions.whyCorrect: Read the row whose UV index is 1 and take the value in the second column. That column counts days, so 9 days had a UV index of 1. No arithmetic is needed; the trap is reading the wrong column or adding rows together.

whyWrong.A: 4 is the largest UV index in the first column, not a count of days.
whyWrong.C: 40 is the total number of days for indexes 2, 3 and 4 combined — the days that were not index 1.
whyWrong.D: 49 is the total number of days observed, the sum of the whole second column.

questions.note: Book prints "Accordinhg"; corrected to "According".

questions.stem:
\[ f(x) = 4x^{2} + 56x + 197 \]

The function g is defined by g(x) = f(x + 6). What is the minimum value of g(x)?
questions.whyCorrect: Replacing x by x + 6 slides the parabola sideways; it does not move it up or down, so g has the same minimum value as f. Find f's minimum at its vertex, \( x = -\frac{56}{2(4)} = -7 \) : \( f(-7) = 4(49) - 392 + 197 = 1 \) . So the minimum value of g is 1.

whyWrong.A: −13 comes from shifting the vertex's x-coordinate (−7 − 6) and reporting that instead of the minimum output.
whyWrong.B: −7 is the x-value where the minimum occurs, not the minimum value.
whyWrong.D: 7 is the same x-value with the sign flipped, again an input rather than an output.

questions.stem:
\[ y = 7x^{2} - bx - 6 \]

Which of the following equations is equal to the given equation above, where b is a positive constant?
questions.whyCorrect: Complete the square after factoring 7 out of the x terms: \( 7\left(x^{2} - \frac{b}{7}x\right) - 6 \) . Half of \( \frac{b}{7} \) is \( \frac{b}{14} \) , so the bracket becomes \( \left(x - \frac{b}{14}\right)^{2} - \frac{b^{2}}{196} \) . Multiplying that leftover by 7 gives \( -\frac{b^{2}}{28} \) , so \( y = 7\left(x - \frac{b}{14}\right)^{2} - 6 - \frac{b^{2}}{28} \) . Expanding it back returns \( 7x^{2} - bx - 6 \) .

whyWrong.B: Dropping \( \frac{b^{2}}{28} \) leaves an expression that expands to \( 7x^{2} - bx - 6 + \frac{b^{2}}{28} \) - it is not equal to the original.
whyWrong.C: The plus sign inside the bracket flips the sign of the middle term, giving \( +bx \) .
whyWrong.D: This has both errors: the wrong sign inside the bracket and the missing correction term.

questions.stem:
\[ -x^{2} + bx - 49 = 0 \]

In the given equation, b is an integer. The equation has no real solution. What is the least possible value of b?
questions.whyCorrect: No real solution means a negative discriminant. Here a = −1 and c = −49, so \( b^{2} - 4(-1)(-49) = b^{2} - 196 < 0 \) , which gives −14 < b < 14. Since b is an integer, the smallest value in that range is −13. The endpoints ±14 are excluded because they make the discriminant exactly zero, which is one real solution, not none.

questions.stem: \[49 = \frac{2K}{v^{2}}\]For an object with a mass of 49 kilograms, the given equation relates the kinetic energy \(K\), in joules, of the object to the object's speed \(v\), in meters per second, where \(K\) and \(v\) are positive. Which equation correctly expresses this object's speed, in meters per second, in terms of the object's kinetic energy, in joules?
questions.whyCorrect: Multiply both sides by \(v^{2}\): \(49v^{2} = 2K\). Divide by 49: \(v^{2} = \frac{2K}{49}\). Then take the positive square root, since \(v > 0\): \(v = \sqrt{\frac{2K}{49}}\).

whyWrong.B: This is the reciprocal inside the root — it comes from dividing in the wrong direction when clearing \(v^{2}\).
whyWrong.C: Squaring the 49 instead of taking a square root of the whole expression; the square is on \(v\), not on 49.
whyWrong.D: Same error, and no square root is taken at all, so the units and the algebra both fail.

questions.stem: \[ |6x - 3| = |5x| \]What is the smallest solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: When two absolute values are equal, the insides are either equal or opposite, so solve both. \( 6x - 3 = 5x \) gives x = 3, and \( 6x - 3 = -5x \) gives \( 11x = 3 \), so \( x = \frac{3}{11} \). Both check out in the original equation, and \( \frac{3}{11} \) is the smaller.

questions.stem: Which table could represent values of \(x\) and their corresponding values of \(f(x)\) for a decreasing exponential function \(f\)?

choices.label: A
choices.content:
x1234
f(x)1234

choices.label: B
choices.content:
x1234
f(x)8421

choices.label: C
choices.content:
x1248
f(x)191725

choices.label: D
choices.content:
x1248
f(x)251791

questions.whyCorrect: An exponential function multiplies by the same factor for each equal step in \(x\); a decreasing one uses a factor between 0 and 1. In this table \(x\) goes up by 1 each time and \(f(x)\) goes 8, 4, 2, 1 — each value is half the one before, so \(f(x) = 16\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x}\). Test for a constant ratio, not a constant difference.

whyWrong.A: \(f(x)\) increases by a constant 1 each step, so this is linear and increasing — neither exponential nor decreasing.
whyWrong.C: \(f(x)\) increases, so it cannot be decreasing; the values also rise by a constant 8 per listed row, which is a linear pattern in the row number.
whyWrong.D: This does decrease, but the ratios \(\frac{17}{25}, \frac{9}{17}, \frac{1}{9}\) are all different, so the decay is not exponential. The \(x\)-values are also unequally spaced, which is the clue to check ratios against actual \(x\)-steps.

questions.stem: In the xy-plane, line \(s\) passes through the point (0, 0) and is parallel to the line represented by the equation y = 36x + 6. If line \(s\) also passes through the point \((9, d)\), what is the value of \(d\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Parallel lines have equal slopes, so line \(s\) has slope 36. It passes through the origin, so its equation is \(y=36x\) with no constant term. At \(x=9\), \(d=36(9)=324\). The +6 belongs to the other line and must not be carried over.

questions.stem: A gallery had \(x\) artifacts in a collection. When more artifacts were added to the collection, the number of artifacts increased by 149%. What is the number of artifacts in the collection in terms of \(x\)?
questions.whyCorrect: "Increased by 149%" means the increase, \(1.49x\), is added to the original \(x\). The new total is \(x + 1.49x = 2.49x\).

whyWrong.A: This is roughly a 410% increase; the multiplier for a 149% increase is \(1 + 1.49\), not 5.1.
whyWrong.B: This is smaller than \(x\), so it describes a decrease. Adding artifacts must give a larger number.
whyWrong.C: This is the size of the increase alone, or the multiplier for "149% of" rather than "increased by 149%". The original \(x\) still has to be included.

questions.stem: The function f is defined by \[ f(x) = (x - 9)(x - 6)(x - 5). \]In the xy-plane, the graph of y = g(x) is the result of translating the graph of y = f(x) up 4 units. What is the value of g(0)?
questions.whyCorrect: Translating up 4 units adds 4 to every output, so g(x) = f(x) + 4 and the input is unchanged. Compute f(0) = (-9)(-6)(-5) = -270 — three negative factors give a negative product. Then g(0) = -270 + 4 = -266.

questions.stem:
\[ 5x + 4y = 44 \]
\[ 3x - 7y = 17 \]The solution to the given system of equations is \( (x, y) \). What is the value of \( 8x - 3y \)?
questions.whyCorrect: Eliminate y: multiply the first equation by 7 and the second by 4 to get 35x + 28y = 308 and 12x − 28y = 68. Adding them gives 47x = 376, so x = 8, and substituting back into 5x + 4y = 44 gives y = 1. Then 8x − 3y = 64 − 3 = 61.

questions.stem: \[x^{2} - 10x + y^{2} - 6y - 47 = 0\]In the xy-plane, the graph of the given equation is a circle. If this circle is inscribed in a square, what is the perimeter of the square?
questions.whyCorrect: Complete the square on each variable: \(x^{2}-10x\) needs \(+25\) and \(y^{2}-6y\) needs \(+9\), so the equation becomes \((x-5)^{2}+(y-3)^{2} = 47+25+9 = 81\) and the radius is 9. A circle inscribed in a square touches all four sides, so each side of the square equals the circle's diameter, 18. The perimeter is 4(18) = 72.

whyWrong.A: This is the diameter, which is one side of the square, not all four.
whyWrong.B: This uses the radius 9 as the side length instead of the diameter. The inscribed circle spans the full width of the square.
whyWrong.D: This comes from working with 47 (or from adding constants incorrectly) instead of completing the square properly. The right-hand side after completing the square is 81, not 47.

questions.stem:
Survey Results
Annuals159
Perennials295
A total of 454 gardeners selected at random were asked if they preferred perennials or annuals. The results of the survey are shown in the table. According to these results, if 5,448 gardeners were choosing plants, how many more would prefer perennials than would prefer annuals?
questions.whyCorrect: Find the difference in the survey first: 295 - 159 = 136 out of 454 gardeners. The larger group is \( \frac{5{,}448}{454} = 12 \) times as big, so scale the difference by the same factor: 136 x 12 = 1,632.

whyWrong.A: 136 is the difference in the original survey of 454 gardeners, not in the group of 5,448. It still has to be scaled up by 12.
whyWrong.C: 1,908 is 159 x 12, the number who would prefer annuals, not the difference between the two preferences.
whyWrong.D: 3,540 is 295 x 12, the number who would prefer perennials. Subtract the annuals figure to get the difference.

questions.stem:
\( y \le 5x - 21 \)
Which point (x, y) is a solution to the given inequality in the xy-plane?
questions.whyCorrect: Substitute each x into 5x - 21 and check whether y is at or below it. For (5, -21): \( 5(5) - 21 = 4 \), and -21 is less than 4, so the point satisfies the inequality.

whyWrong.A: At x = -5 the boundary is \( 5(-5) - 21 = -46 \), and -21 sits above -46, not below it.
whyWrong.B: At x = 0 the boundary is -21, and 21 is well above it.
whyWrong.D: At x = 6 the boundary is \( 30 - 21 = 9 \), and 21 is above 9.

questions.stem: For the polynomial function \(f\), the graph of \(y=f(x)\) in the xy-plane passes through the points \((-4, 0)\), \((1, 0)\), and \((9, 0)\). Which of the following must be a factor of \(f(x)\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The zeros are −4, 1 and 9, so the factors are \(x+4\), \(x-1\) and \(x-9\). \(x-1\) is the only one among the choices.

whyWrong.B: \(x+9\) corresponds to a zero at −9; the graph crosses at \(+9\).
whyWrong.C: \(x-4\) corresponds to a zero at \(+4\); the given zero is −4.
whyWrong.D: \(x+1\) corresponds to a zero at −1, which is not one of the points.

questions.note: Same template as this section’s questions 1 and 6 — dedupe candidate if more than one is used in a test.

questions.stem: In right triangle \(ABC\), angle \(B\) is a right angle and the measure of angle \(A\) is 56°. What is the measure of \(\angle C\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The angles total 180°, and angle \(B\) uses 90° of that, so angles \(A\) and \(C\) share the remaining 90°. Therefore \(\angle C = 90 - 56 = 34\) degrees.

whyWrong.A: 124° is \(180 - 56\), which ignores the right angle. It is also obtuse, impossible in a triangle that already has a 90° angle.
whyWrong.B: 146° is \(90 + 56\) — the two known angles added instead of subtracted.
whyWrong.C: This assumes the triangle is isosceles; nothing states that \(\angle A = \angle C\), and 56 + 56 + 90 exceeds 180.

questions.note: The printed figure adds nothing beyond the stated right angle at B and 56 degrees at A.

questions.stem:
The table shows the number of trees planted for 4 separate plots of land on a tree farm.
PlotTrees planted
Plot 185
Plot 295
Plot 3100
Plot 478
What is the maximum number of trees planted on one of these 4 plots of land?
questions.whyCorrect: "Maximum" means the largest single value in the data, not the largest possible reading on the scale and not an average. Compare the four counts and take the biggest: 100, at Plot 3.

whyWrong.B: 95 is Plot 2, the second-largest count.
whyWrong.C: 85 is Plot 1.
whyWrong.D: 78 is Plot 4, the minimum rather than the maximum.

questions.note: Source prints this as a bar graph (Plot 1-4 against trees planted, axis to 110). Bar heights are exactly the four answer choices, so it is rendered here as an equivalent table.

questions.stem: To make a bookcase, a worker charged a one-time fee plus $17 per hour worked. The equation 17h + 45 = 164 represents this situation, where h is the number of hours worked. Which of the following is the best interpretation of 164 in this context?

choices.label: C
choices.content: The charge per hour, in dollars

questions.whyCorrect: Match each number in the equation to a phrase in the sentence. The $17 multiplies h, so it is the hourly rate; 45 is added on regardless of hours, so it is the one-time fee. The 164 sits alone on the other side of the equals sign, so it is what the two parts add up to — the total charge in dollars.

whyWrong.A: The one-time fee is 45, the amount added no matter how many hours are worked. 164 is the sum of the fee and the hourly charges.
whyWrong.B: The number of hours is h, the unknown being solved for. Solving gives h = 7, not 164.
whyWrong.C: The charge per hour is 17, the number multiplying h. 164 is not a rate; it has no "per hour" attached to it.

questions.stem: \[ f(x) = 6.4(0.5)^{3x} \] A sample of carbon-11 radioactively decays. The function \(f\) models the mass, in grams (g), of carbon-11 in the sample \(x\) hours after it is initially measured. Which statement is the best interpretation of \(f(2) = 0.1\)?

choices.label: A
choices.content: After 0.1 hour, the mass of carbon-11 in the sample is 2 g.

choices.label: B
choices.content: After 2 hours, the mass of carbon-11 in the sample is 0.1 g.

choices.label: C
choices.content: After 0.1 hour, the mass of carbon-11 in the sample has decreased by exactly 2 g.

choices.label: D
choices.content: After 2 hours, the mass of carbon-11 in the sample has decreased by exactly 0.1 g.

questions.whyCorrect: The input of \(f\) is time in hours and the output is the mass remaining, so \(f(2) = 0.1\) reads directly as: at \(x = 2\) hours, the mass is 0.1 gram. The output is the amount left, not the amount lost.

whyWrong.A: This swaps input and output. The 2 is the time and the 0.1 is the mass, not the other way round.
whyWrong.C: It swaps input and output and reads the output as a decrease.
whyWrong.D: The time is right, but \(f\) gives the mass remaining. The decrease after 2 hours would be \(6.4 - 0.1 = 6.3\) grams.

questions.stem: Each side of square \(A\) has a length of 11 inches. Each side of square \(A\) is multiplied by a scale factor of 3 to create square \(B\). What is the length, in inches, of each side of square \(B\)?
questions.whyCorrect: A scale factor multiplies each length: 11 × 3 = 33 inches.

whyWrong.A: This subtracts 3 from 11. A scale factor multiplies.
whyWrong.B: 11 is square A's side, unchanged.
whyWrong.C: This adds 3 to 11 instead of multiplying.

questions.stem: For a particular tree species, it is recommended to plant a maximum of 92 trees per acre. Based on this recommendation, what is the maximum number of trees of this species that can be planted on 2 acres?
questions.whyCorrect: Multiply the per-acre maximum by the number of acres: 92 × 2 = 184 trees.

whyWrong.A: This is 92 × 3, using three acres instead of two.
whyWrong.C: This is 92 + 2. Adding the acreage to a rate does not give a total.
whyWrong.D: This is 92 − 2, subtracting the acreage from the rate.

questions.stem: A furniture company is selling all tables with a 20% discount off their original price for the month of October. What is the discount, in dollars, on a table with an original price of $130?
questions.whyCorrect: The question asks for the discount itself, not the sale price. The discount is 20% of the original: \(0.20 \times 130 = 26\) dollars.

whyWrong.A: This is the sale price after the discount, \(130 - 26\), not the discount.
whyWrong.B: This is neither; it is close to 70% of 130 and does not match any step of this problem.
whyWrong.C: This is 40% of 130 — the percent doubled.

questions.stem:
\[ -4(v - 9)(v - 2)(v + 7) = 0 \]

What value of v is a solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero, and the constant −4 can never be zero. Setting each bracket to zero gives v = 9, v = 2 and v = −7. Of those, only 9 appears among the choices.

whyWrong.A: −2 flips the sign of the root from \( (v - 2) \) ; that factor is zero at v = +2.
whyWrong.B: 7 flips the sign of the root from \( (v + 7) \) ; that factor is zero at v = −7.
whyWrong.D: −4 is the constant multiplier out front, not a root.

questions.stem: A data set of 27 different numbers has a mean of 18 and a median of 18. A new data set is created by adding 20 to all of the values greater than the median while leaving all other numbers in the data set unchanged. Which of the following values will not change?
questions.whyCorrect: With 27 values the median is the 14th in order, and that value is 18. Only the 13 values above it are changed, and adding 20 keeps each of them above 18, so nothing crosses the middle position. The 14th value is still 18, so the median is unchanged.

whyWrong.A: The total rises by \(13 \times 20 = 260\), so the mean rises by \(\frac{260}{27}\), roughly 9.6.
whyWrong.B: The maximum gains 20 while the minimum (below the median) is untouched, so the range grows by 20.
whyWrong.D: The sum grows by exactly 260 for the same reason as the mean.

questions.stem: Right rectangular prism X is similar to right rectangular prism Y. The surface area of right rectangular prism X is 52 square centimeters, and the surface area of right rectangular prism Y is 3,328 square centimeters. The volume of right rectangular prism X is 10.5 cubic centimeters. What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of right rectangular prism Y?
questions.whyCorrect: For similar solids, areas scale by the square of the linear ratio and volumes by its cube. The area ratio is \( \frac{3328}{52} = 64 \) , so the linear ratio is \( \sqrt{64} = 8 \) and the volume ratio is \( 8^{3} = 512 \) . Therefore the volume of Y is 10.5(512) = 5,376. Multiplying the volume by 64 instead of 512 is the standard error.

questions.stem: A survey of 500 adults finds a correlation coefficient of 0.7 between the number of hours spent reading per week and their vocabulary test scores. The survey also reports that 60% of participants read more than 5 hours per week, with a margin of error of ±5%. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.content: Reading more hours per week causes higher vocabulary scores.

choices.label: B
choices.content: There is a strong positive relationship between reading hours and vocabulary scores, but causation cannot be determined.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Between 55% and 65% of adults read more than 5 hours per week, and this improves their vocabulary.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The correlation of 0.7 means 70% of vocabulary scores are explained by reading hours.

questions.whyCorrect: This is a survey, not an experiment: nobody was assigned a number of reading hours, so a third factor (schooling, income, time available) could drive both variables. A coefficient of 0.7 does establish a strong positive association, and that is exactly as far as the data go.

whyWrong.A: Observational data cannot support a causal claim, however strong the correlation.
whyWrong.C: The first half is a fair reading of the margin of error, but "this improves their vocabulary" smuggles causation back in.
whyWrong.D: That interpretation belongs to \(r^2\), not r. Here \(r^2 = 0.49\), so about 49% of the variation is accounted for — and even that is not a causal statement.

questions.stem: In the figure, parallel lines \(a\) and \(b\) are intersected by lines \(c\), \(d\), and \(e\). If \( z = 49 \), \( y = 136 \), and \( v < z \), which statement about \(x\) and \(w\) must be true?
questions.whyCorrect: Each of \(x\) and \(w\) is an angle of a triangle-like crossing formed by two of the transversals, and the exterior-angle relationship (using the parallel lines to transfer angles from \(a\) to \(b\)) gives \( w = y - z \) and \( x = y - v \). With \( y = 136 \) and \( z = 49 \), \( w = 87 \). Since \( v < z \), subtracting the smaller \(v\) leaves more, so \( x = 136 - v > 136 - 49 = 87 = w \).

whyWrong.A: This reverses the effect of \( v < z \): a smaller angle subtracted from the same 136 gives a larger result, so \(x\) exceeds \(w\).
whyWrong.C: Equality would need \( v = z \), which the condition \( v < z \) rules out.
whyWrong.D: \( w = 87 \) alone already exceeds 90 when added to any positive \(x\); nothing here makes the two angles complementary.

questions.note: Figure needed: vertical parallel lines a and b crossed by three transversals — c rising to the right, d and e falling to the right. v is at a on line d, y and z are at b on lines c and e, x is where c meets d (right of b), and w is where c meets e (left of a).
questions.imageAlt: A line diagram: two parallel vertical lines labelled a and b crossed by three slanted lines labelled c, d and e, with five of the angles formed marked by letters.

questions.stem: A data set of 77 different numbers has a mean of 1,073. A new data set is created by adding 93 to each number in the original data set that is greater than the median and subtracting 93 from each number in the original data set that is less than the median. Which of the following measures does NOT have the same value in both the original and the new data sets?
questions.whyCorrect: With 77 different numbers, exactly 38 lie above the median and 38 below. Pushing the top 38 up by 93 and the bottom 38 down by 93 leaves the total untouched, so sum and mean are unchanged, and the middle value never moves, so the median is unchanged. But every value is now farther from the mean than before, so the spread — the standard deviation — grows.

whyWrong.A: The 38 additions of 93 exactly cancel the 38 subtractions of 93, so the total is identical.
whyWrong.B: The mean is the unchanged sum divided by the unchanged count of 77.
whyWrong.D: The median value itself is neither greater nor less than the median, so it is left alone, and no value crosses it. The 39th value in order is still the same number.

questions.stem: A polygon has exactly 87 sides. If the measure of each of the 87 interior angles of this polygon is \( (180p)^{\circ} \) , what is the value of p?
questions.whyCorrect: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon sum to \( (n-2)180^{\circ} \) , so here the total is \( 85 \cdot 180 \) degrees. All 87 angles are equal, so each is \( \frac{85 \cdot 180}{87} \) degrees. Setting that equal to 180p and dividing both sides by 180 leaves \( p = \frac{85}{87} \) , a little under 1.
questions.note: Exact value 85/87, about 0.9770. Enter as the fraction 85/87.

questions.stem: There are 50 unique numbers in a data set. If the value of each number increases by 25%, which of the following will be true?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The new mean will remain the same, but the new standard deviation will be 25% more than the previous standard deviation.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The new mean will be 25% more than the previous mean, but the standard deviation will remain the same.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The new mean will be 25% more than the previous mean, but the standard deviation will increase.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Neither the mean nor the standard deviation of the values will change.

questions.whyCorrect: Increasing every value by 25% multiplies each one by 1.25. Multiplying scales the mean by the same factor, so the mean is 25% larger, and it also stretches every distance between values by 1.25, so the standard deviation grows too. This is the key difference from adding a constant, which shifts the mean but leaves the spread alone.

whyWrong.A: The mean cannot stay put when every single value gets larger.
whyWrong.B: This is the rule for adding a constant. Scaling changes the gaps between values, so the spread changes as well.
whyWrong.D: Both change: the mean is multiplied by 1.25 and so is the standard deviation.

questions.note: Choice C says only that the standard deviation "will increase"; it in fact increases by exactly 25%, the same factor as the mean.

questions.stem: Right rectangular prism X is similar to right rectangular prism Y. The surface area of right rectangular prism X is 59 square centimeters \( \left(\text{cm}^2\right) \), and the surface area of right rectangular prism Y is 1,475 cm². The volume of right rectangular prism Y is 1,500 cubic centimeters \( \left(\text{cm}^3\right) \). What is the sum of the volumes, in cm³, of right rectangular prism X and right rectangular prism Y?
questions.whyCorrect: For similar solids, areas scale as the square of the linear ratio and volumes as the cube. The surface areas are in the ratio \( \frac{1475}{59} = 25 \), so the linear ratio of Y to X is \( \sqrt{25} = 5 \) and the volume ratio is \( 5^3 = 125 \). So prism X has volume \( \frac{1500}{125} = 12 \) cm³, and the two volumes sum to \( 12+1500 = 1512 \) cm³.

questions.stem: The mass of object A is 144% of the mass of object B, and the mass of object A is 0.740% of the mass of object C. If the mass of object C is p% of the mass of object B, what is the value of p?
questions.whyCorrect: Write both facts about A: \(A = 1.44B\) and \(A = 0.0074C\). Setting them equal gives \(0.0074C = 1.44B\), so \(C = \frac{1.44}{0.0074}B \approx 194.5946B\). As a percentage of B that is \(p \approx 19{,}459.46\). The decimal in 0.740% is the whole difficulty: it converts to 0.0074, not 0.74.
questions.note: The exact value is 19,459.4594...; a grid-in field would take 19459. The parallel question 24 in this book asks for p/1,000 instead, which keeps the answer griddable.

questions.stem: For triangle \(ABC\), the length of \( \overline{AB} \) is 11 less than the length of \( \overline{AC} \). Point \(D\) (not shown) lies on \( \overline{AC} \) such that \( \overline{BD} \) (not shown) is perpendicular to \( \overline{AC} \). What is the value of \( \frac{BC}{BD} \)?
questions.whyCorrect: From the figure the right angle is at \(B\) and \( AC = 28 \), so \( AB = 28-11 = 17 \). Dropping the altitude \( \overline{BD} \) to the hypotenuse creates triangle \(BDC\), which is similar to triangle \(ABC\) (both are right triangles sharing angle \(C\)). Matching corresponding sides, \( \frac{BC}{BD} = \frac{AC}{AB} = \frac{28}{17} \) — you never need \(BC\) itself. (Checking directly: \( BC = \sqrt{495} \) and \( BD = \frac{17\sqrt{495}}{28} \), whose ratio is \( \frac{28}{17} \).)
questions.note: Figure needed: right triangle ABC with the right angle at B, A above B, C to the right, and hypotenuse AC labelled 28.
questions.imageAlt: A right triangle with its three vertices labelled, the right angle marked with a small square, and the hypotenuse labelled with its length.

questions.stem: A nutritionist wants to conduct a survey to estimate the mean number of servings of vegetables eaten by a certain group of people each day. The nutritionist has not yet decided which group of people to survey. Surveying a random sample from which of the following groups would most likely result in the smallest margin of error?

choices.label: C
choices.content: Viewers of the same television show

choices.label: D
choices.content: Students who are following the same daily diet plan

questions.whyCorrect: For a fixed sample size, the margin of error shrinks as the variability in the data shrinks. People on the same daily diet plan eat close to the same number of vegetable servings, so their measurements cluster tightly and the estimate of the mean is the most precise.

whyWrong.A: A whole city contains every eating habit there is, so vegetable servings vary enormously.
whyWrong.B: Sharing one restaurant says almost nothing about what people eat the rest of the day.
whyWrong.C: Watching the same show has no connection to diet at all, so this group is as varied as the general population.

questions.stem: In the figure, \( \overline{LQ} \) intersects \( \overline{MP} \) at point \(R\) and \( \overline{LM} \) is parallel to \( \overline{PQ} \). The lengths of \( \overline{MR} \) and \( \overline{RP} \) are 8 and 14 units, respectively. The area of \( \triangle LMR \) is 36 square units. What is the area of \( \triangle PQR \), in square units?
questions.whyCorrect: The parallel sides make the alternate interior angles equal, and the angles at \(R\) are vertical, so \( \triangle LMR \sim \triangle QPR \) with \(MR\) corresponding to \(RP\). The linear ratio from \(LMR\) to \(PQR\) is \( \frac{14}{8} = \frac{7}{4} \), and areas scale by the square of that: \( \left(\frac{7}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{16} \). So the area is \( 36 \times \frac{49}{16} = \frac{441}{4} \).

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{576}{49} \) is \( 36 \times \frac{16}{49} \) — the ratio applied upside down, shrinking the larger triangle.
whyWrong.B: \( \frac{144}{7} \) is \( 36 \times \frac{4}{7} \), using the linear ratio (also inverted) instead of its square.
whyWrong.C: 63 is \( 36 \times \frac{7}{4} \), scaling the area by the linear ratio rather than by its square.

questions.note: Figure needed: segments LQ and MP crossing at R, with triangle LMR above-left and triangle PQR below-right, LM parallel to PQ.
questions.imageAlt: Two straight segments crossing at a labelled interior point, forming two triangles that point in opposite directions; all five points are labelled.

questions.stem: The value of a collectible comic book increased by 167% from the end of 2011 to the end of 2012 and then decreased by 16% from the end of 2012 to the end of 2013. What was the net percentage increase in the value of the collectible comic book from the end of 2011 to the end of 2013?
questions.whyCorrect: Chain the growth factors: an increase of 167% multiplies by \(1 + 1.67 = 2.67\), and a decrease of 16% multiplies by \(1 - 0.16 = 0.84\). Together \(2.67 \times 0.84 = 2.2428\), so the value ends at 224.28% of where it started, a net increase of 124.28%.

whyWrong.B: \(1.67 \times 0.84 = 1.4028\): this reads "increased by 167%" as "is 167% of", losing the original value.
whyWrong.C: \(167 - 16 = 151\). Percent changes applied one after the other multiply; they cannot be added and subtracted.
whyWrong.D: \(2.67 \times 1.16 = 3.0972\): the second change was applied as a 16% increase rather than a decrease.

questions.stem: A circle is inscribed in a square such that the circle touches the midpoint of each side of the square. The length of the diagonal of the square is 228 units. What is the area, in square units, of the circle?
questions.whyCorrect: The diagonal of a square is \( s\sqrt{2} \) , so \( s = \frac{228}{\sqrt{2}} = 114\sqrt{2} \) . An inscribed circle touching each side's midpoint has diameter equal to the side, so \( r = \frac{s}{2} = 57\sqrt{2} \) and \( r^{2} = 57^{2} \cdot 2 = 6{,}498 \) . The area is \( 6{,}498\pi \) .

whyWrong.B: 12,996 is \( s^{2} \) , the area of the square divided by nothing — it uses the side as the radius instead of the diameter, doubling r.
whyWrong.C: 25,992 comes from treating the diagonal 228 as the diameter of the circle, giving r = 114 and \( r^{2} = 12{,}996 \) , then doubling again.
whyWrong.D: 51,984 is \( 228^{2} \) , the square of the diagonal, with no halving or dividing by 2 at all.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = a^x - b\), where a and b are constants. The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the xy-plane passes through the points (0, −5) and (1, 2). What is the value of a?
questions.whyCorrect: Use the point with x = 0 first, because \(a^0 = 1\) no matter what a is: \(1 - b = -5\) gives b = 6. Then substitute (1, 2): \(a^1 - 6 = 2\), so a = 8.

whyWrong.B: 7 is the vertical gap between the two given y-values, 2 - (-5), not the value of a.
whyWrong.C: 6 is b, the constant being subtracted.
whyWrong.D: 5 comes from reading the y-value -5 as if it gave a directly; the \(-b\) has to be undone first.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(158t^{3} - 24t^{2}u\)?
questions.whyCorrect: The common factor is \(2t^{2}\): both coefficients are even (158 = 2·79, 24 = 2·12) and both terms have at least \(t^{2}\). Only the second term has \(u\), so \(u\) cannot come out. That leaves \(2t^{2}(79t - 12u)\).

whyWrong.A: Expanding gives \(158t^{3} - 24tu\); one factor of \(t\) is missing from the second term.
whyWrong.C: \(u\) cannot be factored out because the first term \(158t^{3}\) contains no \(u\); expanding gives \(158t^{3}u\).
whyWrong.D: Same problem — pulling \(u\) out puts a \(u\) into the first term that was never there.

questions.stem:
\(y=-3x^2-40\)
\(y=qx-37\)

In the given system of equations, \(q\) is a positive constant. The graphs of the equations in the given system intersect at exactly one point, \((x,y)\), in the \(xy\)-plane. What is the value of \(x\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Set the sides equal: \(-3x^2-40=qx-37\), which rearranges to \(3x^2+qx+3=0\). One intersection point means the discriminant is zero: \(q^2-36=0\), and \(q\) is positive so \(q=6\). The single root is at the vertex, \(x=-\frac{q}{2(3)}=-1\).

whyWrong.A: \(-77\) comes from combining \(-40\) and \(-37\), the two constants, rather than solving.
whyWrong.B: \(-43\) comes from \(-40-3\), again just arithmetic on the given constants.
whyWrong.C: \(-6\) is \(-q\); the root is \(-\frac{q}{2a}\), and \(2a=6\) here.

questions.stem:
\(-5x + 15rx = 135\)

In the given equation, \(r\) is a constant. The equation has no solution. What is the value of \(r\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Factor the left side into \((-5 + 15r)x = 135\). A linear equation of the form \(ax = b\) has no solution only when \(a = 0\) while \(b \ne 0\), because \(0 = 135\) is impossible. Set \(-5 + 15r = 0\), so \(15r = 5\) and \(r = \frac{1}{3}\).

whyWrong.A: This is \(\frac{1}{9}\), which you get by dividing 5 by 45 or mishandling the 15; the coefficient condition is \(15r = 5\).
whyWrong.C: This is the reciprocal of the right answer — you solved \(5r = 15\) instead of \(15r = 5\).
whyWrong.D: With \(r = 9\) the coefficient is \(-5 + 135 = 130 \ne 0\), so the equation has exactly one solution, not none.

questions.stem: \[ 7|x - 7| = 42 \] What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Divide by 7 first: \( |x - 7| = 6 \) . An absolute value of 6 means the inside is 6 or -6, so \( x = 13 \) or \( x = 1 \) , and the sum is 14. A shortcut: the two solutions sit the same distance either side of 7, so their sum is \( 2 \times 7 = 14 \) .

whyWrong.A: -6 is the negative value of \( x - 7 \) , not a value of x, and the question asks for a sum of two numbers.
whyWrong.B: 0 is \( 6 + (-6) \) , the sum of the two values of \( x - 7 \) . Each solution for x is 7 larger than that, so the sum is 14 larger.
whyWrong.D: 49 is 42 + 7, which adds the 7 that is subtracted inside the bars to the other side of the equation. That 7 is subtracted from x only, not from the whole equation.

questions.stem: In the relationship between variables \(x\) and \(y\), each increase of 8 in the value of \(x\) decreases the value of \(y\) by 3. When the value of \(x\) is 16, the value of \(y\) is 10. Which equation represents this relationship?
questions.whyCorrect: Slope is change in \(y\) over change in \(x\): a drop of 3 for every rise of 8 gives \(-\frac{3}{8}\). The point \((16,10)\) then fixes the intercept: \(10=-\frac{3}{8}(16)+b=-6+b\), so \(b=16\).

whyWrong.A: This uses the given \(y\)-value 10 as the intercept, but 10 is the output at \(x=16\), not at \(x=0\).
whyWrong.C: The slope is upside down — \(\frac{8}{3}\) would mean \(x\) changing 3 for every 8 in \(y\).
whyWrong.D: Same inverted slope, with the intercept computed consistently from it.

questions.stem:
\[ x^2-11x-3=0 \]
What is a solution to the given equation?
questions.whyCorrect: Identify the coefficients before substituting: \(a=1\), \(b=-11\), \(c=-3\). The formula is \(x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\), so the numerator starts with \(-(-11)=11\) and the denominator is \(2(1)\).

whyWrong.A: The numerator is right but the denominator uses \(2c\) instead of \(2a\). The denominator always comes from the leading coefficient.
whyWrong.C: \(b\) and \(c\) have been swapped, and the denominator uses \(c\) as well.
whyWrong.D: The denominator is right, but \(b\) and \(c\) are swapped: \(b\) is \(-11\), the coefficient of \(x\), and \(c\) is \(-3\).

questions.stem: A plant nursery classifies a perennial flower species as tall if its typical height when fully grown is more than 100 centimeters. Each of the following inequalities represents the possible heights h, in centimeters, for a specific perennial flower species when fully grown. Which inequality represents the possible heights h, in centimeters, for a tall perennial flower species?
questions.whyCorrect: Every height the range allows has to exceed 100 cm for the species to qualify, so the lower bound must itself be at least 100. Only the range beginning at 110 does that.

whyWrong.A: Every value here is below 95, short of 100.
whyWrong.B: Every value here is below 89.
whyWrong.C: This range stops at 100, so it never exceeds 100 — the classification requires more than 100.

questions.note: Near-identical template to satmath-ma2-linear-inequalities-23; do not place both in one test.

questions.stem: The principal of a local high school is conducting a survey on whether students felt online learning was still effective during the COVID-19 pandemic. Of the 200 students who were randomly sampled, 43% felt that online learning is still effective. Based on the margin of error, the principal expects that somewhere between 35% and 51% of all students feel that online learning is still effective during the COVID-19 pandemic. What is the margin of error?
questions.whyCorrect: The interval runs from the sample percentage out to each end by the same amount: 43 − 35 = 8 and 51 − 43 = 8. The margin of error is that one-sided distance, 8%.

whyWrong.A: 43% is the sample result itself, the center of the interval, not its half-width.
whyWrong.B: 16% is the full width of the interval, from 35 to 51. The margin of error is half of that, since it extends in both directions.
whyWrong.D: 2% is not a distance anywhere in this interval; the sample of 200 is not used to compute the margin here, it is read off the given range.

questions.stem: A circle has center \(O\), and points \(A\) and \(B\) lie on the circle. The measure of arc \(AB\) is 20°, and the length of this arc is 4 inches. What is the circumference, in inches, of the circle?
questions.whyCorrect: An arc's length is the same fraction of the circumference as its central angle is of 360°. Here that fraction is \( \frac{20}{360} = \frac{1}{18} \), so the 4-inch arc is one eighteenth of the whole circle and the circumference is \( 4 \times 18 = 72 \) inches.

whyWrong.A: 4 is the arc length itself, not the full circumference.
whyWrong.B: 8 doubles the arc, which would be right only if the arc were a semicircle (180°).
whyWrong.C: 16 multiplies by 4; that treats the arc as a quarter of the circle, i.e. a 90° arc.

questions.stem: A biologist mixed a solution that is 0.3% sodium chloride by mass with a solution that is 0.15% sodium chloride by mass to obtain a new solution, which has a mass of 80 grams and contains 0.21 grams of sodium chloride. How many grams of 0.3% sodium chloride solution did the biologist use?
questions.whyCorrect: Track the salt, not the solution. Let x be the grams of the 0.3% solution; the rest, 80 − x grams, is the 0.15% solution. The salt each contributes must total 0.21 grams: \(0.003x+0.0015(80-x)=0.21\). That becomes \(0.0015x+0.12=0.21\), so \(0.0015x=0.09\) and x = 60. Check it: 60(0.003) = 0.18 and 20(0.0015) = 0.03, which sum to 0.21. The usual slip is writing 0.3 and 0.15 instead of 0.003 and 0.0015.

whyWrong.A: 0.14 is on the scale of the salt, not the solution. A mere 0.14 grams of a 0.3% solution holds about 0.0004 grams of salt, nowhere near 0.21 grams.
whyWrong.B: 20 grams is the amount of the 0.15% solution, the other unknown. The question asks for the 0.3% one.
whyWrong.D: This is 80 − 0.14, the complement of choice A. It fails immediately: 79.86 grams of the 0.3% solution alone would already contain about 0.24 grams of salt, more than the 0.21 grams in the mixture.

questions.stem: A right square pyramid has a total surface area of 28,160 square inches, and the combined surface area of the four lateral faces of this pyramid is 16,060 square inches. What is the height, in inches, of this pyramid?
questions.whyCorrect: Subtract to get the base: \( 28{,}160-16{,}060 = 12{,}100 \) square inches, so the base edge is \( \sqrt{12{,}100} = 110 \). Each lateral face is a triangle with base 110 and height equal to the slant height \(l\), so \( 4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}(110)l = 16{,}060 \) gives \( l = 73 \). The slant height, the pyramid's height, and half the base edge form a right triangle: \( h = \sqrt{73^2-55^2} = \sqrt{2{,}304} = 48 \).

whyWrong.B: 55 is half the base edge, one leg of that right triangle, not the height.
whyWrong.C: 73 is the slant height — the distance up the middle of a triangular face, not the vertical height.
whyWrong.D: 110 is the base edge itself.

The tables give the distribution of daily travel times between two towns for bus A and bus B over a 40-day period.

Bus A

Which statement correctly compares the standard deviations of travel times for bus A and bus B?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The standard deviation of travel times for bus A is less than the standard deviation of travel times for bus B.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The standard deviation of travel times for bus B is less than the standard deviation of travel times for bus A.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The standard deviation of travel times for bus A is equal to the standard deviation of travel times for bus B.

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is not enough information to compare these standard deviations.

questions.whyCorrect: The two tables have the identical frequency pattern - 5, 10, 15, 10 - so the shape of the two distributions is the same and only the spacing of the values differs. Bus A's times run from 44 to 48, a spread of 4 minutes; bus B's run from 25 to 40, a spread of 15 minutes. Standard deviation measures how far values sit from their mean, so the set packed into a 4-minute window has the smaller one. You do not need to compute either number.

whyWrong.B: This has the comparison backwards. Bus B's times are spread across 15 minutes, bus A's across 4.
whyWrong.C: Equal frequencies do not mean equal standard deviation - the values themselves are far more spread out for bus B.
whyWrong.D: There is enough information. Both complete distributions are given, so both standard deviations are fully determined; you only need to compare their spreads.

questions.note: Parsed upstream as free response, but the book prints four lettered choices; recorded here as multiple choice.

questions.stem: Point F lies on a unit circle in the xy-plane and has coordinates (1, 0). Point G is the center of the circle and has coordinates (0, 0). Point H also lies on the circle and has coordinates \( (-1, y) \) , where y is a constant. Which of the following could be the positive measure of angle FGH, in radians?
questions.whyCorrect: H is on the unit circle, so \( (-1)^{2} + y^{2} = 1 \) forces y = 0 and H = (-1, 0). F and H are then opposite ends of a diameter, so the angle at G is a straight angle, \( \pi \) radians — or \( \pi \) plus any whole number of full turns, that is any odd multiple of \( \pi \) . Of the choices, only \( 25\pi \) is an odd multiple of \( \pi \) .

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{27\pi}{2} \) is \( 13.5\pi \) , which reduces to \( \frac{3\pi}{2} \) — a quarter turn short of the straight angle.
whyWrong.B: \( \frac{29\pi}{2} \) reduces to \( \frac{\pi}{2} \) , a right angle, not a straight one.
whyWrong.C: \( 24\pi \) is an even multiple of \( \pi \) , which is a whole number of full turns and reduces to 0, placing H back at F.

questions.stem: In 2005, Aster earned 12% more than in 2004, and in 2006 Aster earned 6% more than in 2005. If Aster earned y times as much in 2004 as in 2006, which of the following is closest to the value of y?
questions.whyCorrect: Chain the two increases forward first: 2006 earnings are \(1.12 \times 1.06 = 1.1872\) times 2004 earnings. The question asks the other way round — 2004 as a multiple of 2006 — so take the reciprocal: \(y = \frac{1}{1.1872} \approx 0.8423\).

whyWrong.A: 0.5 would mean earnings doubled between 2004 and 2006. Growth of 12% then 6% is nowhere near a doubling.
whyWrong.B: 0.72 corresponds to 2006 earnings about 1.39 times those of 2004, far more growth than 12% followed by 6% produces.
whyWrong.D: 1.1872 is the ratio in the wrong direction — 2006 as a multiple of 2004. Since Aster earned less in 2004, y must be below 1.

questions.stem: A rectangular region of land is divided into 88 square lots of equal area R, in square units. The length of the region is 5.5 times the width of the region. If the width of the region is \( x\sqrt{R} \) units, what is the value of x?
questions.whyCorrect: Each lot is a square of area R, so each has side \( \sqrt{R} \) . Count lots instead of lengths: let the width be m lots and the length n lots, so mn = 88. The length being 5.5 times the width means n = 5.5m, so \( 5.5m^{2} = 88 \) and \( m^{2} = 16 \) , giving m = 4. The width is therefore \( 4\sqrt{R} \) and x = 4.

questions.stem: A researcher selected 26 guinea pigs from one habitat and 18 wild cavies from another habitat at random in Venezuela. The researcher found that in early adolescence, the number of virtual squares the wild cavies crossed was significantly more than the number of virtual squares the guinea pigs crossed. The researcher also found that the number of virtual squares crossed by both the wild cavies and the guinea pigs decreased from early adolescence to late adolescence. Based on the researcher's findings, which of the following statements is an appropriate conclusion that can be drawn from this study?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The statistically significant difference in behavior between the two age groups was caused by the differences in habitat.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The statistically significant difference in behavior between the two age groups was caused by aging.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The statistically significant difference in behavior during early adolescence between the two groups of animals can be generalized to all guinea pigs and wild cavies.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The statistically significant difference in behavior during early adolescence between the two groups of animals can only be generalized to the habitats in the study.

questions.whyCorrect: The animals were selected at random from two particular habitats, not randomly assigned to conditions. Random selection lets you generalize to the populations sampled — the animals in those two habitats — and nothing wider; the lack of random assignment means no cause can be claimed at all.

whyWrong.A: This claims a cause. Species and habitat vary together here, so the study cannot separate them, and an observational study cannot establish causation in any case.
whyWrong.B: Also a causal claim, and the same objection applies: nothing was manipulated, so aging is only one of several possible explanations.
whyWrong.C: Too wide. The sample came from two specific habitats in Venezuela, so it supports conclusions about those populations, not about every guinea pig and wild cavy.

The table shows the exponential relationship between the number of years, \(x\), since Hana started training in pole vault, and the estimated height \(h(x)\), in meters, of her best pole vault for that year. Which of the following functions best represents this relationship, where \(x \le 4\)?
questions.whyCorrect: At \(x = 0\) the table gives 1.25, so the coefficient is 1.25. The rows advance by 2 years and \(\frac{1.80}{1.25} = 1.44\), so the one-year factor is \(\sqrt{1.44} = 1.20\). The model is \(h(x) = 1.25(1.20)^{x}\); it gives \(1.25(1.20)^{4} = 2.59\), matching the last row.

whyWrong.A: The constants are swapped, so this starts at 1.20, and a base of 0.25 would cut the height to a quarter each year.
whyWrong.B: Also swapped: \(h(0) = 1.20\), but the table says 1.25. The base 1.25 is the two-year-ish factor misread as the yearly one.
whyWrong.C: The coefficient is right but the base 0.20 makes the function decrease sharply, contradicting the rising table values.

questions.stem: On average, a certain tree grows 87 centimeters every \( m \) months. At this rate, which expression represents the number of centimeters, on average, the tree grows every \( k \) years?
questions.whyCorrect: The monthly rate is \( \frac{87}{m} \) centimeters per month, and \( k \) years is \( 12k \) months. Multiplying gives \( \frac{87}{m} \cdot 12k = \frac{1{,}044k}{m} \). The conversion multiplies by 12 because a year contains more months, not fewer.

whyWrong.A: \( \frac{29m}{4k} \) is \( \frac{87m}{12k} \): it divides by 12 instead of multiplying, and it puts \( m \) and \( k \) on the wrong sides of the fraction.
whyWrong.B: \( \frac{29k}{4m} \) is \( \frac{87k}{12m} \), so it converts in the wrong direction — dividing by 12 rather than multiplying.
whyWrong.C: \( \frac{1{,}044m}{k} \) uses the right factor of 12 but swaps \( m \) and \( k \), making growth increase when the tree grows more slowly.

questions.stem:
\[ h(t)=-16t^2+b \]
The function \(h\) estimates an object’s height, in feet, above the ground \(t\) seconds after the object is dropped, where \(b\) is a constant. The function estimates that the object is 40.96 feet above the ground when it is dropped at t = 0. How many seconds after being dropped does the function estimate the object will hit the ground?
questions.whyCorrect: At \(t=0\) the function gives \(h(0)=b\), so \(b=40.96\). Hitting the ground means \(h(t)=0\): \(-16t^2+40.96=0\), so \(t^2=2.56\) and \(t=1.6\) (the negative root is before the drop, so discard it).

Do not expand. Treat the repeated quantity \( 15 - 3x \) as a single unknown, say \( u \): the equation is \( -9u + 5 = -10u + 21 \). Adding \( 10u \) to both sides gives \( u + 5 = 21 \), so \( u = 16 \) — and \( u \) is exactly what the question asks for, so you never need x.

questions.stem: If \( f(x) = x + 2 \) and \( g(x) = 2x \) , what is the value of \( 3f(-5) - g(-5) \) ?
questions.whyCorrect: Evaluate each function first, then combine. \( f(-5) = -5 + 2 = -3 \) and \( g(-5) = 2(-5) = -10 \) . So \( 3(-3) - (-10) = -9 + 10 = 1 \) . The trap is the double negative: subtracting -10 adds 10.

whyWrong.A: -19 is \( -9 - 10 \) , which treats \( g(-5) \) as +10. Substituting -5 into 2x gives -10, and subtracting a negative adds.
whyWrong.B: -3 is \( f(-5) \) by itself. It still has to be tripled, and \( g(-5) \) subtracted.
whyWrong.D: 7 is \( -3 + 10 \) , which forgets to multiply \( f(-5) \) by 3.

questions.stem: Two customers bought the same kind of cheese and milk at a store. The first customer paid 12.45 dollars for 1 pound of cheese and 2 gallons of milk. The second customer paid 19.70 dollars for 3 pounds of cheese and 1 gallon of milk. What is the cost, in dollars, of 1 gallon of milk?
questions.whyCorrect: Let c be the price of a pound of cheese and m the price of a gallon of milk, so c + 2m = 12.45 and 3c + m = 19.70. Multiply the first equation by 3 to get 3c + 6m = 37.35, then subtract the second: 5m = 17.65, so m = 3.53. The question asks for milk, so 3.53 is the answer.

whyWrong.B: This is 12.45 divided by 3, which would only be the milk price if the first customer had bought three identical items. They bought one pound of cheese and two gallons of milk, two different goods at two different prices.
whyWrong.C: This is close to 19.70 divided by 4, treating the second customer's four items as identically priced. Cheese and milk cost different amounts, so the total cannot be split evenly.
whyWrong.D: This is the correct solution for c, the price of a pound of cheese. The question asks for the price of a gallon of milk, which is 3.53.

questions.stem: One of the factors of \( 2x^{3} + 44x^{2} + 234x \) is \( x + b \) , where b is a positive constant. What is the smallest possible value of b ?
questions.whyCorrect: Pull out the common factor first: \( 2x^{3}+44x^{2}+234x = 2x(x^{2}+22x+117) \) . Now factor the quadratic — you need two numbers multiplying to 117 and adding to 22, which are 9 and 13. So the factors of the form \( x+b \) are \( x+9 \) and \( x+13 \) , and the smaller b is 9.

questions.stem:
\[ -x^2+bx-64=0 \]
In the given equation, \(b\) is an integer. The equation has no real solutions. What is the least possible value of \(b\) ?
questions.whyCorrect: No real solution means \(b^2-4ac<0\). With \(a=-1\) and \(c=-64\), \(4ac=256\), so the condition is \(b^2-256<0\), i.e. \(-16<b<16\). The least integer strictly greater than \(-16\) is \(-15\); \(b=-16\) itself would give exactly one real solution.

questions.stem: If \(\frac{72}{x} = 6x\), what is the value of \(6x^{2}\)?
questions.whyCorrect: Multiply both sides by \(x\): \(72 = 6x^{2}\). The expression asked for is already on the right, so the answer is 72 — solving for \(x\) is unnecessary.

whyWrong.A: 432 is \(72 \times 6\); the factor of 6 is already included once you clear the denominator.
whyWrong.C: 12 is \(x^{2}\) (since \(x^{2}=12\)), missing the coefficient 6.
whyWrong.D: 6 is only the coefficient in the expression, not its value.

questions.whyCorrect: For an exponential function with \(x\) increasing by 1 each row, consecutive outputs must have a constant ratio. Here \(\frac{15}{5} = 3\) and \(\frac{45}{15} = 3\), so \(f(x) = 5(3)^{x}\), which increases. Constant differences signal a linear function instead.

whyWrong.A: The outputs fall by a constant 10, so this is linear, and it is decreasing rather than increasing.
whyWrong.B: The outputs rise by a constant 10 — increasing, but linear. The ratios \(\frac{15}{5}=3\) and \(\frac{25}{15}\approx 1.67\) are not equal.
whyWrong.D: The ratios are constant at \(\frac{1}{3}\), so this is exponential, but it decreases.

questions.stem: \[ w(t) = 600 - 8t \]The function \(w\) models the volume of water, in milliliters, in a container t seconds after it begins draining from a hole at the bottom. According to the model, what is the predicted volume, in milliliters, draining from the container each second?
questions.whyCorrect: Each extra second subtracts 8 from the volume left, so 8 millilitres drain per second. The rate is the coefficient of t, not a volume read off the function.

whyWrong.B: 75 is 600 ÷ 8, the number of seconds the container takes to empty — a time, not a volume per second.
whyWrong.C: 592 is w(1), the volume still in the container after one second. The amount that drained is 600 - 592 = 8.
whyWrong.D: 600 is the starting volume, the value at t = 0.

questions.stem: For a certain classification, the positive mass m, in grams, of an object must be less than 510 grams. Which inequality represents this situation?
questions.whyCorrect: Two conditions are stated, not one. "Positive" gives m > 0 and "less than 510" gives m < 510, so both bounds belong in the answer.

whyWrong.A: This is the opposite of "less than 510".
whyWrong.B: A mass cannot be negative, and the stem explicitly says the mass is positive.
whyWrong.C: This range is entirely negative, which no mass can be.

questions.stem: \[ y = x^{2} - 18x + 51 \] The given equation relates the variables x and y. For what value of x does the value of y reach its minimum?
questions.whyCorrect: The leading coefficient is positive, so the parabola opens upward and its minimum is at the vertex, \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} = \frac{18}{2} = 9 \) . Completing the square gives \( (x - 9)^{2} - 30 \) , which shows the same thing.

whyWrong.A: -18 is the coefficient b copied straight out. The formula also flips its sign and halves it.
whyWrong.C: 18 flips the sign but forgets to divide by \( 2a = 2 \) .
whyWrong.D: 51 is the constant term, which is the value of y at x = 0, not where the minimum occurs.

questions.stem: Ari examined a set of 86 plants. The lightest plant has a mass of 2.8 kilograms (kg) and the heaviest plant has a mass of 6.2 kg. Chihiro examined the same set of 86 plants and also an additional plant with a mass of 11.7 kg. Which of the following must be true about the set of plants that Ari examined and the set of plants that Chihiro examined?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The standard deviation of the masses, in kg, of the plants that Ari examined is greater than the standard deviation of the masses, in kg, of the plants that Chihiro examined.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The range of the masses, in kg, of the plants that Ari examined is greater than the range of the masses, in kg, of the plants that Chihiro examined.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The median of the masses, in kg, of the plants that Ari examined is less than the median of the masses, in kg, of the plants that Chihiro examined.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The mean of the masses, in kg, of the plants that Ari examined is less than the mean of the masses, in kg, of the plants that Chihiro examined.

questions.whyCorrect: Every one of Ari's 86 masses is at most 6.2 kg, so Ari's mean is at most 6.2. Chihiro's set is Ari's set plus a single 11.7 kg plant, and adding a value that sits above the current mean always pulls the mean up. That argument works no matter what the 86 individual masses are, which is what "must be true" demands.

whyWrong.A: Backwards. The extra 11.7 kg plant sits far outside the 2.8–6.2 kg spread of the rest, so it increases the spread; Chihiro's standard deviation is the larger one.
whyWrong.B: Also backwards. Ari's range is 6.2 − 2.8 = 3.4 kg; Chihiro's is 11.7 − 2.8 = 8.9 kg.
whyWrong.C: The median can only move up or stay put, and "must be true" rules this out because it can stay put. Ari's median is the average of the 43rd and 44th masses; Chihiro's is the 44th. If those two masses are equal — entirely possible — the two medians are the same, so "less than" is not guaranteed.

questions.stem: The figure shown is a right rectangular pyramid, where \(l = 18\) units, \(w = 9\) units, and \(h = 12\) units. What is the surface area, in square units, of the pyramid?
questions.whyCorrect: A rectangular pyramid has two different pairs of triangular faces, each pair needing its own slant height, plus the rectangular base. Base: 18 × 9 = 162. The faces standing on the 9-unit edges have slant height \(\sqrt{12^2 + 9^2} = 15\) (using half of 18), contributing \(2 \cdot \frac{1}{2}(9)(15) = 135\). The faces on the 18-unit edges have slant height \(\sqrt{12^2 + 4.5^2} = \sqrt{164.25} \approx 12.82\), contributing \(2 \cdot \frac{1}{2}(18)(12.82) \approx 230.69\). The total is about 527.69. Using h itself as the slant height is the usual mistake — it gives 162 + 108 + 216 = 486.
questions.note: Answer is not a clean number: exactly \(297 + 9\sqrt{657} \approx 527.688\), which is unusual for a grid-in and worth a human check. Stem refers to a figure. Drawn as printed.
